flows.title: Accessibility QA
flows.description: Make your app usable by everyone: keyboard, contrast, labels, focus, and screen-reader basics.

steps.title: Keyboard-only audit
steps.purpose: Unplug the mouse: can you use the whole app?
checklist: Every page was tabbed through
The core journey was attempted by keyboard
Focus visibility was checked per element

steps.title: Fix keyboard operability
steps.purpose: Everything clickable must be tabbable, activatable, and visibly focused.
checklist: All controls reachable and activatable
Focus indicators visible everywhere
The core journey passes keyboard-only

steps.title: Contrast and visual pass
steps.purpose: Text people cannot read is text that does not exist.
checklist: Failing pairs were measured with ratios
Fixes applied at token level
Error/success/muted text re-verified

steps.title: Names, semantics, and structure
steps.purpose: Assistive tech needs names and structure to navigate.
checklist: No unnamed interactive elements in the accessibility tree
Heading hierarchy is sane per page
Toasts/errors are announced

steps.title: Focus management and forms
steps.purpose: The dynamic layer: modals, updates, and error handling must guide focus.
checklist: Modal focus traps and restores
Every input has a real label
Failed submit focuses the first error

flows.title: Add Activity Feed Feature
flows.description: Implement a persistent activity timeline with backend storage, API, and UI integration

steps.title: Define Activity data model
steps.purpose: Create a durable schema for storing activity events
checklist: Does prisma/schema.prisma contain a model named Activity with all five fields?
Is there a migration file named something like `2023xxxxxx_add-activity-model.sql`?
Can you query the database (e.g., via psql) and see an Activity table with the correct columns?

steps.title: Create server‑side API endpoints
steps.purpose: Expose activities via a RESTful interface for the frontend
checklist: Does GET /api/activities return a JSON list ordered newest‑first and respect page/limit?
Does POST /api/activities create a record in the database and return it with status 201?
Are both routes protected by `requireAuth` and scoped to `req.userId`?

steps.title: Emit activity events from key actions
steps.purpose: Automatically generate activity records when users perform important actions
checklist: After creating a post, does a new Activity with type "post_created" exist?
After liking a post, does a new Activity with type "post_liked" exist?
If activity creation throws, does the original post/like still succeed?

steps.title: Build the ActivityFeed React component
steps.purpose: Display a paginated list of activities on the client side
checklist: When the Dashboard loads, does the ActivityFeed show at least one real activity (if present)?
Does clicking "Load more" fetch the next page and append items?
Are timestamps formatted and messages human‑readable?

steps.title: Integrate ActivityFeed into the Dashboard
steps.purpose: Make the feed part of the existing user interface
checklist: When navigating to /dashboard, is the "Recent Activity" section visible?
Does the section list real activity items (not placeholders)?
Does the page still load without TypeScript or runtime errors?

steps.title: Test end‑to‑end functionality
steps.purpose: Confirm the whole pipeline works from action to UI
checklist: Does the integration test create a post and then find a matching activity in the DB?
Does the ActivityFeed unit test render the mocked activity message correctly?
Does `npm test` finish with zero failing tests?

flows.title: Add Database Persistence
flows.description: Your app forgets everything on refresh: move state into a real database with working CRUD.

steps.title: Inventory unpersisted state
steps.purpose: Find everything the app forgets - the full list, not samples.
checklist: Each row was refresh-tested
Every user-created data type appears
PERSIST rows cover all important data

steps.title: Design models and endpoints
steps.purpose: Give each PERSIST item a schema and API before wiring.
checklist: Every PERSIST item has a model
User-scoped data includes an owner field
Endpoints cover each needed operation

steps.title: Wire writes to the backend
steps.purpose: Every create/edit/delete must hit the database, not just state.
checklist: Each create survives refresh
Each edit survives refresh
Each delete stays deleted
Failures show errors without fake success

steps.title: Wire reads with proper states
steps.purpose: The UI must load truth from the backend with honest states.
checklist: Hardcoded arrays are gone
Loading and empty states render
Fetch failure shows retry

steps.title: Persistence QA pass
steps.purpose: Prove the app remembers everything, everywhere.
checklist: Full CRUD-with-refresh cycle per entity
Second-session consistency verified
Offline behavior shows errors, not silent loss
All failures fixed

flows.title: Add File-Based Persistent Memory
flows.description: Give your agent durable memory with plain files - the radical-minimalism approach production practitioners keep converging on.

steps.title: Design the memory file structure
steps.purpose: Structure is what keeps file memory useful at write 50.
checklist: Five sections with clear purposes
Caps and entry format defined
Rules embedded in the file itself

steps.title: Load memory at session start
steps.purpose: Reading is the easy half - do it first and prove it matters.
checklist: File loaded under a clear header
Over-budget handling prioritizes preferences and issues
Hand-written entries respected in the test

steps.title: Build the guarded memory_update tool
steps.purpose: One write path, validated, logged, duplicate-checked.
checklist: All three actions validated
Near-duplicate adds rejected helpfully
Audit log captures every write

steps.title: Add consolidation and run the 20-write test
steps.purpose: Memory hygiene is scheduled work, not a hope.
checklist: Cap-triggered consolidation works
Superseded entries show latest form only
Early facts still answered correctly at the end

flows.title: Add a Working Team Invite System to a SaaS App
flows.description: Build a real invite flow for a SaaS app so existing users can invite teammates by email, store invite records, validate tokens, accept invitations, and join the correct workspace with proper permissions.

steps.title: Audit the current auth and workspace model
steps.purpose: Make the AI inspect the existing app structure before changing anything so the invite system fits the current data model and authorization rules.
checklist: The builder identifies the existing user model
The builder identifies the workspace or organization model
The builder identifies how roles and permissions are enforced today
The plan names the pages or screens where invite UI belongs
The plan includes both backend and frontend changes

steps.title: Add the invite data model and migration
steps.purpose: Create persistent invite storage with fields needed for secure invite handling.
checklist: An invite table or model exists in the real database schema
Workspace, inviter, and role fields are included
Status and expiration fields exist
Token storage is secure or intentionally handled
The migration runs without schema errors

steps.title: Build secure invite creation on the server
steps.purpose: Implement backend logic that creates invites only for authorized users and generates usable tokens.
checklist: Unauthorized users cannot create invites
Email input is validated and normalized
Secure tokens are generated server-side
Invite records are saved in the database
Duplicate pending invites are blocked or intentionally replaced

steps.title: Add the invite UI in workspace settings or members
steps.purpose: Give admins a real interface to send invites and see immediate results.
checklist: The invite form appears in the correct workspace context
Only authorized roles can see or use it
Submitting the form triggers the real backend flow
Loading and error states are visible
A real invite link or send confirmation is shown on success

steps.title: Implement invite listing, resend, and revoke
steps.purpose: Let workspace admins manage pending invites after sending them.
checklist: Pending invites are queried from the database
Revoke updates the invite status persistently
Revoked invites are no longer valid
Resend produces a real link or send result
The list refreshes correctly after actions

steps.title: Build the invite acceptance page and token validation
steps.purpose: Create the recipient flow that validates the invite and guides the user to sign in or sign up.
checklist: The token is validated server-side against stored invite data
Invalid and expired invites show distinct messages
The page shows real workspace and role details
Unauthenticated users are routed into auth without losing invite context
Already accepted invites are handled safely

steps.title: Implement the final accept action and membership creation
steps.purpose: Make acceptance actually grant access by creating or updating the workspace membership.
checklist: Accepting an invite creates a real workspace membership
The invite status becomes accepted in the database
The same invite cannot be accepted twice
The user lands in the correct workspace after acceptance
Partial failure does not leave mismatched membership and invite state

steps.title: Handle edge cases and validation rules
steps.purpose: Close the gaps AI builders often skip, including duplicate membership, mismatched emails, and expiration behavior.
checklist: Duplicate membership attempts are blocked cleanly
Expired and revoked invites fail server-side
Duplicate active invite behavior is intentional and enforced
Email mismatch policy is implemented server-side if applicable
User-facing errors are specific instead of generic

steps.title: Test the end-to-end invite flow
steps.purpose: Verify the feature works from send to acceptance for both existing and new users.
checklist: A real invite record is created when sending
An existing user can accept and join the workspace
A new user can sign up and then join the workspace
Revoked and expired invites fail correctly
Database membership reflects accepted invites

flows.title: Add Loading/Error States
flows.description: Eliminate silent failures and frozen screens: add loading, empty, and error states across the whole app.

steps.title: Inventory async surfaces
steps.purpose: List every place the app waits or can fail.
checklist: Every fetch and mutation is listed
Gaps verified by actual throttling/failure tests
Empty-capable lists identified

steps.title: Add loading states
steps.purpose: Replace blank waits with skeletons and spinners.
checklist: Skeletons appear under slow network
Pending buttons disable and indicate work
Content swap causes no jarring shift

steps.title: Add error states with retry
steps.purpose: Failures must be visible and recoverable.
checklist: Forced fetch failure shows error + retry
Mutation failure preserves user input
No empty catch blocks remain

steps.title: Add empty states
steps.purpose: Empty is a state, not a bug - design it.
checklist: New-account emptiness is handled
No-results emptiness has distinct copy
Empty states include a useful action

steps.title: States QA sweep
steps.purpose: Verify the app under slow, broken, and empty conditions.
checklist: Throttled pass completed
Forced-failure pass completed
Fresh-account empty pass completed
All failures fixed

flows.title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent
flows.description: Give your agent the planning discipline of the leading harnesses: an explicit, model-visible todo list that survives long tasks.

steps.title: Design the todo data model and tool
steps.purpose: Structured plans beat prose plans because the harness can enforce them.
checklist: Full-list-replace semantics chosen and documented
One in_progress enforced by validation
State lives in the harness, not chat history

steps.title: Render the plan into context every turn
steps.purpose: A plan the model cannot see is a plan it will not follow.
checklist: Reminder block regenerated from state each turn
Block stays compact (under 15 lines)
Logged context confirms freshness

steps.title: Enforce plan-first and completion gates
steps.purpose: The two gates that turn a todo list into reliability.
checklist: Plan-first gate blocks premature tool use
Completion gate blocks finishing with open items
Items can be cancelled with a recorded reason

steps.title: Test the full planning lifecycle
steps.purpose: Prove the plan survives execution, failure, and resumption.
checklist: Happy path executes items in order
Failed step is never marked completed
Resume continues from the correct item

flows.title: Add Real-Time Presence Indicators to a Chat App with WebSockets
flows.description: A step-by-step flow for implementing real-time online, offline, and typing presence in a chat app using WebSockets, including backend presence tracking, frontend updates, reconnect handling, and verification.

steps.title: Inspect the existing chat architecture and choose presence data flow
steps.purpose: Establish where WebSocket connections, user identity, and chat participants already exist so presence can be added without breaking the app.
checklist: Identified the backend entry point for socket connections
Confirmed how authenticated user identity is attached to requests or sockets
Found the frontend chat screen or conversation header where presence will display
Documented whether conversation participants are already known on client and server
Listed exact files or modules to modify

steps.title: Define the presence event contract and server-side state model
steps.purpose: Create a reliable event schema and in-memory or persistent tracking model before implementation.
checklist: Event names are defined consistently for server and client
Payloads include user ID and conversation ID where relevant
Multiple active sockets per user are accounted for
Offline transition is tied to final disconnect only
Typing events are scoped to a conversation

steps.title: Implement authenticated WebSocket connection handling on the server
steps.purpose: Ensure the backend can identify users on socket connect and maintain a real presence registry.
checklist: Each socket resolves to a real authenticated user ID
Active sockets are tracked per user
Disconnect removes only the current socket connection
User stays online if another socket remains active
Last seen is updated when the final socket disconnects

steps.title: Broadcast presence changes to relevant chat participants
steps.purpose: Send online and offline updates only to users who should see them.
checklist: Online event is emitted only when the first socket connects
Offline event is emitted only when the final socket disconnects
Recipients are derived from real conversation or participant data
Other connected clients receive the event without refresh
Current user does not need to manually poll for updates

steps.title: Add initial presence sync and frontend presence state management
steps.purpose: Ensure the UI has the correct presence map when the chat screen first loads and stays updated from socket events.
checklist: Presence state is keyed by user ID
Initial presence data is loaded on screen open or socket connect
Online and offline events update the store immediately
Last seen is stored for offline users if supported
Socket listeners are cleaned up to avoid duplicate handlers

steps.title: Render presence indicators in the chat UI
steps.purpose: Display presence in conversation headers, user lists, or message panes using the live presence state.
checklist: Presence indicator appears in the real chat UI
Indicator updates when another client connects or disconnects
Offline state or last seen renders correctly
UI works for the app's conversation types
Existing chat layout and message rendering still function

steps.title: Implement conversation-scoped typing indicators
steps.purpose: Add real-time typing state that appears only in the relevant conversation and clears correctly.
checklist: Typing events include conversation context
Typing indicator is shown only to other participants
Typing state clears after idle timeout
Typing state clears when a message is sent
Typing does not appear in unrelated conversations

steps.title: Handle reconnects, stale sockets, and edge cases
steps.purpose: Make presence resilient during refreshes, temporary network drops, and multi-tab usage.
checklist: Closing one of multiple tabs does not mark user offline
Reconnect restores presence updates without manual refresh
Initial sync runs again after reconnect
Typing state does not remain stuck after disconnect
Temporary network loss does not permanently desync presence

steps.title: Test with two or more real clients and instrument debug output
steps.purpose: Verify that presence is actually driven by backend socket events across separate clients.
checklist: Tested with at least two distinct authenticated users
Verified live online transition with no refresh
Verified offline or last seen on final disconnect only
Verified typing appears and clears correctly
Verified multi-tab and reconnect scenarios with logs

steps.title: Fix discovered issues and clean up implementation details
steps.purpose: Resolve mismatches, remove temporary hacks, and leave a maintainable presence system.
checklist: No duplicate socket listeners remain
Presence transitions match real connection state
Typing state clears in all tested paths
Initial sync and reconnect behavior are stable
Temporary debug noise is removed or minimized

flows.title: Add Team Invites to a SaaS App
flows.description: Build a real team invitation system for a SaaS app, including invite creation, email/share flow, acceptance, membership creation, role assignment, validation, and end-to-end testing.

steps.title: Audit Existing Team, User, and Auth Models
steps.purpose: Map the current app structure so the invite system integrates with real existing models and permission rules.
checklist: Existing user model is identified
Existing team and membership models are identified
Current role or permission logic is documented
Files/routes/components to modify are named explicitly

steps.title: Add Invitation Data Model and Migration
steps.purpose: Create persistent backend storage for invites so links and statuses are real.
checklist: Invitation table/model exists in schema
Status and expiration fields are present
Team, inviter, and accepter references are defined
Indexes or constraints for lookup and duplicates are added

steps.title: Implement Secure Invite Creation API
steps.purpose: Create the server-side action or endpoint that authorized users use to generate invites.
checklist: Unauthenticated users cannot create invites
Non-admin/non-owner team members cannot create invites
Invalid email or role is rejected
Duplicate pending invites are blocked or handled explicitly
Existing team members cannot be invited again

steps.title: Build the Team Invite Management UI
steps.purpose: Add a usable interface for admins to create, review, and revoke invites.
checklist: Invite form is visible to authorized users only
Submitting the form creates a real invite
Pending invites render from backend data
Revoke action is available for pending invites
Loading, success, and error states are visible

steps.title: Implement Invite Link Lookup and Acceptance Screen
steps.purpose: Create the public or semi-public acceptance flow that resolves an invite token and guides the recipient.
checklist: Tokenized invite route exists
Server-side lookup validates the token against stored invite data
Signed-out users are prompted to authenticate
Invalid, expired, revoked, and accepted states are distinct
Valid invite details show correct team and role

steps.title: Implement Final Invite Acceptance and Membership Creation
steps.purpose: Convert a valid invite into a real team membership and mark the invite as accepted.
checklist: Accept action requires authentication
Membership row is created in the database
Invite status changes from pending to accepted
Duplicate membership is prevented
Partial-write failure is avoided or handled

steps.title: Add Revoke, Expiration, and Edge-Case Handling
steps.purpose: Make the invite system robust against stale or invalid invite states.
checklist: Authorized users can revoke pending invites
Revoked invites cannot be accepted
Expired invites are blocked in lookup and acceptance
Already accepted invites cannot be reused
Existing members are handled cleanly

steps.title: Wire Email or Share-Link Delivery
steps.purpose: Make the invitation usable by actually delivering or exposing the link.
checklist: Email is only used if real email infrastructure exists
Copy-link flow works if email is unavailable
Delivery success is tied to real underlying result
Invite URL includes the correct token

steps.title: Add Validation, Permissions, and UX Guardrails
steps.purpose: Polish the system so invalid actions fail clearly and authorized flows feel reliable.
checklist: Backend and UI permission rules match
Role assignment is restricted appropriately
Error states are user-readable
Loading and disabled states prevent duplicate actions

steps.title: Run End-to-End Testing and Fix Failures
steps.purpose: Verify the invite system works in real scenarios instead of appearing complete.
checklist: Happy-path invite creation and acceptance work
Unauthorized creation is blocked
Revoked and expired invites fail correctly
Duplicate membership and duplicate invites are prevented
Critical backend paths are covered by tests if supported

flows.title: Admin Dashboard
flows.description: Build a real admin dashboard with live data tables, stats, filters, and actions that actually mutate data.

steps.title: Define admin scope and data
steps.purpose: Decide exactly what the admin manages so the dashboard is concrete, not decorative.
checklist: Entities to manage are listed
Each stat has a defined query
Each row action states its database effect
Admin access rule is defined

steps.title: Build admin layout and access control
steps.purpose: Stand up the admin shell and lock it down before adding data.
checklist: Non-admin users cannot open /admin
Admin API endpoints reject non-admins with 403
A test admin account exists and works

steps.title: Implement real stats cards
steps.purpose: Stats must come from live queries so the dashboard tells the truth.
checklist: Each stat matches a hand-checked database count
Adding a record changes the relevant stat
Loading and error states render properly

steps.title: Build the data table with search and filters
steps.purpose: The core admin surface: browse real records with search, filters, and pagination.
checklist: Search narrows results correctly
Filters combine with search
Pagination fetches new pages from the server
Empty and error states display

steps.title: Add working row actions
steps.purpose: Admin actions must mutate the database and survive refresh.
checklist: Edits persist after a full refresh
Delete/disable asks for confirmation
Failures show a visible error, and the row is not silently wrong

steps.title: QA the dashboard end to end
steps.purpose: Verify truthfulness: stats, tables, and actions must reflect the database exactly.
checklist: All stats verified against direct queries
Actions persist across refresh
Non-admin block verified at UI and API level
All failures fixed and re-tested

flows.title: Stand Up an Adversarial Verification Agent
flows.description: Stop trusting your agent's own 'it works': dispatch a read-only verifier that must run real commands, probe adversarially, and return an evidence-backed PASS/FAIL verdict.

steps.title: Define the verifier with hard read-only constraints
steps.purpose: Constraints in the tool pool, not just the prompt.
checklist: Edit/write tools absent from the pool (asserted in a test)
Constraint re-injected every turn
Fix-attempt test refused correctly

steps.title: Feed it the real task and require evidence
steps.purpose: Verification quality is bounded by input honesty and output proof.
checklist: Original task text passed through unmodified
Every check shows command + observed output
Each requirement mapped to a concrete check

steps.title: Add adversarial probes
steps.purpose: The happy path passing is where real verification begins.
checklist: At least one probe per verification from the required classes
Anti-80% and anti-avoidance rules in the prompt
Probe results recorded pass or fail

steps.title: Gate completion on the verdict
steps.purpose: A verdict nobody acts on is decoration.
checklist: 'Done' automatically triggers verification
FAIL/PARTIAL findings become the implementer's next tasks
Cycle counts logged with an escalation threshold

flows.title: Implement the Six Core Orchestration Patterns
flows.description: Worker pool, pipeline, supervisor-worker, adversarial, fork-join, resume chain - build the reusable orchestration patterns every serious multi-agent system converges on.

steps.title: Build the shared lifecycle infrastructure
steps.purpose: Six patterns, one chassis: registration, state, delivery, cleanup.
checklist: Child abort scopes independent of the parent's
Reports arrive in the parent's next turn, verified
Cleanup runs on normal, error, and cancel paths (tested)

steps.title: Implement fan-out patterns: worker pool and fork-join
steps.purpose: Parallelism is the payoff; delivery discipline is the price.
checklist: Single-turn parallel dispatch with disjoint work slices
Join proceeds sensibly on partial failure
Per-child timeout and concurrency cap enforced

steps.title: Implement sequential and hierarchical patterns
steps.purpose: Pipeline hand-offs and supervisor delegation live on explicit messages.
checklist: Stage outputs validated before feeding the next stage
Supervisor prompt names the delivery tool as the only channel
Resume rehydrates from transcript and completes

steps.title: Implement the adversarial pattern and harden the whole
steps.purpose: Verification pressure plus leak-free operation makes it production-grade.
checklist: Adversarial verdict gates completion end-to-end
Kill-tests show zero orphaned resources per pattern
Selection guide lives in the orchestrator prompt

flows.title: Agent-to-Agent Protocols (A2A)
flows.description: Connect two agents over an explicit protocol - task handoff, acknowledgment, and failure handling - instead of hoping chat works out.

steps.title: Define the protocol
steps.purpose: Write the message schemas and state machine before any agent code.
checklist: Envelope and all message types specified
State machine covers rejection and failure
Two failure sequences diagrammed

steps.title: Build the message layer
steps.purpose: Reliable-enough transport with full observability.
checklist: Schema validation on send and receive
All messages in the protocol log
Timeouts generated for silent recipients

steps.title: Wrap agents as protocol endpoints
steps.purpose: Each agent's loop stays private; the protocol is its public face.
checklist: Ack and status sent at the right moments
Critiques are structured, not prose blobs
Invalid payloads rejected with reasons

steps.title: Run the revision loop with failure injection
steps.purpose: The demo that matters: cooperation surviving imperfection.
checklist: Revision round uses the structured critique
Timeout, rejection, and max-rounds all handled
Full run reconstructed from logs by correlation ID

flows.title: Build an AI Affiliate Marketing Agent That Finds, Publishes, and Tracks Revenue Opportunities
flows.description: Create a working AI agent system that discovers affiliate opportunities, generates compliant content, publishes or prepares campaign assets, and tracks clicks, conversions, and revenue in a usable dashboard.

steps.title: Define the affiliate agent scope and data model
steps.purpose: Set the exact product scope, entities, relationships, and success metrics before building screens or AI features.
checklist: There are persistent models/tables for offers, campaigns, content assets, tracked links, clicks, conversions, and earnings
Relationships are defined, such as campaign belongs to offer and content asset belongs to campaign
The app navigation includes the main sections needed for the full workflow
No analytics numbers are hardcoded in the foundation

steps.title: Build affiliate offer intake and management
steps.purpose: Create the real workflow for entering and managing affiliate offers that the AI agent will promote.
checklist: A new offer can be created and appears in the offer list after refresh
Editing an offer persists the updated values
Both destination URL and affiliate tracking URL are validated
Disclosure text is stored per offer
Offer records are searchable or filterable

steps.title: Create campaigns and operational statuses
steps.purpose: Turn offers into trackable marketing campaigns with lifecycle states and planning metadata.
checklist: A campaign cannot be created without selecting an offer
Status changes persist after refresh
Campaign list can be filtered by status
Campaign detail page shows linked offer information
Campaigns store channel and audience angle

steps.title: Add AI content generation tied to campaigns
steps.purpose: Make the agent produce usable affiliate content variants connected to specific campaigns and offers.
checklist: Generating content creates persistent content asset records
Each asset is linked to both a campaign and an offer
At least three channel-specific outputs are produced
Generated output uses the campaign angle and offer details
Previously generated assets remain accessible after refresh

steps.title: Enforce disclosures and compliance checks
steps.purpose: Prevent risky or non-compliant affiliate content from being generated or published without required disclosure.
checklist: Disclosure text is pulled from the offer record
Generated content shows or stores the disclosure where required
Risky phrases trigger warnings or flagged status
Compliance status persists on each content asset

steps.title: Implement tracked affiliate links and click logging
steps.purpose: Create the core monetization plumbing so outbound clicks are recorded before users are redirected.
checklist: Tracked links are generated from real offer or campaign records
Visiting a tracked link creates a stored click event
The visitor is redirected to the affiliate URL after the click is logged
Click records include campaign or offer linkage
The UI provides a copyable tracked URL

steps.title: Add conversion and earnings capture
steps.purpose: Create a reliable way to record monetization outcomes so ROI reporting is real.
checklist: A user can create a manual earnings or conversion record
The record is linked to an offer and optionally a campaign or tracked link
Saved earnings appear after refresh
Revenue is not stored only as a static campaign field
Optional CSV import works if implemented

steps.title: Build analytics dashboard with computed monetization metrics
steps.purpose: Turn tracked events and earnings records into decision-ready reporting.
checklist: Dashboard numbers change when new clicks or earnings are added
Conversion rate is computed from stored clicks and conversions
EPC is computed from earnings divided by clicks
Breakdowns by campaign and offer are available
No hardcoded sample metrics remain in the analytics UI

steps.title: Add workflow filters, readiness states, and operator usability
steps.purpose: Make the app usable day to day by organizing records and exposing what needs action.
checklist: Search works across offers or campaigns
Records can be filtered by status and other useful fields
Readiness indicators are based on actual data requirements
Flagged content or incomplete campaigns are easy to identify

steps.title: Run end-to-end tests with seeded realistic data
steps.purpose: Verify the full affiliate monetization workflow actually works from intake to revenue reporting.
checklist: One realistic offer exists with valid URLs and disclosure
A campaign is linked to that offer
Generated content assets are saved and visible
At least one tracked click event is recorded
At least one earnings or conversion record is saved
Dashboard metrics reflect the test data correctly

steps.title: Fix weak spots and harden the monetization loop
steps.purpose: Resolve the most common AI-build failures so the app is not just impressive-looking but operationally reliable.
checklist: No core monetization metric depends on hardcoded sample data
Status changes persist across reloads
Generated content remains linked to campaigns and offers
Tracked links reliably create click records
Revenue reporting is computed from saved records

flows.title: AI Chatbot Feature
flows.description: Add a real AI chat feature with streaming responses, conversation history, and graceful failure handling.

steps.title: Define the assistant spec
steps.purpose: Decide what the assistant does, its boundaries, and its system prompt.
checklist: System prompt text is written out
Key location is backend env only
Conversation/message model is defined

steps.title: Build the chat UI
steps.purpose: A trustworthy chat surface with all interaction states.
checklist: Send disables while pending
Typing indicator renders
Auto-scroll works on new messages

steps.title: Integrate the real LLM API
steps.purpose: Replace nothing with something: real model responses through the backend.
checklist: Responses are genuinely from the model
The key is absent from all frontend code
API failure shows a retry-able error, not a stuck spinner

steps.title: Persist conversation history
steps.purpose: Chats must survive refresh and be scoped to their owner.
checklist: Refresh restores the conversation
The assistant remembers earlier messages
New conversation starts clean
Users see only their own conversations

steps.title: Harden failure and limit handling
steps.purpose: AI features fail in production - make every failure visible and recoverable.
checklist: A simulated API failure shows the error UI
Retry resends the failed message
Overlong/empty messages are blocked inline

steps.title: Chat QA pass
steps.purpose: Verify realness, persistence, and resilience end to end.
checklist: Context memory demonstrated
Forced failure path verified
History persistence verified via refresh
All failures fixed

flows.title: API/Error Handling QA
flows.description: Verify every API contract and failure path: status codes, error shapes, timeouts, and frontend recovery.

steps.title: Inventory the API contracts
steps.purpose: Write down what every endpoint promises before testing it.
checklist: Every endpoint appears with expected codes
A single error shape is defined
Unknowns are flagged for testing

steps.title: Test success and failure codes
steps.purpose: Fire real requests: does each endpoint honor its contract?
checklist: Every endpoint was hit with all scenario classes
No 200s carrying errors remain
Bad input yields 400s, not 500s

steps.title: Normalize error responses
steps.purpose: One error shape everywhere - safe, consistent, frontend-friendly.
checklist: Every failure class returns the standard shape
No internals leak in responses
Field-level validation details included

steps.title: Verify frontend failure handling
steps.purpose: Each failure class needs a visible, correct UI response.
checklist: Each class was forced against the real UI

flows.title: Working Signup/Auth System
flows.description: Build a real signup, login, session, and protected route flow - not a form that only looks functional.

steps.title: Define auth requirements
steps.purpose: Clarify exactly what the authentication system must do before building it.
checklist: Signup requirements are defined
Login requirements are defined
Session persistence is included
Protected route behavior is included
Validation and errors are included

steps.title: Choose auth method
steps.purpose: Lock the auth mechanism so the AI does not mix approaches or silently pick something insecure.
checklist: Exactly one auth method was chosen
Token/session storage location is specified
Refresh persistence is addressed
The choice supports logout and protected routes

steps.title: Define the user database model
steps.purpose: A real signup needs a real user record. Define the schema before generating any UI.
checklist: Email field is unique and normalized
Passwords are hashed, never plaintext
Password hash is never returned by any API
Model exists in the actual codebase

steps.title: Generate the signup page
steps.purpose: Build the signup UI with all fields and states - the visible half of signup.
checklist: Email, password, confirm password fields exist
Submit button shows a loading state
Inline validation messages render under fields
Layout works at 375px width

steps.title: Implement real signup logic
steps.purpose: Make sure the form actually creates a user instead of only looking functional.
checklist: Can a new user sign up?
Does a duplicate email fail cleanly?
Is the user redirected to the dashboard after signup?
Is the session active immediately after signup?
Do errors show clearly in the UI?

steps.title: Generate the login page
steps.purpose: Build login with real credential verification against stored users.
checklist: Correct credentials log in and redirect
Wrong password shows a visible UI error
Unknown email shows the same generic error
Submit button has a loading state

steps.title: Add session persistence
steps.purpose: Keep users logged in across refreshes - the most commonly faked auth behavior.
checklist: Refresh on the dashboard keeps you logged in
Closing and reopening the tab keeps you logged in
Logout clears the session completely
No logged-out flash while the session restores

steps.title: Add protected dashboard routes
steps.purpose: Actually block logged-out users - not just hide links.
checklist: Opening /dashboard while logged out redirects to login
No flash of protected content before redirect
Private API endpoints return 401 without a session
After login you land on the originally requested page

steps.title: Add validation and error states
steps.purpose: Cover every input and failure path so auth feels trustworthy.
checklist: Empty submits show required-field errors
Bad email format is caught inline
Short passwords are rejected with the rule shown
Server failures show a visible error, not console-only

steps.title: Add password reset flow
steps.purpose: Complete the auth loop so locked-out users can recover.
checklist: Reset request shows a neutral confirmation
Reset link/token opens the set-new-password page
New password works on next login
Old password stops working
Token cannot be reused

steps.title: Test auth edge cases
steps.purpose: Attack the auth flow like a hostile tester before calling it done.
checklist: All edge cases were actually executed
Each result includes observed behavior
Back button after logout shows no private data
All FAILs were fixed and re-tested

steps.title: Generate fix prompt for broken auth
steps.purpose: Create a reusable repair prompt for when auth breaks later in the build.
checklist: The prompt covers signup, login, session, guards, and APIs
It demands PASS/FAIL evidence
It is self-contained and paste-ready

steps.title: Final QA checklist
steps.purpose: Verify the definition of done with evidence and close the flow.
checklist: Every DoD item has evidence, not claims
All NOT DONE items were fixed and re-verified
The full flow was tested on mobile width

tactics.title: Accessibility QA: Keyboard-only audit
tactics.body: Unplug the mouse: can you use the whole app? Checklist: Every page was tabbed through; The core journey was attempted by keyboard; Focus visibility was checked per element Audit the entire app using only the keyboard. Tab through every page: record every interactive element that cannot be reached, cannot be activated (Enter/Space), or has no visible focus indicator; note tab order absurdities; test Escape on dismissibles; attempt the core journey end to end by keyboard. Produce the issue table: element -> problem -> page. If stuck: The audit was code-scanning, not keyboard use. Put the mouse away and tab through every page, recording each unreachable or unactivatable control.
checklist: Every page was tabbed through
The core journey was attempted by keyboard
Focus visibility was checked per element

tactics.title: Accessibility QA: Fix keyboard operability
tactics.body: Everything clickable must be tabbable, activatable, and visibly focused. Checklist: All controls reachable and activatable; Focus indicators visible everywhere; The core journey passes keyboard-only Fix every keyboard issue. Requirements: replace click-divs with buttons/links (or add tabindex and key handlers where unavoidable); ensure Enter/Space activates controls; add a visible focus style consistent with the design (never remove outlines without replacement); fix tab order via DOM order; make dismissibles respond to Escape. Re-run the keyboard core journey to verify. If stuck: Click-divs remain unreachable. Convert them to semantic buttons and re-verify by tabbing to and activating each with the keyboard.
checklist: All controls reachable and activatable
Focus indicators visible everywhere
The core journey passes keyboard-only

tactics.title: Accessibility QA: Contrast and visual pass
tactics.body: Text people cannot read is text that does not exist. Checklist: Failing pairs were measured with ratios; Fixes applied at token level; Error/success/muted text re-verified Audit and fix contrast. Check every text style (body, muted, labels, placeholders, buttons, links) against its background for WCAG AA (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) - report the failing pairs with their ratios; check UI element contrast (borders, icons, focus rings) at 3:1; check state-dependent text (disabled, errors, success). Fix failures by adjusting the tokens, not one-off overrides, and re-report the ratios. If stuck: Muted text still fails AA. Darken/lighten the muted token to pass 4.5:1 against its backgrounds and re-measure every usage.
checklist: Failing pairs were measured with ratios
Fixes applied at token level
Error/success/muted text re-verified

tactics.title: Accessibility QA: Names, semantics, and structure
tactics.body: Assistive tech needs names and structure to navigate. Checklist: No unnamed interactive elements in the accessibility tree; Heading hierarchy is sane per page; Toasts/errors are announced Fix semantics and naming. Requirements: every icon-only button gets an accessible name (aria-label); images get meaningful alt (or empty alt if decorative); heading levels form a sane hierarchy per page (one h1, no skips); landmarks (nav/main) present; links say where they go (no naked 'click here'); dynamic status messages (toasts, errors) use live regions where they matter. Verify with the accessibility tree… If stuck: Icon buttons still read as 'button'. Add aria-labels describing the action ('Copy prompt', 'Delete item') and re-inspect the accessibility tree.
checklist: No unnamed interactive elements in the accessibility tree
Heading hierarchy is sane per page
Toasts/errors are announced

tactics.title: Accessibility QA: Focus management and forms
tactics.body: The dynamic layer: modals, updates, and error handling must guide focus. Checklist: Modal focus traps and restores; Every input has a real label; Failed submit focuses the first error Fix focus management and forms. Modals/drawers: focus moves in on open, stays trapped inside, returns to the trigger on close. Forms: every input has a programmatically associated label; errors are visible, specific, and associated with their fields (aria-describedby); on failed submit, focus moves to the first error; required fields communicated. Route changes: focus/announce the new page context. Verify each… If stuck: Focus escapes modals and errors are unassociated. Add the focus trap and return, link errors via aria-describedby, and move focus to the first invalid field on submit.
checklist: Modal focus traps and restores
Every input has a real label
Failed submit focuses the first error

tactics.title: Add Database Persistence: Inventory unpersisted state
tactics.body: Find everything the app forgets - the full list, not samples. Checklist: Each row was refresh-tested; Every user-created data type appears; PERSIST rows cover all important data Audit the app and produce a table of every piece of state that should persist but currently does not: the data (e.g. tasks, profile edits, settings), where it lives now (useState/localStorage/nowhere), what user action creates or changes it, and whether refresh loses it. Test by performing each action then refreshing. Mark each row KEEP-LOCAL (genuinely UI-only) or PERSIST. If stuck: The inventory is partial. Walk every screen, perform every create/edit action, refresh, and add every piece of lost data to the table.

Note which lists need pagination and which data is user-scoped versus global. Then create the models and endpoint skeletons in the codebase. If stuck: Models are missing owners or operations. Add ownerId to user-scoped models and fill in the missing update/delete endpoints.

tactics.title: Add Database Persistence: Wire writes to the backend
tactics.body: Every create/edit/delete must hit the database, not just state. Checklist: Each create survives refresh; Each edit survives refresh; Each delete stays deleted; Failures show errors without fake success Wire all mutating actions to the backend. Requirements: create/edit/delete handlers call their endpoints and await success before confirming in the UI; failures show visible errors and do not fake success; optimistic updates (if used) roll back on failure; after each mutation the data refetches or reconciles. Prove each with a mutation followed by a hard refresh. If stuck: Some actions still only touch state. List every mutation handler, wire each to its endpoint, and re-verify with refreshes.

Each delete stays deleted

User-scoped views must filter by the authenticated user. If stuck: Views still render demo data or flash empty. Fix all failures and re-run. If stuck: QA skipped entities or the second-session check. Complete the full cycle for every PERSIST row and fix any data that still evaporates.

tactics.title: Add File-Based Persistent Memory: Design the memory file structure
tactics.body: Structure is what keeps file memory useful at write 50. Checklist: Five sections with clear purposes; Caps and entry format defined; Rules embedded in the file itself Design the project memory format. Create MEMORY.md with sections: ## Project Facts (architecture, key paths, stack choices), ## Preferences (user style and tool preferences, one per line), ## Working Recipes (commands and approaches that work, with context), ## Known Issues & Failed Approaches (what breaks and why), ## Decisions Log (dated one-liners: decision + reason). Define per-section caps (e.g. 30 lines each)… If stuck: Sections blur together in practice. Sharpen the definitions with an example entry under each header and a one-line 'belongs here if...' rule.
checklist: Five sections with clear purposes
Caps and entry format defined
Rules embedded in the file itself

tactics.title: Add File-Based Persistent Memory: Load memory at session start
tactics.body: Reading is the easy half - do it first and prove it matters. Checklist: File loaded under a clear header; Over-budget handling prioritizes preferences and issues; Hand-written entries respected in the test Implement memory loading. At session start in a project: read MEMORY.md if present; include it in the system context under a clear 'PROJECT MEMORY - honor these facts and preferences' header; if the file exceeds the context budget allotted (default ~1000 tokens), include Preferences and Known Issues fully and summarize the rest. Handle the no-file case silently. Prove it works: hand-write a preference into the file… If stuck: The agent contradicts the memory file. Strengthen the header instruction ('these override defaults') and confirm the block is in the system context, not lost mid-history.
checklist: File loaded under a clear header
Over-budget handling prioritizes preferences and issues
Hand-written entries respected in the test

tactics.title: Add File-Based Persistent Memory: Build the guarded memory_update tool
tactics.body: One write path, validated, logged, duplicate-checked. Checklist: All three actions validated; Near-duplicate adds rejected helpfully; Audit log captures every write Implement the memory_update tool. Interface: memory_update(section, action, entry, replaces?) where action is add | revise | remove. Validation: section must exist; entry must fit the format rules (single line, length cap); on add, check for near-duplicates in the section (normalized comparison) and reject with the existing entry shown; on revise/remove, 'replaces' must match an existing entry. The tool rewrites… If stuck: Duplicates accumulate anyway. Tighten normalization (lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace) and have the reject message show the near-match so the model revises instead of re-adding.
checklist: All three actions validated
Near-duplicate adds rejected helpfully
Audit log captures every write

tactics.title: Add File-Based Persistent Memory: Add consolidation and run the 20-write test
tactics.step_title: Add consolidation and run the 20-write test
tactics.body: Memory hygiene is scheduled work, not a hope. Checklist: Cap-triggered consolidation works; Superseded entries show latest form only; Early facts still answered correctly at the end Implement consolidation and prove durability. Consolidation: when a section exceeds its cap, run a consolidation prompt over that section (merge overlapping entries, drop superseded ones, keep the newest phrasing, never drop unique facts) and rewrite it within cap - triggered automatically at session end when needed. The 20-write test: script a series of sessions performing 20+ memory updates including deliberate… If stuck: Consolidation dropped a unique fact. Re-run with the rule 'compress wording, never delete unique semantics' emphasized, and add a post-consolidation diff check that every removed line has a surviving semantic match.
checklist: Cap-triggered consolidation works
Superseded entries show latest form only
Early facts still answered correctly at the end

tactics.title: Add Loading/Error States: Inventory async surfaces
tactics.body: List every place the app waits or can fail. Checklist: Every fetch and mutation is listed; Gaps verified by actual throttling/failure tests; Empty-capable lists identified Scan the app and produce a table of every async surface: data fetches (per view), mutations (per button/form), and lists that can be empty. For each record: current loading treatment (none/spinner/skeleton), current error treatment (none/console/UI), and empty-state presence. Test each by throttling the network and forcing a failure in devtools. If stuck: The table missed surfaces. Grep for every fetch/axios/mutation call and every list render, and re-verify each with throttled network.
checklist: Every fetch and mutation is listed
Gaps verified by actual throttling/failure tests
Empty-capable lists identified

tactics.title: Add Loading/Error States: Add loading states
tactics.body: Replace blank waits with skeletons and spinners. Checklist: Skeletons appear under slow network; Pending buttons disable and indicate work; Content swap causes no jarring shift Add loading treatments to every fetch and mutation. Requirements: list/detail views get skeletons matching their layout; buttons get spinners or label changes and are disabled while pending; page transitions with data get a top-level loading treatment; avoid layout shift when content arrives. No artificial delays. If stuck: Blank flashes remain under throttling. Add skeleton components to the missing views and gate content render on the loading flag.
checklist: Skeletons appear under slow network
Pending buttons disable and indicate work
Content swap causes no jarring shift

tactics.title: Add Loading/Error States: Add error states with retry
tactics.body: Failures must be visible and recoverable. Checklist: Forced fetch failure shows error + retry; Mutation failure preserves user input; No empty catch blocks remain Add error handling to every async surface. Requirements: fetch failures render an inline error card with a Retry button that refetches; mutation failures show a toast or inline message with the reason and keep user input intact; remove empty catch blocks; global handler for unexpected errors so nothing is swallowed. Force a failure on each surface to verify. If stuck: Some failures are still silent. Search for try/catch blocks and promise chains without UI handling, and wire each to a visible error treatment; re-force failures to verify.
checklist: Forced fetch failure shows error + retry
Mutation failure preserves user input
No empty catch blocks remain

tactics.title: Add Loading/Error States: Add empty states
tactics.body: Empty is a state, not a bug - design it. Checklist: New-account emptiness is handled; No-results emptiness has distinct copy; Empty states include a useful action Add empty states to every list/collection view. Requirements: an icon or illustration, one sentence explaining why it is empty, and a primary action to fill it (e.g. 'Create your first project'); differentiate 'no data yet' from 'no search results' with appropriate copy; verify each by clearing data or searching nonsense. If stuck: Lists still render blank space when empty. Add the empty component branch to each list render, with copy and action per view.
checklist: New-account emptiness is handled
No-results emptiness has distinct copy
Empty states include a useful action

tactics.title: Add Loading/Error States: States QA sweep
tactics.body: Verify the app under slow, broken, and empty conditions. Checklist: Throttled pass completed; Forced-failure pass completed; Fresh-account empty pass completed; All failures fixed Run the states QA: with throttled network, walk every view (loading verified); with backend killed or forced 500s, walk every fetch and one mutation per form (errors verified, retry works); with a fresh/emptied account, walk every list (empty states verified); rapid-click every async button (single-fire verified). Report PASS/FAIL per surface with fixes applied. If stuck: The sweep skipped conditions. Re-run all three passes (slow, failing, empty) surface by surface and fix each gap found.
checklist: Throttled pass completed
Forced-failure pass completed
Fresh-account empty pass completed
All failures fixed

tactics.title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent: Design the todo data model and tool
tactics.flow_title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent
tactics.step_title: Design the todo data model and tool
tactics.body: Structured plans beat prose plans because the harness can enforce them. Checklist: Full-list-replace semantics chosen and documented; One in_progress enforced by validation; State lives in the harness, not chat history Design a todo subsystem for the agent. Data model: a list of items, each with id, content (imperative phrase), and status (pending | in_progress | completed). Tool interface: todo_write(items) replaces the full list (simplest correct design - the model always sends the complete list). Harness rules to implement: reject lists with more than one in_progress item; reject status regressions from completed to pending… If stuck: The todo tool accepts partial updates and state is drifting. Switch to full-list replacement: the model sends the entire list every call, and the harness validates it as a whole - simpler and self-healing.
checklist: Full-list-replace semantics chosen and documented
One in_progress enforced by validation
State lives in the harness, not chat history

tactics.title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent: Render the plan into context every turn
tactics.flow_title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent
tactics.step_title: Render the plan into context every turn
tactics.body: A plan the model cannot see is a plan it will not follow. Checklist: Reminder block regenerated from state each turn; Block stays compact (under 15 lines); Logged context confirms freshness Implement plan rendering: every turn, after tool results are folded in, append a synthetic system-style reminder block containing the current todo list rendered compactly (id, status marker, content), the current in_progress item highlighted, and counts (done/total). Keep it under 15 lines. This block is regenerated each turn from harness state so it never goes stale. Verify by logging the exact context sent to the… If stuck: The model references an outdated plan. Confirm the reminder block is rebuilt from harness state each turn rather than appended once - stale copies in history should be superseded by the latest block.
checklist: Reminder block regenerated from state each turn
Block stays compact (under 15 lines)
Logged context confirms freshness

tactics.title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent: Enforce plan-first and completion gates
tactics.flow_title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent
tactics.body: The two gates that turn a todo list into reliability. Checklist: Plan-first gate blocks premature tool use; Completion gate blocks finishing with open items; Items can be cancelled with a recorded reason Add two harness gates. Gate 1 (plan-first): if the user task is non-trivial (heuristic: request mentions multiple actions, or the model's first response proposes multiple steps), require a todo_write call before any other tool executes - if the model tries to skip, return a corrective message. Gate 2 (completion): when the model signals finish, check todo state; if pending or in_progress items remain, block the… If stuck: The agent finishes with pending items anyway. Ensure the finish path checks harness todo state (not the model's claim) and that the block message lists the exact open items so the model can act on them.
checklist: Plan-first gate blocks premature tool use
Completion gate blocks finishing with open items
Items can be cancelled with a recorded reason

tactics.title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent: Test the full planning lifecycle
tactics.flow_title: Add a Plan/Todo System to Your Agent
tactics.body: Prove the plan survives execution, failure, and resumption. Checklist: Happy path executes items in order; Failed step is never marked completed; Resume continues from the correct item Run three lifecycle tests. Test A (happy path): a 5-step task - verify plan created first, items move pending -> in_progress -> completed one at a time, finish allowed only at 5/5. Test B (failure mid-plan): make step 3 fail - verify the item stays in_progress or gains a new corrective item rather than being falsely completed. Test C (resume): stop the loop after step 2, restart with persisted state - verify the… If stuck: After resume the agent restarts from step 1. Persist todo state outside the process (file or DB) keyed by session, and rehydrate it into the reminder block before the first resumed turn.
checklist: Happy path executes items in order
Failed step is never marked completed
Resume continues from the correct item

tactics.step_title: Feed it the real task and require evidence

tactics.flow_title: Stand Up an Adversarial Verification Agent
tactics.body: A verdict nobody acts on is decoration. tactics.title: Implement the Six Core Orchestration Patterns: Build the shared lifecycle infrastructure
tactics.flow_title: Implement the Six Core Orchestration Patterns
tactics.body: Six patterns, one chassis: registration, state, delivery, cleanup. Checklist: Child abort scopes independent of the parent's; Reports arrive in the parent's next turn, verified; Cleanup runs on normal, error, and cancel paths (tested) Implement the agent lifecycle layer all patterns share. Registration: every dispatched child gets an id, a state (foreground/background/completed/failed/cancelled), and its own cancellation scope - a child's abort control must be independent so cancelling the parent's current step does not kill background workers. Delivery: completed children enqueue their report through one notification path that inserts it into… If stuck: Background children die when the user cancels the parent's step. Your cancellation scopes are shared - give each child its own controller at registration and have the parent's cancel signal exclude background ids explicitly.

tactics.step_title: Implement fan-out patterns: worker pool and fork-join
tactics.body: Parallelism is the payoff; delivery discipline is the price. Checklist: Single-turn parallel dispatch with disjoint work slices; Join proceeds sensibly on partial failure; Per-child timeout and concurrency cap enforced Build the two fan-out patterns on the chassis. WORKER POOL: dispatch N same-type children in a single turn, each with an independent slice of the work (a checklist the orchestrator prompt enforces: disjoint scopes, uniform report format); collect reports as they deliver; the parent merges once all arrive. FORK-JOIN: the same shape but with fork-mode dispatch (inherited context) for splittable research - the join… If stuck: The join hangs waiting for a dead worker. Every child must deliver SOMETHING on every exit path - wire the failure/cancellation paths to enqueue a failure report through the same delivery mechanism, so the join's completion condition is…

tactics.body: Verification pressure plus leak-free operation makes it production-grade. tactics.title: Agent-to-Agent Protocols (A2A): Define the protocol
tactics.body: Write the message schemas and state machine before any agent code. Checklist: Envelope and all message types specified; State machine covers rejection and failure; Two failure sequences diagrammed Define a minimal A2A protocol. Message envelope: {message_id, correlation_id, sender, recipient, type, timestamp, body}. Message types: task_submit {intent, payload, deadline}, task_ack {accepted: bool, reason?}, task_status {state, note}, task_result {ok, output, evidence?}, task_reject {reason, retryable: bool}. Task state machine: submitted -> accepted -> working -> (completed | failed); submitted -> rejected.… If stuck: The protocol has no failure paths. Add them first - the value of a protocol is almost entirely in what happens when things go wrong.

tactics.title: Agent-to-Agent Protocols (A2A): Build the message layer
tactics.body: Reliable-enough transport with full observability. tactics.title: Agent-to-Agent Protocols (A2A): Wrap agents as protocol endpoints
tactics.body: Each agent's loop stays private; the protocol is its public face. Checklist: Ack and status sent at the right moments; Critiques are structured, not prose blobs; Invalid payloads rejected with reasons Wrap two agents as protocol endpoints. The builder agent: accepts build_component tasks, runs its internal loop (plan, code, self-check), and returns task_result with the artifact and a brief evidence note. The reviewer agent: accepts review_component tasks, evaluates the artifact against the payload's acceptance criteria, and returns either approval or a structured critique list (issue, location, severity,… If stuck: The reviewer returns an essay the builder cannot parse. tactics.title: Agent-to-Agent Protocols (A2A): Run the revision loop with failure injection
tactics.step_title: Run the revision loop with failure injection

tactics.title: API/Error Handling QA: Inventory the API contracts
tactics.body: Write down what every endpoint promises before testing it. Checklist: Every endpoint appears with expected codes; A single error shape is defined; Unknowns are flagged for testing Produce the API contract inventory: every endpoint with method, path, purpose, auth requirement, request shape, success response (code + body shape), and the expected failure responses (validation 400, unauthorized 401/403, not found 404, conflict 409, server 500). tactics.title: API/Error Handling QA: Test success and failure codes
tactics.body: Fire real requests: does each endpoint honor its contract? Checklist: Every endpoint was hit with all scenario classes; No 200s carrying errors remain; Bad input yields 400s, not 500s Test every endpoint with real requests (curl/fetch): the success case (verify code and body shape); invalid input (must be 400 with the standard error shape, not 500 or 200-with-error-string); missing/invalid auth (401/403); nonexistent resources (404, not empty 200 or 500); wrong methods (405 or clean rejection). Record the result matrix endpoint-by-endpoint and fix every deviation, then re-test the fixed ones. If stuck: Bad input still causes 500s. Add validation at the endpoint boundary returning 400 with the standard shape, and re-run the exact failing requests.

Requirements: a global error handler producing the standard shape for all failures; no stack traces, internal paths, or query details in any response (log those server-side instead); consistent codes per failure class; validation errors including field-level details the frontend can render; verify by re-triggering each failure class and diffing the shapes. If stuck: Different endpoints still return different error formats. Route all exceptions through the global handler and re-trigger each class to confirm uniformity.

No internals leak in responses
Field-level validation details included

tactics.title: API/Error Handling QA: Verify frontend failure handling

Checklist: Each class was forced against the real UI; No silent or console-only failures remain; Retry paths work where offered Verify the frontend handles each failure class. Force each against the running app: 400 validation (field errors render at the fields); 401 (redirect to login or session-expired message); 403 (permission message, no crash); 404 (not-found state); 500 (visible error with retry); network-down (offline-style error, no white screen). No failure may produce a silent nothing, an infinite spinner, or a console-only error.… If stuck: Some classes still fail silently. Map each response class in the API client to a UI treatment and re-force every class to verify the rendering.

No silent or console-only failures remain

tactics.flow_title: Assemble a System Prompt Like the Pros
tactics.body: A rule the harness cannot check is a wish. Checklist: Every rule has an enforcement decision; Three harness guards implemented and tested; Prompt-only rules are marked as accepted risk Take every hard rule and decide its enforcement. For each rule choose: (a) harness-enforced - implement a code check (e.g. 'never edit unread files' becomes a read-before-write guard; 'never touch .env' becomes a path blocklist in the write tool), (b) test-enforced - write an eval case that fails if the model violates it, or (c) prompt-only - keep it in the prompt but mark it as unverified risk. Produce a rules… If stuck: Rules exist only as prose. Pick the single most dangerous rule and implement its code guard today - then verify the guard fires by deliberately violating the rule in a test.

tactics.title: Assemble a System Prompt Like the Pros: Ablate to prove section value
tactics.flow_title: Assemble a System Prompt Like the Pros
tactics.body: Measure the prompt like a system, not a spell. Checklist: Every section tested by removal; Suite covers tools, rules, and format; Final prompt smaller or better-justified than the original Run an ablation pass over the assembled prompt. For each major section, build a variant with that section removed and run a fixed 5-task smoke suite (mix of tool use, rule compliance, and formatting). Record per-variant: task success, rule violations, and format breaks. Sections whose removal changes nothing are candidates for cutting or merging; sections whose removal breaks rules confirm their value. Deliver the… If stuck: Ablation results are noisy. Suite covers tools, rules, and format

tactics.title: Audit Trails for Tool Calls: Define the audit record and scope
tactics.step_title: Define the audit record and scope
tactics.body: Decide what is auditable and what each record must answer. Checklist: Consequential actions scoped; trivia excluded; Authority and triggering request captured; Who/what/when/why/outcome answerable Design the audit record. SCOPE: audit consequential actions - state mutations (writes, deletes), external effects (network calls, sends, spends), permission decisions, and security-relevant events (blocks, escalations); read-only trivia need not be audited (avoid drowning the trail). RECORD FIELDS: timestamp, actor (agent id + session), action (tool + operation), arguments (scrubbed, but specific - which file,… If stuck: Records show what happened but not why it was allowed. Add the authority and triggering-request fields - an audit trail that cannot explain why an action was permitted is useless in an incident.
checklist: Consequential actions scoped; trivia excluded
Authority and triggering request captured
Who/what/when/why/outcome answerable

tactics.title: Audit Trails for Tool Calls: Write records reliably and scrubbed
tactics.body: Non-suppressible, secret-free, at the moment of action. Checklist: Records sourced from harness state, not model claims; Auditing not suppressible by the model; High-sensitivity actions fail closed if audit fails Implement audit writing in the action path. Every consequential tool execution writes its audit record at execution time (before returning), sourced from harness state (the permission decision, the request lineage) - not from anything the model can fabricate or omit; the model cannot disable auditing. Run record content through the secrets scrubber (from secrets hygiene) so the trail is safe to retain, while… If stuck: Some consequential actions have no record. Move the audit write into the same choke point that executes and permission-checks actions - if auditing is a separate optional step, it will be skipped exactly when it matters.
checklist: Records sourced from harness state, not model claims
Auditing not suppressible by the model
High-sensitivity actions fail closed if audit fails

tactics.title: Audit Trails for Tool Calls: Make the trail tamper-evident
tactics.body: An alterable audit trail is not evidence. Checklist: Integrity chaining or write-once storage in place; Verification detects alterations and deletions; Write access restricted to the audit path Add tamper-evidence to audit storage. Options by environment: hash-chaining (each record includes the hash of the previous, so any alteration or deletion breaks the chain and is detectable) is a strong self-contained choice; or a write-once/append-only store (WORM storage, an append-only table with restricted permissions, or shipping records to a separate system the agent's host cannot rewrite). Implement chain… If stuck: Altering a record went undetected. Ensure each record commits to the previous (hash chain) or lives in truly append-only storage - if records are independently editable in place, the trail is not evidence.
checklist: Integrity chaining or write-once storage in place
Verification detects alterations and deletions
Write access restricted to the audit path

tactics.title: Audit Trails for Tool Calls: Enable investigation and set retention
tactics.body: The trail proves its worth when someone has to ask hard questions of it. Checklist: Resource-history and authority queries work; Retention and read-access controls set; Incident drill fully answered from the trail Make the trail usable and governed. INVESTIGATION: build queries that answer real questions - all actions in a session, full history affecting a given resource (every write/delete to file/record X, with who/why), all actions authorized by a specific approval, and all security events in a window; support reconstructing an incident timeline from the records. RETENTION & ACCESS: set retention appropriate to… If stuck: The drill hit a question the trail could not answer. The gap is a missing link or field (usually the request-to-action lineage) - add it to the record schema and backfill the linkage so the trail supports real investigations, not just…
checklist: Resource-history and authority queries work
Retention and read-access controls set
Incident drill fully answered from the trail

tactics.title: Auth Flow QA: Test the signup surface
tactics.body: Account creation is the front door - test it including the ugly inputs. Checklist: A real record was verified created; Duplicate rejection is visible in the UI; No plaintext password exists Execute signup tests with a fresh state and record PASS/FAIL with observations: valid signup creates a persisted account (verify the record exists) and lands correctly with an active session; duplicate email is rejected with a visible, non-technical error; each validation rule fires inline (empty fields, bad email format, short password, mismatched confirmation); the submit button disables while working; the… If stuck: Signup tests skipped verification of the stored record. Query the user store after the test signup and confirm the record with a hashed password.
checklist: A real record was verified created
Duplicate rejection is visible in the UI
No plaintext password exists

tactics.title: Auth Flow QA: Test the login surface
tactics.body: Login must pass friends and stop strangers - test both. Checklist: Wrong-password and no-account errors are identical; Failures are visible in the UI; Rapid attempts were actually tried Execute login tests and record results: correct credentials succeed and land with a session; wrong password is rejected with a generic visible error; nonexistent email is rejected with the SAME generic error (no account-existence leak); empty submits are blocked inline; five rapid wrong attempts behave sanely (no crash; rate limiting noted if present or absent); the loading state shows during authentication. If stuck: The error messages reveal whether an email exists. Normalize both failures to the same 'Invalid email or password' message and re-test.
checklist: Wrong-password and no-account errors are identical
Failures are visible in the UI
Rapid attempts were actually tried

tactics.title: Auth Flow QA: Test the session lifecycle
tactics.body: Sessions are where fake auth dies - test persistence hard. Checklist: Refresh and tab-reopen persistence verified; Post-logout API call rejected; Tampered token handled cleanly Execute session tests: refresh on a protected page (session persists, no logged-out flash); close and reopen the tab (persists); logout (session fully cleared - verify by trying a protected API call after); back button after logout (no protected content from cache); two browsers/sessions simultaneously (both work independently); token/session tampering (edit the stored token - app must reject and recover cleanly,… If stuck: Logout only hides the UI - the API still accepts the old session. Invalidate/clear the token on logout and verify a protected call fails afterward.
checklist: Refresh and tab-reopen persistence verified
Post-logout API call rejected
Tampered token handled cleanly

tactics.title: Auth Flow QA: Test guards at both layers
tactics.body: Routes and APIs must both reject the logged-out - verify by attack. Checklist: Every protected route URL-tested; Every private endpoint called directly; Post-login redirect returns to the intended page Execute guard tests from a fully logged-out state: open every protected route by direct URL (redirects to login, no content flash - list each route tested); call every private API endpoint directly (401/403 for each - list each endpoint); after logging in from a guard redirect, land on the originally-requested page; verify no logged-in-only data appears in any public page or response. Produce the two-layer guard… If stuck: API guards were assumed from route guards. Call each private endpoint with no session and fix any that return data - the API layer must enforce independently.
checklist: Every protected route URL-tested
Every private endpoint called directly
Post-login redirect returns to the intended page

tactics.title: Auth Flow QA: Test recovery and close
tactics.body: Reset flows and the final edge sweep complete the audit. Checklist: The reset actually changed the password; Token reuse was rejected; The consolidated table shows all sections passing Execute recovery tests (if reset exists): request reset for an existing email (neutral confirmation), and a nonexistent one (identical response); complete the reset - the new password works, the old fails, and the token is single-use (reuse rejected). Then the final sweep: session expiry handling (if tokens expire - expired token redirects cleanly), auth forms on mobile widths, and a summary table of the entire… If stuck: The reset email path was tested but the reset never completed. Execute the full reset: set the new password, log in with it, confirm the old fails, and retry the used token.
checklist: The reset actually changed the password
Token reuse was rejected
The consolidated table shows all sections passing

tactics.title: Integrate Background Jobs & Queue System: Implement a sample background job
tactics.body: Demonstrate real work performed asynchronously. Checklist: Does enqueueFetchUrl add a job to appQueue (check queue length increase)?; After a job runs, is there a new row in job_results with correct url and status? Create src/jobs/fetchUrlJob.js. Import { Worker } from "bullmq", the Queue from ../queue.js, and the DB client (assume an existing Prisma client exported from src/db.js). Define a processing function that receives a job with data { url: string }. tactics.step_title: Test errors and edge behavior through the protocol
tactics.body: Error paths are where integrations actually break. tactics.title: Build a Repo Map for Code Navigation: Rank by relevance
tactics.flow_title: Build a Repo Map for Code Navigation
tactics.body: The budget goes to what the task touches. Checklist: Import-graph centrality computed; Task text drives per-request scores; Top-10 lists match human judgment Implement ranking to decide what the map shows. Signals to combine: TASK RELEVANCE - lexical/semantic match between the task description (and conversation so far) and file paths + symbol names; GRAPH CENTRALITY - files imported/referenced by many others rank higher (build a light import graph; a PageRank-style pass over it is the proven approach); RECENCY - recently edited or recently discussed files get a boost;… If stuck: Rankings ignore the task. Check the task-relevance signal weight - centrality alone produces the same map for every request; the combination is what makes the map task-aware.

tactics.flow_title: Build a Repo Map for Code Navigation
tactics.body: Graceful degradation: many files shallowly, top files deeply. Given the ranked files and a token budget (e.g. 1-2k tokens): allocate detail by rank - top files show full symbol listings, middle files show class/function names only, tail files show path only; render compactly (a tree-ish layout with signatures indented under paths); always include a header stating what the map is and that the agent should open files before editing. If even paths… If stuck: The render blows the budget on long signatures. Truncate signatures (params elided past N chars) before dropping whole files - breadth of orientation beats parameter completeness.

Header explains usage
