tactics.title: Choose the Right Dispatch: Spawn, Fork, or Direct: Implement spawn: fresh context specialists
tactics.flow_title: Choose the Right Dispatch: Spawn, Fork, or Direct
tactics.body: A spawn is a new employee: they know only what the dispatch tells them. Checklist: Registry with prompt/tools/model/permission per definition; Child context contains zero parent history; Dispatch prompts carry complete background Build the spawn path. Maintain a registry of agent definitions (explorer, planner, verifier, general) each with: its own system prompt, tool list, default model (cheap+fast for read-only scouts, inherit for reasoning-heavy roles), and permission mode. On dispatch: look up the definition, build a FRESH context containing only the definition's system prompt plus the dispatch message - no parent history. Assemble the… If stuck: Spawned agents keep asking about things the parent already knows. That is the design - the fix is in the dispatch prompt, not shared state: require the orchestrator to include the missing background, or conclude this task wanted a fork…

Child context contains zero parent history

tactics.step_title: Implement fork: inherited context, shared cache
tactics.body: A fork is a clone at the current moment - cheap because the prefix is already paid for. Checklist: Placeholder results identical across sibling forks; System prompt and tool array reused byte-for-byte; Worker contract injected with every directive Build the fork path. The child's message list starts with the parent's conversation reproduced exactly, then: placeholder tool-results for any pending tool calls in the parent's last assistant message (identical placeholder text for every fork, so all siblings share the same byte prefix), followed by the child's directive as the only differing content. Use the parent's already-rendered system prompt bytes and the… If stuck: Fork children behave like chatty main agents. The behavior contract is missing or buried - inject it adjacent to the directive (the last thing in context), and verify your prefix stability by diffing two sibling requests: ev
checklist: Placeholder results identical across sibling forks
System prompt and tool array reused byte-for-byte
Worker contract injected with every directive

tactics.title: Choose the Right Dispatch: Spawn, Fork, or Direct: Add guards and async lifecycle
tactics.flow_title: Choose the Right Dispatch: Spawn, Fork, or Direct
tactics.body: Parallel dispatch needs recursion limits and a results path. Checklist: Recursion refused via two independent checks; Children survive parent-step cancellation; Parallel siblings share cache (verify via provider metrics) Add the safety rails. Recursion guard: mark forked children (a tag in their context and a flag in their execution options) and refuse fork/spawn requests from inside one - two independent checks, because a single guard eventually gets bypassed by a refactor. Run forks async by default: dispatch returns immediately with a task id; children execute in the background with independent abort handling (cancelling the… If stuck: Results arrive but the parent never acts on them. The notification path must inject reports as visible turn content, not a silent log - if the parent's next turn does not contain the child's report, the orchestration loop is broken…
checklist: Recursion refused via two independent checks
Children survive parent-step cancellation
Parallel siblings share cache (verify via provider metrics)

tactics.title: Choose the Right Dispatch: Spawn, Fork, or Direct: Encode the decision matrix
tactics.flow_title: Choose the Right Dispatch: Spawn, Fork, or Direct
tactics.body: The strategies only pay off if the orchestrator picks correctly. Checklist: Spawn/fork/direct each have stated conditions and costs; Prompt contains the policy, not just your docs; Transcript audit confirms correct choices predominate Write the decision policy and put it in the orchestrator's prompt. SPAWN when the task needs a specialist definition (exploration with a cheap model, planning, verification), when context isolation is the point (an investigation whose noise should not pollute the parent), or when a different permission/tool profile is required. FORK when the task is splittable research or implementation where the parent's context… If stuck: The orchestrator still forks specialists and spawns trivia. Add contrast examples to the prompt (three tasks, three correct choices, one sentence why) - decision policies land far better as worked examples than as abstract rules.
checklist: Spawn/fork/direct each have stated conditions and costs
Prompt contains the policy, not just your docs
Transcript audit confirms correct choices predominate

tactics.title: From CLI Harness to Product: Implement persistent sessions
tactics.body: Sessions turn a script into a tool people trust with long work. Checklist: Saved after every turn, not on exit; Session includes plan state and cwd; Kill -9 mid-run leaves a loadable session Add session persistence to the harness. tactics.body: Verify the full conversation lifecycle across both roles. Checklist: The full conversation was executed across roles; States verified after refresh on both sides; Third-account scoping verified QA the support system end to end with a user and an admin account: user submits; admin sees it, replies, sets in-progress; user sees the reply and indicator, responds; admin resolves; user sees resolved. Verify every state after refresh on both sides; empty states for fresh accounts; validation and error paths on both forms; scoping with a third account. Fix everything that fails and re-run. If stuck: The lifecycle was tested from one side only. Run the two-account conversation to resolution, refreshing at each step, and fix any state that does not propagate.
checklist: The full conversation was executed across roles
States verified after refresh on both sides
Third-account scoping verified

tactics.title: Add Dark Mode Toggle: Create Theme Context
tactics.body: Provide global theme state and toggle function. Checklist: Can the app import { ThemeProvider } without syntax errors?; Does localStorage.getItem('appTheme') return a value on first load?; Does calling toggleTheme switch the stored value between 'light' and 'dark'? Create a new file src/theme/ThemeContext.{js,tsx} that: 1. Imports createContext, useState, useEffect from React. 2. Defines a ThemeContext via createContext({ theme: 'light', toggleTheme: () => {} }). 3. Exports a ThemeProvider component that: a. Initializes theme state from localStorage key 'appTheme' (fallback 'light'). b. Provides toggleTheme that switches between 'light' and 'dark', updates state, and writes… If stuck: The generated ThemeContext does not actually persist to localStorage or fails to export. Provide concrete code that fulfills all three checklist items.
checklist: Can the app import { ThemeProvider } without syntax errors?
Does localStorage.getItem('appTheme') return a value on first load?
Does calling toggleTheme switch the stored value between 'light' and 'dark'?

tactics.title: Add Dark Mode Toggle: Define Light/Dark CSS Variables
tactics.body: Enable UI styling based on the theme value. Checklist: Inspect compiled CSS: does .dark change background color?; Changing the <html> or <body> class to 'dark' updates variables? In the main stylesheet (e.g., src/index.css or src/global.scss): 1. Define CSS variables inside :root for --bg-color, --text-color, etc., using light theme defaults. 2. Create a .dark selector that redefines those variables with dark theme values. 3. Ensure the stylesheet is imported at the app root. 4. Do not include any placeholder comments; provide concrete color values. If stuck: If toggling the 'dark' class does not affect colors, rewrite the CSS with proper variable definitions and ensure the class selector is correct.
checklist: Inspect compiled CSS: does .dark change background color?
Changing the <html> or <body> class to 'dark' updates variables?

tactics.title: Add Dark Mode Toggle: Build DarkModeToggle Component
tactics.body: Provide UI for users to switch themes. Checklist: Can import DarkModeToggle without errors?; Clicking the button flips the theme value in context? In src/components/DarkModeToggle.{js,tsx}: 1. Import React, useContext, and ThemeContext. 2. Render a button showing an icon or text indicating the current theme (e.g., ☀️ for light, 🌙 for dark). 3. On click, invoke toggleTheme from context. 4. Export the component as default. 5. Do not include placeholder UI; provide real button markup. If stuck: If the component fails to import or the click does nothing, provide a corrected implementation that satisfies the checklist.
checklist: Can import DarkModeToggle without errors?
Clicking the button flips the theme value in context?

tactics.title: Add Dark Mode Toggle: Apply Theme Class at Root
tactics.body: Bind the CSS dark class to the current theme state. Checklist: Inspect DOM after toggle: does <div> have class 'dark'?; Background color changes correspond to CSS variables? In src/index.js (or wherever <App/> is rendered): 1. Import ThemeProvider and ThemeContext. 2. Wrap <App/> with <ThemeProvider>. 3. Inside a top‑level component (e.g., App or a Layout), use useContext(ThemeContext) to get theme. 4. Apply className={theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : ''} to the topmost <div> that contains the app. 5. Ensure the class updates instantly on toggle. 6. No placeholder comments; fully functional… If stuck: When the class does not appear or colors stay the same, provide corrected code that binds the class to the theme value.
checklist: Inspect DOM after toggle: does <div> have class 'dark'?
Background color changes correspond to CSS variables?

tactics.title: Add Dark Mode Toggle: Integrate Toggle into UI
tactics.body: Place the DarkModeToggle where users can access it. Checklist: Is the toggle visible in the header?; Does clicking it change the theme instantly? In src/components/Header.{js,tsx}: 1. Import DarkModeToggle. 2. Add <DarkModeToggle /> to the JSX, preferably on the right side of the header. 3. Ensure the header still renders correctly and the toggle is visible. 4. No placeholder comments; component must be used in real JSX. If stuck: When the button is invisible or non‑functional, provide corrected Header code that satisfies the checklist.
checklist: Is the toggle visible in the header?
Does clicking it change the theme instantly?

tactics.title: Add Dark Mode Toggle: Validate Persistence Across Sessions
tactics.body: Ensure the chosen theme remains after page reloads. Checklist: localStorage.getItem('appTheme') matches UI theme after reload; Automated test suite reports PASS for theme persistence Manually test the app: 1. Click DarkModeToggle to switch to dark mode. 2. Observe the root element gains 'dark' class. 3. Refresh the browser. 4. Verify that the 'dark' class is still present and the UI remains dark. 5. Repeat for light mode. 6. No code to write; just produce a verification script. If you prefer automated verification, add a small test in src/__tests__/theme.test.{js,tsx} that: - Mocks… If stuck: When persistence is broken, ensure ThemeProvider reads from localStorage on mount and that the test correctly mocks and verifies it.
checklist: localStorage.getItem('appTheme') matches UI theme after reload
Automated test suite reports PASS for theme persistence

tactics.title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks: Build multi-view quote extraction
tactics.flow_title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks
tactics.body: Different attacks are visible at different stripping levels. Checklist: Three views produced and documented with their use cases; Backslash processed before quote toggling; Tracker edge cases covered by tests Implement an extraction function producing three views of every command: KEEP-DOUBLE (single-quoted content stripped, double-quoted kept - because shell metacharacters like ';' and '|' still act inside double quotes in some positions and this view exposes them), FULLY-UNQUOTED (all quoted content stripped - the view for redirection detection, since quoted '<' and '>' are inert), and KEEP-QUOTE-CHARS (content… If stuck: The tracker desyncs on a command with an escaped double quote. That is the classic ordering bug: handle the backslash first (consume the next character unconditionally outside single quotes) and only then consider quote toggling - re-run…
checklist: Three views produced and documented with their use cases
Backslash processed before quote toggling
Tracker edge cases covered by tests

tactics.title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks: Detect quote-trick flag smuggling
tactics.flow_title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks
tactics.body: Flags assembled from quote fragments defeat every naive flag check. Checklist: ANSI-C, empty-quote, quote-chain, and triple-quote detectors implemented; All detectors run on the original string; Benign dash-containing filenames pass Implement detectors for the flag-smuggling family, each on the ORIGINAL string. ANSI-C quoting: any occurrence of the $'...' form can encode arbitrary characters including dashes - ask on sight in argument positions. Empty-quote concatenation: patterns of empty quote pairs followed by a dash (a shell joins the empty string with '-exec' to produce a flag your parser saw as a filename) - detect adjacent empty quotes… If stuck: The quote-chain detector floods benign commands with asks. Tighten it: only fire when the assembled word starts with a dash AND sits in an argument position where a flag would change semantics - the goal is smuggled FLAGS, not any…
checklist: ANSI-C, empty-quote, quote-chain, and triple-quote detectors implemented
All detectors run on the original string
Benign dash-containing filenames pass

tactics.title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks: Detect parser-vs-shell divergence
tactics.flow_title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks
tactics.body: The deadliest class: your parser sees one command, bash runs two. Checklist: Outermost-level comma/range detection with nesting depth; Escaped-operator detection outside double quotes only; Known false positives documented as accepted Implement the divergence detectors. Brace expansion: your parser reads '{a,b}' as one literal token but bash expands it into multiple arguments - detect unquoted braces containing commas or dot-dot ranges at the outermost nesting level, imbalanced braces after quote stripping, and quoted brace characters in the original (a hiding pattern); ask on all three. Backslash-escaped operators: in bash, an escaped semicolon… If stuck: A legitimate brace-using command keeps asking. Verify your nesting-depth logic only fires at the outermost level and ignores quoted braces; if it is genuinely a brace expansion, the ask is CORRECT - the user approves it once, which is
checklist: Outermost-level comma/range detection with nesting depth
Escaped-operator detection outside double quotes only
Known false positives documented as accepted

tactics.title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks: Grow the regression corpus
tactics.flow_title: Detect Command Obfuscation and Parser-Mismatch Attacks
tactics.body: Obfuscation is an arms race; the corpus is your institutional memory. Checklist: Corpus covers all families plus mutations and benign twins; New bypasses become tests before fixes; Periodic red-team pass scheduled Assemble the obfuscation corpus: every attack variant from the previous steps plus mutations (different quote types, whitespace variants, unicode lookalike characters - flag non-ASCII in security-relevant positions outright), each labeled with the expected outcome and the detector expected to fire. Add an equal weight of benign commands asserting no false fires. Wire it into CI as a blocking suite. Establish the… If stuck: The corpus passes but a manual red-team trick still gets through. Add it to the corpus immediately even before you know the fix - a failing test that documents a real bypass is worth more than a green suite that lies.
checklist: Corpus covers all families plus mutations and benign twins
New bypasses become tests before fixes
Periodic red-team pass scheduled

tactics.title: Deferred Tool Loading: Measure usage and pick the core
tactics.step_title: Measure usage and pick the core
tactics.body: The data decides what stays eager. Checklist: Frequency and timing measured from real logs; Safety-critical tools kept eager; Savings projection computed Analyze tool usage to define the core set. From transcript logs, compute per-tool: call frequency across sessions, task-type coverage (which task categories touch it), and first-call timing (tools needed in early turns favor eager loading). Also measure the token cost of each tool's definition. Core-set criteria: high frequency OR early-turn necessity OR safety-critical (permission gates should not be deferred).… If stuck: No usage logs exist. Instrument tool-call logging now and run a week of normal usage first - core-set guesses without data produce exactly the discovery failures this flow exists to avoid.
checklist: Frequency and timing measured from real logs
Safety-critical tools kept eager
Savings projection computed

tactics.title: Deferred Tool Loading: Build the catalog and discovery
tactics.body: The model can only load what it can find. Checklist: One steering line per deferred tool; Catalog cost is a small fraction of definitions; Model issues load_tools unprompted in the test Implement discovery. Build the deferred-tool catalog: one line per tool - name plus a purpose phrase written like a steering description in miniature ('code_metrics: complexity and duplication reports for source files'). Include the catalog in context under a header explaining: 'additional tools exist; call load_tools([names]) to activate the ones your task needs'. Group the catalog by capability area for… If stuck: The model never calls load_tools. Strengthen the header with one worked example (task X -> load [Y]) and check the catalog phrasing - purpose phrases must contain the words a task description would use.
checklist: One steering line per deferred tool
Catalog cost is a small fraction of definitions
Model issues load_tools unprompted in the test

tactics.title: Deferred Tool Loading: Implement dynamic registration
tactics.body: Mid-session loading that keeps the loop and cache sane. Checklist: Loaded tools callable immediately; Unknown names get suggestions; Cache resets logged and batched Implement load_tools(names). On call: validate names against the catalog; register the requested tools' full definitions into the session's active toolset; return a confirmation listing the loaded tools with their descriptions; keep them active for the session's remainder. Cache-awareness: append newly-loaded definitions in a stable position per your provider's tool-definition handling (accept the one-time cache… If stuck: Calls to a just-loaded tool fail. Check that registration updates the actual toolset sent on the NEXT model call (not a stale snapshot) - the definition must be present in the request for the model to call it validly.
checklist: Loaded tools callable immediately
Unknown names get suggestions
Cache resets logged and batched

tactics.title: Deferred Tool Loading: Measure savings and guard capability
tactics.body: Prove the win and prove nothing broke. Checklist: 10-task savings report produced; Regression matches all-eager completion; Discovery failures diagnosed and fixed Run the evaluation. SAVINGS: measure tool-definition tokens per session before vs after deferral across 10 representative tasks; report average and range. CAPABILITY: run a regression suite of tasks that collectively require several deferred tools; success requires the model discovering, loading, and using each without human help; compare completion rates against the all-eager baseline. DISCOVERY FAILURES: for any… If stuck: A capability regression appeared. Promote that tool to core OR fix its catalog line - and add the failing task to the permanent regression suite so the fix stays fixed.
checklist: 10-task savings report produced
Regression matches all-eager completion
Discovery failures diagnosed and fixed

tactics.title: Demo Video Script: Choose format and story
tactics.body: One video, one audience, one story - decide before scripting. Checklist: Length matches the placement; The story is one persona, one task; The magic moment is identified Plan my demo video. I will describe the product and where the video will live below. Recommend: the right length (30s hook video vs 90s standard vs 3min deep demo) with reasoning; the ONE user story to follow (a named persona with a concrete task, start to finish); and the magic moment - the single most impressive beat - with where it should land in the timeline (before 40%). List what NOT to show. PRODUCT AND… If stuck: The plan is a feature tour. Replace it with one persona completing one real task, and cut every screen that does not advance that story.
checklist: Length matches the placement
The story is one persona, one task
The magic moment is identified

tactics.title: Demo Video Script: Write the hook and opening
tactics.body: Viewers decide in 5 seconds - open with the pain or the payoff. Checklist: Each hook works in 5 seconds; The chosen open shows something real; The setup is one sentence Write the demo opening. Produce 3 hook options for the first 5 seconds: a pain cold-open ('Here is the mess this replaces'), a payoff-first open (show the end result, then rewind), and a bold-claim open. Each with: exact narration line and exact first screen shown. Then recommend one and write the transition from hook into the story setup (5-15 seconds) naming the persona and task in one sentence. If stuck: The opening starts with a logo and welcome. Cut straight to the pain or the payoff in second one - branding can live in the corner.
checklist: Each hook works in 5 seconds
The chosen open shows something real
The setup is one sentence

tactics.title: Demo Video Script: Script the core demo beats
tactics.body: The middle must show, not tell - every beat pairs action and line. Checklist: Narration adds context, never describes the visible; The magic moment gets emphasis; Actions are click-by-click specific Script the core demo (the middle 60-70%). Produce timestamped beats where each beat has: the exact screen action (what I click/type - specific), the narration line (add context the screen cannot show - never describe what is visible), and any zoom/highlight callouts. Follow the user story to the magic moment, land it with a beat of silence or emphasis, then complete the task's payoff. Keep narration lines under 15… If stuck: The narration reads the screen aloud. Rewrite every line to say why it matters or what just happened invisibly - the viewer can see the what.
checklist: Narration adds context, never describes the visible
The magic moment gets emphasis
Actions are click-by-click specific

tactics.title: Demo Video Script: Write the close and CTA
tactics.body: End with proof and one clear action. Checklist: The recap mirrors the opening pain; Exactly one CTA; The final frame has name, URL, action Write the demo close (final 10-20%). Produce: the result recap in one line (what the persona now has, tied to the opening pain); an optional proof beat (a number, a second quick example, or a testimonial line); the CTA - one action, spoken and on-screen (try it, sign up, link) with any friction-remover (free, no card); and the final frame contents (product name, URL, CTA). No new features in the close. If stuck: The close introduces three more features and two CTAs. Cut to: result recap, one proof, one action, end card.
checklist: The recap mirrors the opening pain
Exactly one CTA
The final frame has name, URL, action

tactics.title: Demo Video Script: Prepare the recording checklist
tactics.body: Great scripts die to sloppy recordings - prep the environment. Checklist: Demo data is specified realistically; Notifications and clutter are handled; A dry run precedes recording Create my recording checklist: demo data preparation (realistic names/content matching the persona - list exactly what to create, no 'test 123'); app state reset steps so the flow starts clean; environment (resolution 1920x1080 or as needed, browser zoom, hide bookmarks/notifications/dock, close other tabs); audio notes (mic check line, room, pace - read narration at conversational speed); and a dry-run… If stuck: The checklist skips demo data, which produces 'asdf test' embarrassments. Script the exact records to pre-create so every screen shows a believable world.
checklist: Demo data is specified realistically
Notifications and clutter are handled
A dry run precedes recording

tactics.title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents: Intercept dependency additions
tactics.flow_title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents
tactics.body: Every new dependency is a trust decision - catch it at the source. Checklist: Installs and manifest/lockfile edits both caught; New vs existing dependency distinguished; Write-then-install evasion covered Hook the dependency-adding actions. Identify every way the agent can add a dependency: package-manager install commands (pip install, npm/yarn add, etc.), direct edits to manifests (requirements.txt, package.json, pyproject, go.mod), and lockfile edits. Route these through a supply-chain gate before they take effect: parse out the package name(s) and version(s) being added, and pause for the checks (next steps)… If stuck: The agent edited the manifest then installed, dodging the gate. Gate on the manifest/lockfile change too, not just the install command - and treat installing after a just-made manifest edit as the same reviewable event.
checklist: Installs and manifest/lockfile edits both caught
New vs existing dependency distinguished
Write-then-install evasion covered

tactics.title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents: Verify existence and reputation
tactics.flow_title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents
tactics.body: The defining AI supply-chain risk: packages that should not be trusted or do not exist. Checklist: Non-existent packages blocked; Typosquat/lookalike detection via name similarity; Legitimate popular packages pass cleanly Implement existence and reputation checks. EXISTENCE: query the package registry - does this exact name exist? A non-existent package (common with AI hallucination) is blocked outright with 'package X not found on the registry - verify the name'. REPUTATION/TYPOSQUAT: for packages that do exist, check signals - age (brand-new packages matching a popular name are high risk), download/usage volume, and similarity to… If stuck: A lookalike passed as legitimate. Strengthen similarity detection against the registry's top packages and weight brand-new-plus-similar as high risk - slopsquatting relies on names one keystroke from real ones combined with recent creation.
checklist: Non-existent packages blocked
Typosquat/lookalike detection via name similarity
Legitimate popular packages pass cleanly

tactics.title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents: Scan for vulnerabilities
tactics.flow_title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents
tactics.body: Real packages can still carry known holes. Checklist: Proposed deps scanned including transitives where feasible; High/critical-without-fix blocks; Existing set scanned on a schedule Add vulnerability scanning. For each proposed dependency (and its transitive dependencies where feasible), check against a vulnerability database/advisory source (an audit tool like the package manager's built-in audit, or an OSS advisory API): known CVEs, severity, and whether a fixed version exists. Blocking policy: high/critical vulnerabilities with no fix block the add; those with a fix prompt the agent to use… If stuck: The scan passed a known-vulnerable version. Verify the advisory source is current and covers this ecosystem, and that version matching is correct - a vuln check that misses known CVEs provides false assurance.
checklist: Proposed deps scanned including transitives where feasible
High/critical-without-fix blocks
Existing set scanned on a schedule

tactics.title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents: Gate review and enforce lockfile discipline
tactics.flow_title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Scanning for Agents
tactics.step_title: Gate review and enforce lockfile discipline
tactics.body: Reviewed set in, reviewed set installed - recorded. Checklist: New deps recorded with rationale and approver; Manifest and lockfile updated together and pinned; CI blocks manifest/lockfile drift Close the loop with review and lockfiles. REVIEW GATE: a NEW dependency passing automated checks still surfaces for a human decision with the evidence (why the agent wants it, existence/reputation/vuln results); approval records {package, version, rationale, approver, date} in a dependency decision log. LOCKFILE DISCIPLINE: approved additions update BOTH the manifest and the lockfile together, pinning exact… If stuck: Manifest and lockfile drifted after an approval. Make the approved-add operation update both atomically and add the CI consistency check - a reviewed manifest with an unreviewed lockfile means the install is unreviewed.
checklist: New deps recorded with rationale and approver
Manifest and lockfile updated together and pinned
CI blocks manifest/lockfile drift

tactics.title: Design the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI): Audit your current tool surface
tactics.body: You cannot design an interface you have not honestly measured. Checklist: Every tool has output-size data; Confusion cases cite real transcripts; Priority order is justified Audit my agent's current tools against ACI principles. For each tool record: typical output size in tokens, whether output is bounded, whether errors state a cause and suggested next action, whether misuse is guarded (e.g. editing a file never read), and 2-3 transcript examples where the tool confused the model. Score each tool 1-5 on model-friendliness. Research context: SWE-agent found that command simplicity,… If stuck: The audit lacks evidence. Pull five recent failed transcripts and trace each failure to the tool interaction that caused it - then rescore.
checklist: Every tool has output-size data
Confusion cases cite real transcripts
Priority order is justified

tactics.title: Design the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI): Build the windowed file viewer
tactics.body: The single highest-leverage ACI component in the research. Checklist: Window header/footer show position context; Navigation state persists across calls; 5,000-line file never dumps fully Replace raw file reads with a windowed viewer. Requirements: open_file(path, line?) shows a window of about 100 lines with line numbers, a header (path, total lines, current window range), and footer hints (lines above/below); scroll_down/scroll_up move the window; goto(line) jumps. Files smaller than the window show fully. The viewer maintains per-file position state across calls. Output is always bounded… If stuck: The model keeps re-reading from line 1. Verify position state persists between calls and that the footer explicitly tells the model how many lines remain below - models navigate on what the interface tells them.
checklist: Window header/footer show position context
Navigation state persists across calls
5,000-line file never dumps fully

tactics.title: Design the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI): Add validated edits with corrective feedback
tactics.step_title: Add validated edits with corrective feedback
tactics.body: An edit command that cannot fail loudly will fail silently. Checklist: Read-before-write is enforced; Lint failure reverts and explains; Success returns the edited window as evidence Implement ACI-grade editing. Requirements: edit(path, start_line, end_line, replacement) applies only if the file was previously opened (read-before-write guard); after applying, run a syntax/lint check appropriate to the file type; on lint failure, revert the edit and return the error with line numbers and the offending snippet so the model can correct; on success, return the new window around the edit as… If stuck: A failed edit left the file broken. Ensure validation runs on a temp copy or the edit is reverted on failure - the file on disk must never hold a state the model was told was rejected.
checklist: Read-before-write is enforced
Lint failure reverts and explains
Success returns the edited window as evidence

tactics.title: Design the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI): Constrain search and command outputs
tactics.body: Concise, ranked results are an interface decision, not a nicety. Checklist: Hit caps enforced with truncation notes; Exit codes always explicit; Head+tail preserved on big outputs Redesign search and command execution for bounded, guiding output. Search: find_text(query, path?) returns at most 20 hits as file:line plus a one-line snippet, deduplicated by file, with a 'N more hits truncated' note; find_file(pattern) returns at most 30 paths. Commands: run_command returns combined stdout/stderr truncated to a token budget with head+tail preserved and a marker showing how much was cut, plus the… If stuck: Truncation is cutting off the error at the tail. Switch to head+tail preservation (first N and last M lines) since errors and summaries cluster at the ends of output.
checklist: Hit caps enforced with truncation notes
Exit codes always explicit
Head+tail preserved on big outputs

tactics.title: Design the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI): Benchmark against the raw baseline
tactics.body: The ACI claim is empirical - test it that way. Checklist: Same tasks, model, and prompt across A/B; Turns, tokens, and success recorded; Regressions traced to specific interface gaps Prove the redesign. Take three representative tasks (find and fix a planted bug, add a small feature, answer a codebase question). Run each with (A) the old raw tool surface and (B) the new ACI, same model and system prompt. Compare: turns to completion, total tokens, wrong-file edits, and success. Record results in a small table. Where the ACI did not win, inspect the transcript and identify the interface gap… If stuck: Results are mixed with no diagnosis. For each B-loss, read the transcript and name the exact tool response that sent the model down the wrong path - then redesign that response and re-run.
checklist: Same tasks, model, and prompt across A/B
Turns, tokens, and success recorded
Regressions traced to specific interface gaps

tactics.title: Design a Memory Index Loaded Every Session: Structure the index and details
tactics.flow_title: Design a Memory Index Loaded Every Session
tactics.body: The index is a map; the details are the territory. Checklist: Index within its token cap; Every description says when to load; All detail files reachable from the index Design the two-layer memory structure. INDEX (memory/INDEX.md, hard cap ~400 tokens): a header stating its role, then one line per topic: `- topic-name: one-line description of what the detail file contains and when to load it -> memory/topics/topic-name.md`. DETAIL FILES (memory/topics/*.md): focused documents per topic (auth-system.md, deployment.md, user-preferences.md...), each starting with a 2-line abstract… If stuck: Descriptions are labels, not signals ('auth stuff'). Rewrite each as a load-trigger: the task keywords and situations that should prompt opening the file.
checklist: Index within its token cap
Every description says when to load
All detail files reachable from the index

tactics.title: Design a Memory Index Loaded Every Session: Wire loading: index always, details on demand
tactics.flow_title: Design a Memory Index Loaded Every Session
tactics.step_title: Wire loading: index always, details on demand
tactics.body: Constant context cost with reach into everything. Checklist: Index loaded with usage instructions; Relevant task triggers the right memory_read; Irrelevant task loads nothing Implement the loading mechanics. At session start: load INDEX.md into the system context under a header explaining 'this is your memory index - load topic files with memory_read when a task touches them'. Implement memory_read(topic) returning the detail file content (with a token cap and truncation note for oversized files). Add index-integrity checks at load: warn on pointers to missing files and on files not in… If stuck: The agent never calls memory_read. Add one worked example to the index header (task X -> load topic Y) and make the instruction imperative: 'Before starting work, check the index for relevant topics and load them.'
checklist: Index loaded with usage instructions
Relevant task triggers the right memory_read
Irrelevant task loads nothing

tactics.title: Design a Memory Index Loaded Every Session: Maintain the index as memory evolves
tactics.flow_title: Design a Memory Index Loaded Every Session
tactics.step_title: Maintain the index as memory evolves
tactics.body: An index that drifts from reality is worse than no index. Checklist: File+pointer operations are atomic; Session-end sweep catches drift; Over-cap merge uses access recency Implement index maintenance. Extend the memory tool so that: creating a new detail file requires an index entry in the same operation (atomic pair); updating a detail file's scope prompts a description refresh; removing a topic removes both file and pointer. Add a session-end sweep: verify index-file bijection (every pointer resolves, every file is pointed at), flag descriptions whose detail files changed… If stuck: Orphans appeared anyway. Route ALL detail-file creation through the memory tool (block direct writes to the topics directory in the write tool's path rules) so the atomic pairing cannot be bypassed.
checklist: File+pointer operations are atomic
Session-end sweep catches drift
Over-cap merge uses access recency

tactics.title: Design the Permission Approval UX: Audit the current approval moments
tactics.body: Count them, read them, feel the fatigue. Checklist: Approvals-per-task measured; Faith approvals identified honestly; Worst prompts captured verbatim Audit approvals as they exist. Instrument or review recent sessions and collect: approvals per task (average and worst case), what each prompt actually displayed, time-to-decision per approval, and any decline-then-nothing dead ends. Classify prompts by information sufficiency: could the user decide correctly from the prompt alone, or did they approve on faith? Interview or observe one real user session if… If stuck: No instrumentation exists to audit. Add approval-event logging first (prompt content, decision, latency) and run three real tasks - the redesign needs a baseline to beat.
checklist: Approvals-per-task measured
Faith approvals identified honestly
Worst prompts captured verbatim

tactics.title: Design the Permission Approval UX: Rebuild the prompt content
tactics.body: Decisions need diffs, commands, and consequences - inline. Checklist: Diffs render with hunk context; Commands show cwd and effect line; Triggering rule named on each ask Redesign the approval prompt per action type. FILE EDITS: render the unified diff (bounded to the changed hunks with context lines), the file path, and a one-line summary of intent; for new files show the full content when small, the head plus structure when large. COMMANDS: exact command string, working directory, a plain-language effect line ('installs package X globally'), and the rule that triggered the ask.… If stuck: Diffs are unreadably long. Bound to changed hunks with 3 context lines and a 'view full diff' expansion - the default view must fit a screen or it will not be read.
checklist: Diffs render with hunk context
Commands show cwd and effect line
Triggering rule named on each ask

tactics.title: Design the Permission Approval UX: Make friction proportional to risk
tactics.body: Routine should be quick; dangerous should be impossible to miss. Checklist: Routine is one-action quick; Dangerous requires deliberate confirmation; Screenshot check confirms distinctness Implement risk-tiered presentation. ROUTINE (session-tier edits, contained commands): compact prompt, single-key approve, muted styling. ELEVATED (installs, network, config changes): standard prompt, explicit approve button, distinct accent color. DANGEROUS (destructive patterns, protected-path overrides): unmissable styling per the app's danger tokens, blast-radius statement ('this deletes 34 files, not… If stuck: Everything still looks similar. The danger tier must break the visual pattern completely - different placement, size, and interaction; if a screenshot thumbnail cannot distinguish them, redesign.
checklist: Routine is one-action quick
Dangerous requires deliberate confirmation
Screenshot check confirms distinctness

tactics.title: Design the Permission Approval UX: Add scoped grants and measure the win
tactics.step_title: Add scoped grants and measure the win
tactics.body: Fewer, better questions - proven with numbers. Checklist: Scope choices on session-tier prompts; Batch approval for planned multi-edits; Before/after table shows improvement without loosened rules Finish with grants and measurement. GRANTS: every session-tier prompt offers scope choices - allow once / allow for session / allow for this directory (where sensible); choices route to the grant store; an active-grants view supports revocation. BATCHING: when the agent plans N similar actions (editing 6 files for one refactor), offer one batched approval listing all targets rather than six prompts. MEASUREMENT:… If stuck: Fatigue barely moved. Check the distribution: if one tool dominates prompts, its tier may be misclassified (session vs ask), or its actions should batch - fix classification before weakening anything.
checklist: Scope choices on session-tier prompts
Batch approval for planned multi-edits
Before/after table shows improvement without loosened rules

tactics.title: Design a Single-Loop Agent: Define the loop contract
tactics.body: Write down exactly what one turn of the loop does before coding it. Checklist: Turn sequence is explicit; Termination has 3 concrete conditions; Message shapes are documented Design the core loop for a single-agent system and write it as a contract before implementation. Specify: (1) INPUT: system prompt + message history + tool registry. (2) TURN: send to model; the model returns either final text or one or more tool calls. (3) EXECUTE: run each tool call in order, capture result or error. (4) FOLD: append tool results as tool-role messages, preserving call order and IDs. (5)… If stuck: The design jumped straight to classes and frameworks. Rewrite it as the sequence of messages exchanged in one turn - if you cannot write the transcript by hand, the design is not ready.
checklist: Turn sequence is explicit
Termination has 3 concrete conditions
Message shapes are documented

tactics.title: Design a Single-Loop Agent: Build the tool registry
tactics.body: Tools are the agent's hands - define them with strict schemas. Checklist: Each tool has schema + description + handler; Invalid calls return structured errors; Descriptions say when NOT to use the tool Implement a tool registry for the agent. Requirements: each tool has a name, a one-paragraph description written for the model (what it does, when to use it, when NOT to use it), a JSON schema for parameters, and a handler function. Include three starter tools: read_file(path), write_file(path, content), run_command(command). Validate every incoming tool call against its schema before executing; on validation… If stuck: Tool calls are being executed without validation. Add schema validation before the handler runs and return the validation error text to the model so it can retry with corrected arguments.
checklist: Each tool has schema + description + handler
Invalid calls return structured errors
Descriptions say when NOT to use the tool

tactics.title: Design a Single-Loop Agent: Implement the loop with result folding
tactics.step_title: Implement the loop with result folding
tactics.body: The loop's job is bookkeeping: order, roles, and IDs must be exact. Checklist: Demo task completes end to end; Tool results keep call order and IDs; Transcript JSONL captures every turn Implement the main loop. Requirements: maintain the full message history; on each turn send system prompt + history to the model; if the response contains tool calls, execute them sequentially and append each result as a tool message linked to its call ID; if the response is plain text, treat it as the final answer and stop; enforce max 20 turns and stop after 3 consecutive turns where every tool call failed. Log… If stuck: The model claims it edited the file but the file is unchanged. Check that write_file results are actually appended to history and that you are not silently catching handler exceptions - the model must see real results, not optimistic…
checklist: Demo task completes end to end
Tool results keep call order and IDs
Transcript JSONL captures every turn

tactics.title: Design a Single-Loop Agent: Harden termination and error paths
tactics.body: An agent that cannot stop is worse than one that cannot start. Checklist: Loop detection interrupts repeated identical calls; Max turns returns a summary; Cancellation works between turns Harden the loop against the classic failure modes. Requirements: (1) max-turn stop returns a partial-result summary, not a crash; (2) repeated identical tool calls (same tool, same args, 3x) trigger an intervention message telling the model it is looping; (3) any unhandled exception in a tool returns a structured error message to the model with the traceback summary; (4) a cancellation flag lets the caller stop the… If stuck: The agent loops on the same failing command. Implement the repeated-call detector and inject a message like 'You have tried this 3 times with the same result - change approach or report the blocker' before the next model call.
checklist: Loop detection interrupts repeated identical calls
Max turns returns a summary
Cancellation works between turns

tactics.title: Design a Single-Loop Agent: Prove it with a transcript review
tactics.step_title: Prove it with a transcript review
tactics.body: Judge the loop the way harness engineers do: by reading transcripts. Checklist: Three transcripts reviewed line by line; Failure task ends with an honest report; Any claim/evidence mismatch is explained and fixed Run the agent on three tasks of increasing difficulty (single edit, multi-file change, task that must fail due to a missing file) and review the transcripts. For each: verify tool order matches the story the model tells, verify no result was dropped, verify the failure task ends with an honest report instead of a fabricated success. Produce a short review doc listing any turn where the model's claim and the tool… If stuck: The transcript shows the model inventing results for a tool that errored. Verify error results are appended verbatim and add a system-prompt rule: never describe a tool result that is not present in the conversation.
checklist: Three transcripts reviewed line by line
Failure task ends with an honest report
Any claim/evidence mismatch is explained and fixed

tactics.title: Design Tool Schemas for Agents: Audit schemas for looseness
tactics.body: Every loose type is an invitation the model will accept. Checklist: Every parameter assessed against its real domain; Transcript misuse evidence attached; Tightening proposals concrete Audit all my tool schemas for constraint weakness. For each parameter record: current type, whether its real domain is narrower (a string that is actually one of 4 modes, a number that must be 1-100), whether it is truly required, whether its description would let a newcomer produce a valid value, and misuse evidence from transcripts (wrong shapes the model has actually sent). Rank the tools by misuse frequency.… If stuck: The audit says everything is fine but misuse continues. Pull 10 failed tool calls from transcripts and work backwards - each failure traces to a constraint the schema failed to express.
checklist: Every parameter assessed against its real domain
Transcript misuse evidence attached
Tightening proposals concrete

tactics.title: Design Tool Schemas for Agents: Tighten the schemas
tactics.body: Make illegal states unrepresentable in the call. Checklist: Enums, ranges, and patterns applied; additionalProperties false on all tools; Happy-path tests pass post-tightening Apply the tightening. Rules: strings with finite options become enums; numbers get minimum/maximum; identifiers get pattern constraints where formats exist (paths, slugs); arrays get minItems/maxItems and item types; every field gets a description with purpose + format + example; defaults documented in the description AND implemented in the handler; additionalProperties set to false everywhere. For genuinely… If stuck: A legitimate call now fails validation. Good - the schema found an undocumented usage. Decide deliberately: widen the schema with a documented reason, or fix the caller; never quietly loosen back to strings.
checklist: Enums, ranges, and patterns applied
additionalProperties false on all tools
Happy-path tests pass post-tightening

tactics.title: Design Tool Schemas for Agents: Make validation errors teach
tactics.body: The error message is the model's documentation at the moment it matters most. Checklist: Errors name field, received, and allowed; Unknown params get nearest-match hints; Misuse replay shows fixable messages Rebuild validation error responses as corrective teaching. Format: which field failed, what was received, what is allowed (for enums: list the values; for ranges: state them; for patterns: show a valid example), plus a complete corrected example call when cheap to construct. Reject unknown parameters by name ('unknown parameter: file - did you mean path?') with nearest-match suggestions. Ensure errors return to the… If stuck: The model retries with the same bad call. The error is not teaching - add the corrected-example line to the message and verify the retry uses it.
checklist: Errors name field, received, and allowed
Unknown params get nearest-match hints
Misuse replay shows fixable messages

tactics.title: Design Tool Schemas for Agents: Lock it in with a misuse suite
tactics.step_title: Lock it in with a misuse suite
tactics.body: Schemas regress silently unless tests hold the line. Checklist: 10 rejects and 5 boundary passes asserted; Error content asserted, not just status; Live misuse compared to baseline Build the permanent misuse suite. Collect at least 10 bad calls: real transcript misuses plus constructed edge cases (out-of-range numbers, invalid enum values, extra parameters, missing required fields, wrong types, oversized arrays). Assert each is rejected AND the error message contains the allowed values or a corrected hint. Add 5 boundary calls that must PASS (values exactly at limits). Wire the suite into the… If stuck: Misuse persists on one tool despite tight schemas. Look at its description and name - if the tool's purpose is ambiguous, the model picks it wrongly regardless of schema; fix the description or split the tool.
checklist: 10 rejects and 5 boundary passes asserted
Error content asserted, not just status
Live misuse compared to baseline

tactics.title: DeSlop Audit: Score the slop
tactics.body: Name the problem precisely across four dimensions. Checklist: All four dimensions scored with evidence; Findings include locations; Function-slop is separately identified Run a brutal slop audit on this app and score each dimension 1-10 with evidence. DESIGN: default fonts, generic gradients, emoji-as-icons, identical card grids, no visual identity. COPY: lorem ipsum, robotic microcopy, 'Welcome to your dashboard' filler, inconsistent tone. FUNCTION: dead buttons, fake success states, data that resets, missing states. DETAILS: default favicon/title, console errors, no focus states,… If stuck: The audit is soft and vague. Re-run it hostile: click everything, read every string, check the favicon and console - list findings someone could act on.
checklist: All four dimensions scored with evidence
Findings include locations
Function-slop is separately identified

tactics.title: DeSlop Audit: Fix function-slop first
tactics.body: A beautiful dead app is still dead - real function precedes polish. Checklist: Every dead/fake control now works; Persistence verified by refresh; States exist for async operations Fix every FUNCTION finding from the audit. Requirements: every dead button gets its real handler; every fake success gets the real operation with persistence; every missing loading/error/empty state is added; forms validate and actually submit; data survives refresh. Verify each fix with the action + refresh test and update the audit table with evidence. Do not touch visuals yet. If stuck: Function fixes were claimed without the refresh test. Re-verify each fixed item by performing it and refreshing; reopen anything that does not stick.
checklist: Every dead/fake control now works
Persistence verified by refresh
States exist for async operations

tactics.title: DeSlop Audit: Fix design-slop
tactics.body: Replace the default-AI look with an intentional identity. Checklist: Fonts and colors changed at token level; Zero emoji-icons remain; Hover and focus states are designed Fix every DESIGN finding. Requirements: define and apply a real font pairing and a token-level color system with ONE deliberate accent (kill purple-gradient defaults); replace all emoji-icons with a consistent icon set; differentiate the card-grid sameness with intentional hierarchy (featured vs standard, varied density); add designed hover/focus/active states; apply consistent spacing rhythm. The app should be… If stuck: The restyle swapped one generic look for another. Define the identity first (mood, fonts, accent) then apply it - and verify headings actually render the new font.
checklist: Fonts and colors changed at token level
Zero emoji-icons remain
Hover and focus states are designed

tactics.title: DeSlop Audit: Fix copy-slop
tactics.body: Every string should sound like this product, written by a person. Checklist: No lorem ipsum or filler remains; Errors say what to do next; Titles/meta are set per page Fix every COPY finding. Requirements: rewrite all placeholder and filler text into product-specific copy; give microcopy (buttons, empty states, errors, tooltips) a consistent voice; error messages must say what happened and what to do; empty states must orient and invite action; page titles and meta descriptions set properly per page. Produce a before/after list of the worst 10 strings as proof. If stuck: Copy is still template-speak. Rewrite the worst strings to mention this product's actual objects and actions, and read each aloud to test the voice.
checklist: No lorem ipsum or filler remains
Errors say what to do next
Titles/meta are set per page

tactics.title: DeSlop Audit: Polish the details and re-score
tactics.body: The last 5% - details separate finished from generated. Checklist: Console is clean on main paths; Favicon and titles are real; Before/after scores are reported Fix every DETAILS finding and close the audit. Requirements: real favicon and page titles; zero console errors on the main paths; visible focus states for keyboard users; responsive check at 375px on core pages; scroll behavior, image alt text, and selection states sane; loading transitions smooth. Then re-run the full four-dimension audit, produce the before/after scores, and list anything remaining as… If stuck: Details were skipped as unimportant. Fix the favicon, titles, console errors, and focus states now - judges and users notice these first.
checklist: Console is clean on main paths
Favicon and titles are real
Before/after scores are reported

tactics.title: Add Direct Messaging Feature: Design Message & Conversation Data Model
tactics.body: Create database structures to store chats and individual messages Checklist: Do the new models appear in schema.prisma?; Does `prisma migrate dev` complete without errors?; Are the tables present in the database with correct columns and indexes? Write Prisma schema definitions for two new models: Conversation (id UUID primary key, participantAId UUID, participantBId UUID, createdAt timestamp, updatedAt timestamp) and Message (id UUID primary key, conversationId UUID foreign key, senderId UUID foreign key, content String, sentAt timestamp, read Boolean default false). Add necessary indexes for fast lookup (e.g., participant pair, conversationId). Provide… If stuck: The schema definitions were incomplete or contained placeholder comments. Regenerate the full Conversation and Message model blocks with all required fields, indexes, and foreign keys, and include a runnable `prisma migrate dev
checklist: Do the new models appear in schema.prisma?
Does `prisma migrate dev` complete without errors?
Are the tables present in the database with correct columns and indexes?

tactics.title: Add Direct Messaging Feature: Create API Endpoints for Messaging
tactics.body: Expose HTTP routes to send a message and fetch a conversation's messages Checklist: Can you POST a new message and receive a 201 response with the message JSON?; Does GET /api/conversations/:id/messages return a paginated list of real messages?; Do unauthorized users receive a 403 error? Implement two Express routes: 1. POST /api/messages – body: {conversationId, content}. Validate that `req.userId` matches the conversation participants, create a Message record with senderId = req.userId, sentAt = now, read = false, and update the Conversation's updatedAt. Return the created Message JSON. 2. GET /api/conversations/:id/messages – query params: optional `limit` and `offset`. Validate that… If stuck: The generated router is missing validation or contains placeholder responses. Rewrite the router ensuring real auth checks, proper Prisma create/find calls, and full error handling as specified
checklist: Can you POST a new message and receive a 201 response with the message JSON?
Does GET /api/conversations/:id/messages return a paginated list of real messages?
Do unauthorized users receive a 403 error?

tactics.title: Add Direct Messaging Feature: Persist Messages and Update Read Status
tactics.step_title: Persist Messages and Update Read Status
tactics.body: Ensure messages are saved and can be marked as read Checklist: Does the PATCH call return the updated message with read=true?; Is the readAt timestamp stored in the database?; Do unauthorized attempts return 403? Create a PATCH /api/messages/:id/read route that: - Verifies `req.userId` is either the sender or receiver of the message. - Updates the specific Message record setting `read = true` and `readAt = now` (add readAt column if not present, include migration instructions). - Returns the updated Message. - Handles errors: 403 if not participant, 404 if message not found. Provide any additional Prisma migration needed… If stuck: The route lacks proper participant verification or the migration was omitted. Regenerate the PATCH endpoint with real auth logic and provide the missing Prisma migration to add `readAt`.
checklist: Does the PATCH call return the updated message with read=true?
Is the readAt timestamp stored in the database?
Do unauthorized attempts return 403?

tactics.title: Add Direct Messaging Feature: Build Chat UI Component
tactics.body: Create a visible chat window that lists messages and allows sending new ones Checklist: Does the component display existing messages from the server?; Can a user type and send a new message that appears instantly?; Are messages styled as chat bubbles with sender distinction? Implement a React component `ChatBox` that accepts a `conversationId` prop. Inside, fetch messages from GET /api/conversations/:id/messages on mount (useEffect) and display them in a scrollable list showing sender name, content, timestamp, and read indicator. Provide an input field and Send button; on click, POST to /api/messages with the content, then append the new message to the list without reloading. Use the… If stuck: The component contains dummy data or missing fetch logic. Re‑write ChatBox to perform real API calls, render actual messages, and handle sending with proper state updates.
checklist: Does the component display existing messages from the server?
Can a user type and send a new message that appears instantly?
Are messages styled as chat bubbles with sender distinction?

tactics.title: Add Direct Messaging Feature: Integrate Chat UI into App Navigation
tactics.step_title: Integrate Chat UI into App Navigation
tactics.body: Make the chat reachable from a user's profile or contacts list Checklist: Does the 'Message' button open a URL like /chat/<uuid>?; Is a Conversation created if none existed?; Does the ChatPage render ChatBox with messages for that conversation? 1. In the router configuration, add a new route `<Route path="/chat/:conversationId" element={<ChatPage/>} />`. 2. Create `ChatPage.tsx` that extracts `conversationId` from `useParams()`, renders the `ChatBox` with that ID. 3. On `UserProfile` (or contacts list), add a button that calls an API to either fetch an existing Conversation between the logged‑in user and the profile user or creates one if none exists,… If stuck: The navigation uses a hard‑coded ID or skips the conversation creation step. Rewrite the button handler to call the real backend endpoint, handle the response, and navigate using the returned conversationId.
checklist: Does the 'Message' button open a URL like /chat/<uuid>?
Is a Conversation created if none existed?
Does the ChatPage render ChatBox with messages for that conversation?

tactics.title: Add Direct Messaging Feature: Add Real‑Time Updates (Polling)
tactics.body: Refresh the chat view when new messages arrive without manual reload Checklist: Does the message list update when the other user sends a message?; Is there no memory leak (interval cleared on unmount)?; Are duplicate messages avoided after successive polls? Modify `ChatBox` to start a `setInterval` on mount that calls the GET messages endpoint every 5 seconds, updating the message list state if there are new messages (compare last message timestamp). Clean up the interval on unmount. Ensure duplicate messages are not added. Include a loading indicator while fetching. No placeholder timers; the interval must be real. If stuck: The polling logic is missing or duplicates messages. Re‑implement the interval with proper fetch, deduplication, and cleanup as specified.
checklist: Does the message list update when the other user sends a message?
Is there no memory leak (interval cleared on unmount)?
Are duplicate messages avoided after successive polls?

tactics.title: Add Direct Messaging Feature: End‑to‑End Verification
tactics.body: Confirm the full chat flow works between two real users Checklist: Can User A send a message that User B receives without reload?; Is the full conversation stored in the database after reload?; Does the read flag update correctly when marked read?; Does polling keep both sides in sync? Perform the following manual test steps: 1. Log in as User A, go to User B's profile, click 'Message', start a conversation. 2. Send a message "Hello". Verify it appears in the UI and is stored in the DB (query with Prisma). 3. In a second browser, log in as User B, open the same conversation (via the chat URL). Verify the message appears automatically (polling). 4. Send a reply "Hi" from User B. Confirm it appears… If stuck: If any test step fails, identify the component (API, DB, UI) that caused the issue and regenerate the specific step's code with concrete fixes.
checklist: Can User A send a message that User B receives without reload?
Is the full conversation stored in the database after reload?
Does the read flag update correctly when marked read?
Does polling keep both sides in sync?

tactics.title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop: Inventory soft rules and classify enforcement needs
tactics.flow_title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop
tactics.step_title: Inventory soft rules and classify enforcement needs
tactics.body: Know which promises are currently backed by nothing. Checklist: Every prompt rule captured with worst case; Each rule classed guidance/confirm/block; Gaps between class and existing enforcement listed Extract every behavioral rule from your system and tool prompts into a list. For each, record: what it protects (data loss, money, credentials, repo history, user trust), the worst case if the model ignores it, and how often transcripts show it violated. Classify: GUIDANCE (style, tool preference - prompt-only is fine, though code may add suggestions), CONFIRM (destructive-but-legitimate operations - needs an ask… If stuck: The matrix says most rules are guidance. Re-test each against: 'if the model violated this once at the worst moment, is the damage acceptable and reversible?' If not, it is confirm or block - optimism here is precisely the failure the…
checklist: Every prompt rule captured with worst case
Each rule classed guidance/confirm/block
Gaps between class and existing enforcement listed

tactics.title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop: Implement checks independent of the prompt
tactics.flow_title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop
tactics.step_title: Implement checks independent of the prompt
tactics.body: The code layer must stand alone. Checklist: Checks parse the real action, not conversation text; Each returns allow/ask/deny with a reason; Full suite passes with safety prompts removed For each confirm/block rule, implement a deterministic check in the tool-execution path that inspects the actual action (parsed command, target path, flags, destination) - never the conversation text. Examples: destructive git detection (force-push, hard reset, branch deletion) by parsing the command; protected-path validation that refuses removal of system or credential paths regardless of any permission rule;… If stuck: A check works only when the prompt primes the model to phrase commands a certain way. That is coupling - rewrite the check to parse what will actually execute (post-expansion, post-quoting), because attackers and confused models will not…
checklist: Checks parse the real action, not conversation text
Each returns allow/ask/deny with a reason
Full suite passes with safety prompts removed

tactics.title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop: Wire the escalation path
tactics.flow_title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop
tactics.body: Ask preserves the user's authority; deny is reserved for certainty. Checklist: Ask shows parsed action, effect, and reason; Deny explains and offers the alternative; All escalations logged with the triggering rule Route check outcomes through a consistent escalation: ALLOW proceeds silently; ASK pauses the action and presents the user a specific confirmation ('This will force-push to main and may overwrite remote history. Proceed?') with the parsed action visible, not the raw model output; DENY blocks with an explanation and suggests the safe alternative. Design the ask UX so confirmations are informed: show the target, the… If stuck: Users click through asks blindly. Reduce ask volume: tighten checks so routine safe operations stop triggering (false positives train click-through), and make the confirmation text name the specific consequence rather than generic 'are…
checklist: Ask shows parsed action, effect, and reason
Deny explains and offers the alternative
All escalations logged with the triggering rule

tactics.title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop: Analyze the four failure combinations
tactics.flow_title: Pair Every Prompt Rule with a Code Backstop
tactics.body: Know exactly where the architecture's edges are. Checklist: All four combinations have concrete test cases; A both-fail case exists and its mitigation is stated; Code-wins-on-conflict is asserted in tests Document and test the four combinations. 1) Prompt fails, code catches: model ignores guidance, check fires - verify with transcripts that the ask/deny actually triggered. 2) Prompt works, code idle: the common good case - confirm no needless friction was added. 3) Both fail: construct a red-team case the code misses (novel obfuscation, unicode homoglyphs, a tool interaction you did not model) - this defines your… If stuck: You cannot construct a both-fail case. Try harder: encoding tricks, parser/shell disagreements, or chained innocuous actions with a harmful composite effect - if you genuinely cannot, your red-team imagination is the gap; borrow an attack…
checklist: All four combinations have concrete test cases
A both-fail case exists and its mitigation is stated
Code-wins-on-conflict is asserted in tests

tactics.title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment: Identify conditional blocks
tactics.flow_title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment
tactics.body: Find what only sometimes belongs in the prompt. Checklist: Every section has an explicit condition; Value sources identified for derived blocks; Token cost recorded per block List every section of your current tool/system prompt and mark its activation condition: ALWAYS (core tool description), FEATURE-GATED (sandbox instructions only if sandboxing is enabled; background-task instructions only if background execution is allowed; git safety protocol only in repos), ENVIRONMENT-DERIVED (allowed paths, network hosts, resource limits - values that come from live config), and AUDIENCE… If stuck: Everything got marked ALWAYS. Challenge each block: would this text be wrong or wasted in any deployment (sandbox off, no git repo, feature flag off)? If yes, it is conditional - static-by-default is how prompts rot.
checklist: Every section has an explicit condition
Value sources identified for derived blocks
Token cost recorded per block

tactics.title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment: Build the prompt generator
tactics.flow_title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment
tactics.body: Prompts become code with inputs, not strings. Checklist: Blocks read conditions from real flags/config; Values sourced from the enforcing code's config; Byte-determinism verified for fixed inputs Implement a generator function that takes the environment (feature flags, config objects, user class) and returns the assembled prompt. Structure: an ordered list of block builders, each returning either its text or nothing based on its condition; join the included blocks. Pull live values (allowed paths, hosts) directly from the same config objects the ENFORCEMENT code reads - never a hand-copied list - so prompt… If stuck: Two runs with the same environment produced different bytes. Hunt the nondeterminism: unordered sets or dict iteration, timestamps, or environment reads that changed - cache-friendliness and testability both require byte stability.
checklist: Blocks read conditions from real flags/config
Values sourced from the enforcing code's config
Byte-determinism verified for fixed inputs

tactics.title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment: Dedupe and budget every block
tactics.flow_title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment
tactics.body: Every injected token must earn its place. Checklist: Dedup pass on all injected lists; Token counts logged per block; Budget alert wired and behavior re-verified after cuts Add hygiene passes to the generator: dedupe list values before injection (configs merged from multiple sources often repeat entries - deduping alone can save 150-200 tokens per request), collapse redundant whitespace, and cap list lengths with a 'plus N more' summary where full enumeration adds nothing. Instrument the generator to log token counts total and per block on every assembly. Set a budget per tool prompt… If stuck: Cutting tokens broke a behavior. Restore the specific block and cut elsewhere - the budget is a forcing function for prioritization, not a mandate to delete load-bearing instructions; the logs tell you exactly which block bought which…
checklist: Dedup pass on all injected lists
Token counts logged per block
Budget alert wired and behavior re-verified after cuts

tactics.title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment: Verify against live environments
tactics.flow_title: Assemble Tool Prompts Dynamically per Environment
tactics.body: The generator must be right in every configuration, not just the default. Checklist: All configurations tested for false capability claims; Prompt values programmatically compared to enforcement values; Snapshot tests catch unintended prompt diffs Test the assembled prompt across your real configuration matrix: sandbox on/off, background tasks enabled/disabled, inside/outside a git repo, each user class. For each configuration assert: no block describes a disabled feature, injected values equal the enforcing config's values (compare programmatically, not by eye), and the model behaves correctly on a smoke task. tactics.title: Episodic, Semantic, and Procedural Stores: Define the three schemas
tactics.body: Each memory kind answers a different question - schema follows. Checklist: Schemas capture type-distinct fields; Procedures include verification and failure modes; The split example shows one input becoming multiple typed entries Define schemas for the three stores. EPISODIC (what happened): {session_id, date, task, outcome, notable_events[], artifacts_touched[]} - compact narrative records of sessions and incidents. SEMANTIC (what is true): {statement, topic, provenance, confidence, source_episodes[]} - atomic declarative facts. PROCEDURAL (how to do): {goal, preconditions[], steps[], verification, failure_modes[], last_validated,… If stuck: The examples are interchangeable across stores. Sharpen with the question test: episodes answer 'what happened?', facts answer 'what is true?', procedures answer 'how do I?' - rewrite each example until it answers only its own question.
checklist: Schemas capture type-distinct fields
Procedures include verification and failure modes

tactics.title: Episodic, Semantic, and Procedural Stores: Build classification and routing
tactics.body: The sorting hat for memories. Checklist: Question-test definitions drive classification; Spanning content splits with links; Schema validation bounces incomplete entries Implement the write-time classifier. Given a candidate memory, classify into episodic/semantic/procedural (a compact LLM classification prompt with the three question-test definitions and few-shot examples works well); content spanning types is split into multiple typed entries with cross-links; each entry is then validated against its store's schema (procedures missing verification are bounced back for… If stuck: Classification wobbles on spanning cases. Add the explicit rule to the prompt: 'if the content contains both an event and a durable takeaway, emit separate entries' with one worked example, and re-test.

Spanning content splits with links
Schema validation bounces incomplete entries

tactics.title: Episodic, Semantic, and Procedural Stores: Implement type-appropriate recall
tactics.body: Ask each store the question it exists to answer. Checklist: Each store has fit-for-purpose query mechanics; Query intent routing works on the canonical trio; Procedures render as actionable steps Build recall per store. EPISODIC: query by time range, task keyword, or artifact ('what happened last time we touched the payment code?') - results ordered by recency. SEMANTIC: query by topic with the hybrid recall stack - results are statements with confidence. PROCEDURAL: query by goal ('deploy to staging') - return the single best procedure, preferring recently-validated ones, rendered as its steps. Then build… If stuck: 'How do I deploy' returns an old episode. Fix the intent classifier's few-shots ('how do I' maps to procedural) and ensure the procedural store actually contains a deploy recipe - absence should return 'no procedure recorded', never a…
checklist: Each store has fit-for-purpose query mechanics
Query intent routing works on the canonical trio
Procedures render as actionable steps

tactics.title: Episodic, Semantic, and Procedural Stores: Wire lifecycles and the failure-feedback loop
tactics.step_title: Wire lifecycles and the failure-feedback loop
tactics.body: The payoff link: episodes correcting procedures. Checklist: Episode compression preserves links; Procedure failure flag works; Corrected procedure cites its source episode Implement per-store lifecycles and the feedback loop. Lifecycles: episodes compress after 30 days (keep task, outcome, links; drop detail) and archive after 90; facts follow confirmation/decay rules; procedures gain last_validated on observed success. Feedback loop: when a session episode records a procedure failing, flag that procedure - next use requires caution, and a diagnosed cause updates its steps or… If stuck: The failed procedure kept its old form. Check the episode schema captures which procedure was in use (procedure_id in notable_events) - without that link the feedback loop has nothing to trigger on.

Procedure failure flag works
