tactics.title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop: Build the error taxonomy
tactics.flow_title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop
tactics.body: Recovery starts with classification - each class gets a different answer. Checklist: Every tool's failures classified; Non-idempotent operations flagged; Each class mapped to a recovery strategy Create an error taxonomy for my agent's tools. Classify every known failure into: TRANSIENT (timeouts, rate limits, flaky network - safe to auto-retry), CORRECTIVE (invalid arguments, file not found, lint failure - the model must adjust and retry), FATAL (permission denied at the harness level, missing credentials, unrecoverable environment issues - escalate to the user). For each tool, list its known failure modes… If stuck: Everything is classified transient. Re-check: only failures that can succeed on unchanged retry are transient - a 400 with the same arguments will fail forever and belongs in corrective.
checklist: Every tool's failures classified
Non-idempotent operations flagged
Each class mapped to a recovery strategy

tactics.title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop: Implement retries and corrective feedback
tactics.flow_title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop
tactics.body: Machines handle transient noise; models handle their own mistakes. Checklist: Backoff with jitter implemented; Retries logged without consuming turns; Corrective errors include cause + next step Implement the first two recovery layers. Layer 1 (harness retries): wrap tool execution so TRANSIENT failures retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff plus jitter; retries are logged but do not consume model turns; non-idempotent operations verify state before retrying. Layer 2 (corrective feedback): CORRECTIVE failures return a structured error message to the model: what failed, the specific cause, and a… If stuck: The model keeps making the same bad call. Improve the corrective message: include the exact invalid field and a concrete example of a valid call - vague errors produce vague corrections.
checklist: Backoff with jitter implemented
Retries logged without consuming turns
Corrective errors include cause + next step

tactics.title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop: Add the loop breaker
tactics.flow_title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop
tactics.body: The signature failure of autonomous agents is trying the same thing forever. Checklist: Near-identical detection tolerates trivial arg changes; Interrupt message names the repeated action and error; Second offense blocks execution Implement loop detection. Track a rolling window of recent tool calls; if 3 near-identical calls (same tool, same or trivially varied arguments) all failed, interrupt before the next model call with a strategy-change message: 'You have attempted X three times with the same failure: [error]. Do not repeat it. Either take a different approach or report the blocker.' If the model attempts the same call again after the… If stuck: The model dodges detection by tweaking whitespace in arguments. Normalize arguments before comparison (trim, collapse whitespace, sort keys) so trivial variations still count as identical.
checklist: Near-identical detection tolerates trivial arg changes
Interrupt message names the repeated action and error
Second offense blocks execution

tactics.title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop: Build honest escalation and test the full ladder
tactics.flow_title: Error Recovery and Retry Policy for the Agent Loop
tactics.step_title: Build honest escalation and test the full ladder
tactics.body: Ending well matters as much as running well. Checklist: Escalation report covers goal/done/failed/tried; Run state is 'escalated', not 'completed'; All four layers visible in one transcript Implement FATAL escalation and verify the whole ladder. Escalation produces a structured report: the goal, what was completed, what failed with final errors, what was attempted (including retry and loop-breaker history), and a recommended next action for the human. The run ends in a distinct 'escalated' state, never a fake success. Then run the full ladder test: a task that hits a transient failure (auto-recovers),… If stuck: The final report claims success on failed items. Generate the done/failed lists from harness records (tool results, todo state) rather than asking the model to summarize its own performance.
checklist: Escalation report covers goal/done/failed/tried
Run state is 'escalated', not 'completed'
All four layers visible in one transcript

tactics.title: Evals for Your Harness: Design the task set
tactics.body: Representative, tiered, and partially held out. Checklist: Tasks mined from real usage; Success criteria machine-checkable where possible; Holdout set marked and respected Build the eval task set from real usage. Mine transcripts/issues for 15-25 tasks across the classes that matter: multi-step builds, bug fixes with verification, research/navigation questions, permission-sensitive operations, summarizations, and refusal-appropriate requests. Tier by difficulty (smoke: must always pass; standard: the working band; stretch: currently unreliable). For each task write: the exact… If stuck: Tasks are toy-sized. Take three real sessions from history and convert them into fixtures verbatim - real mess (ambiguity, partial context) is exactly what the suite must contain.
checklist: Tasks mined from real usage
Success criteria machine-checkable where possible
Holdout set marked and respected

tactics.title: Evals for Your Harness: Implement graders
tactics.body: Automate what can be checked; rubric what must be judged. Checklist: Machine checks cover the checkable; Judge calibrated against human grades; Every grade carries evidence Build the grading layer. AUTOMATIC: per task, run the machine checks (test suite passes, endpoint responds, output validates against schema, forbidden actions absent from the decision log) - these produce hard pass/fail plus sub-scores. RUBRIC (for quality dimensions: plan sensibility, summary fidelity, refusal quality): write 3-5 criterion rubrics with anchored scores (what a 2 vs 4 looks like), graded by an LLM… If stuck: Judge grades disagree with humans. Tighten rubric anchors with concrete examples from the calibration set and re-measure agreement - do not ship a judge below the agreement bar you set.
checklist: Machine checks cover the checkable
Judge calibrated against human grades
Every grade carries evidence

tactics.title: Evals for Your Harness: Run honestly: variance and the results store
tactics.step_title: Run honestly: variance and the results store
tactics.body: One run is an anecdote; the distribution is the datum. Checklist: N runs per task with spread reported; Deltas flagged against noise bands; Baseline shows a discriminating suite Build the runner and store. RUNNER: one command executes the suite (or a tier) against the current harness; each task runs N times (default 3; smoke tier can be 1); results capture scores, decisions, durations, and costs per run. STORE: results keyed by harness version + timestamp; the report shows per-task mean and spread, per-tier aggregates, and deltas versus the previous version with variance-aware flagging (a… If stuck: Everything passes at 100%. The suite is too easy - promote harder real tasks into standard tier until the pass band sits where changes can move it in both directions.
checklist: N runs per task with spread reported
Deltas flagged against noise bands
Baseline shows a discriminating suite

tactics.title: Evals for Your Harness: Gate changes and close the loop
tactics.step_title: Gate changes and close the loop
tactics.body: The suite earns its cost when it starts saying no. Checklist: Smoke tier in CI, deltas in PRs; Holdout runs on a schedule; Sabotage produced clear, diagnosable drops Operationalize gating. Process: every harness-artifact PR runs the smoke tier automatically (CI) and standard tier on demand; the PR description includes the eval delta table; regressions beyond the noise band require justification or fixes before merge; the holdout set runs weekly, not per-change, to detect overfitting to the tuned set. Validate the whole system with a sabotage test: deliberately degrade the… If stuck: The sabotage barely moved scores. The suite is not measuring that capability - add tasks that specifically require the degraded component (verification-dependent fixes for a gutted verify step) and re-test.
checklist: Smoke tier in CI, deltas in PRs
Holdout runs on a schedule
Sabotage produced clear, diagnosable drops

tactics.title: Evidence Checklist: Inventory every claim
tactics.body: Collect what the product says about itself - everywhere. Checklist: All copy sources were scraped for claims; Each claim is phrased testably; Vague claims are flagged Inventory every claim this product makes. Sources: the landing page, feature lists, README, submission/marketing copy, and UI microcopy. Extract each claim as a testable statement (e.g. 'users can export to CSV', 'data syncs across devices', 'works on mobile'). Flag vague claims ('fast', 'secure', 'seamless') for definition - each must be rewritten as something checkable or marked for removal. Produce the numbered… If stuck: Claims are still vague. Rewrite each flagged one as a measurable statement ('loads in under 2s on 4G', 'passwords hashed with bcrypt') or queue it for deletion.
checklist: All copy sources were scraped for claims
Each claim is phrased testably
Vague claims are flagged

tactics.title: Evidence Checklist: Define verification procedures
tactics.body: Each claim needs a repeatable test a stranger could run. Checklist: Procedures start from a defined state; Pass conditions are observable; Special setups are noted For every claim, write the verification procedure: the exact steps (from a fresh state), what to observe, and the pass condition. Procedures must be reproducible by someone who has never seen the app - include starting state, test data, and where to look. Mark which claims need special setups (second account, mobile viewport, network throttling). If stuck: Procedures assume insider knowledge. Rewrite them so a stranger with the URL could execute each: exact clicks, exact inputs, exact expected observation.
checklist: Procedures start from a defined state
Pass conditions are observable
Special setups are noted

tactics.title: Evidence Checklist: Execute and collect evidence
tactics.body: Run every procedure and record what actually happened. Checklist: Every procedure was executed; Function evidence shows actions and data, not just UI; PARTIAL results explain the gap Execute every verification procedure now. For each claim record: the result (VERIFIED/FAILED/PARTIAL), what was observed (specific - the record created, the state after refresh, the error shown), and the evidence artifact (what a screenshot/recording would show - describe the exact moment worth capturing). Function claims require action evidence (before/after data), not interface screenshots. No claim gets VERIFIED… If stuck: Claims were verified by looking at the UI. Re-execute with actions: perform the operation, refresh, and record the persisted result as the evidence.
checklist: Every procedure was executed
Function evidence shows actions and data, not just UI
PARTIAL results explain the gap

tactics.title: Evidence Checklist: Fix or reword failures
tactics.body: Reality and copy must match - change one of them. Checklist: Each failure has an explicit resolution; Reworded claims updated everywhere they appear; Fixed claims were re-executed Resolve every FAILED and PARTIAL claim: either fix the product so the claim verifies (then re-run the procedure), or rewrite the claim honestly (downgrade 'real-time' to 'updates on refresh', remove what cannot be delivered). Update all copy sources where reworded claims live. Deliver the change list: claim -> action taken -> final status. If stuck: Failed claims still live in the marketing copy. Update every source (landing, README, submission) to the honest version now - mismatch is worse than modesty.
checklist: Each failure has an explicit resolution
Reworded claims updated everywhere they appear
Fixed claims were re-executed

tactics.title: Evidence Checklist: Assemble the evidence pack
tactics.body: Package the proof so anyone can audit it. Checklist: All claims appear with final statuses; A stranger could re-verify from the pack; Limitations are stated Assemble the final evidence pack document: the claim list with final statuses; per-claim procedure and observed evidence; the environment tested (browser, viewport, date); known limitations stated plainly; and a 5-minute re-verification script - the ordered subset of procedures a reviewer should run to spot-check the pack. Keep it honest, specific, and reproducible. If stuck: The pack is a feature list without procedures. Attach the test steps and observed results per claim - evidence means someone else can check.
checklist: All claims appear with final statuses
A stranger could re-verify from the pack
Limitations are stated

tactics.title: File Upload System: Define upload requirements
tactics.body: Decide file types, limits, and storage before writing upload code. Checklist: Allowed types and max size are set; Storage location is decided; File record fields include owner and unique stored name Define the file upload spec. Specify: allowed file types (e.g. jpg/png/pdf) and max size; where files are stored for this MVP (server uploads directory, database, or object storage) and the tradeoff; the file record model (id, owner, filename, storedPath/url, mimetype, size, uploadedAt); unique storage naming to prevent collisions; and which users can see/delete which files. If stuck: The spec has no storage decision or owner linkage. Choose the storage mechanism now and add ownerId plus unique stored filenames to the model.
checklist: Allowed types and max size are set
Storage location is decided
File record fields include owner and unique stored name

tactics.title: File Upload System: Build the upload UI
tactics.body: A proper upload surface: picker, drag-drop, validation, and progress. Checklist: Wrong type is rejected before upload with a message; Oversized file is rejected with the limit shown; Progress reflects the actual upload request Build the upload UI. Requirements: file picker button plus drag-and-drop zone; client-side validation of type and size with inline error messages before upload; upload progress indicator per file; multiple file selection support; a clear success state per file and a retry option on failure. Do not fake completion - progress must reflect the real request. If stuck: Progress is fake or validation is missing. Wire progress to the real upload events and validate type/size before sending, with visible errors.
checklist: Wrong type is rejected before upload with a message
Oversized file is rejected with the limit shown
Progress reflects the actual upload request

tactics.title: File Upload System: Implement backend storage
tactics.body: The server must receive, validate, store, and record the file for real. Checklist: Server rejects wrong type/size independently of the client; Same-name uploads coexist; The returned URL serves the actual file Implement the backend upload endpoint. Requirements: accept multipart uploads; re-validate type and size server-side (reject with 400 and a clear message); store the file with a unique generated name; create the file record with owner id and metadata; return the record including a URL/endpoint to retrieve the file; ensure retrieval actually serves the stored bytes. Uploading two files with the same original name… If stuck: Files are not really stored or collide by name. Save bytes under a generated unique name, create the database record, and serve files through a working retrieval route.
checklist: Server rejects wrong type/size independently of the client
Same-name uploads coexist
The returned URL serves the actual file

tactics.title: File Upload System: List and display uploaded files
tactics.body: Users must see their files after refresh - the proof uploads are real. Checklist: Files persist across refresh; Images render as real thumbnails; Another account does not see my files Implement the files list. Requirements: fetch the logged-in user's file records from the backend; render image thumbnails for images and type icons for other files; show filename, size, and upload date; clicking opens/downloads the real file; loading skeletons, an empty state for no files, and an error state; the list must be identical after a full page refresh. If stuck: The list shows local blobs that vanish on refresh. Render from backend records and serve previews from the stored files, filtered by owner.
checklist: Files persist across refresh
Images render as real thumbnails
Another account does not see my files

tactics.title: File Upload System: Add delete with confirmation
tactics.body: Deletion must remove both the record and the stored file. Checklist: Deleted file is gone after refresh; Its URL no longer serves content; Another user cannot delete my file Implement file deletion. Requirements: delete button per file with a confirmation dialog; the backend verifies the requester owns the file, deletes the stored bytes and the record; the UI removes the item and shows a success toast; failures show visible errors; a deleted file's URL stops working. Only owners can delete their files. If stuck: Delete only hides the item. Implement the backend deletion of both bytes and record with an ownership check, and refetch the list.

Its URL no longer serves content
Another user cannot delete my file

tactics.title: File Upload System: Upload QA pass
tactics.body: Verify the full upload lifecycle including hostile inputs. Checklist: Server-side rejection tested directly; Persistence verified via refresh; Ownership isolation verified; All failures fixed Run upload QA and report PASS/FAIL with evidence: upload valid image and PDF; reject .exe and oversized file (client AND direct-to-server); refresh shows persisted list; two same-name files coexist; delete removes file and kills its URL; second account isolation; mobile layout for the upload zone. Fix all failures and re-run. If stuck: QA skipped server-side validation or persistence checks. Re-test by hitting the endpoint directly with bad files and refreshing after every operation; fix what fails.
checklist: Server-side rejection tested directly
Persistence verified via refresh
Ownership isolation verified
All failures fixed

tactics.title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work: Run a brutal functional audit
tactics.flow_title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work
tactics.body: Get the honest map: what works, what is fake, what is broken. Checklist: Every feature was action-tested, not eyeballed; Persistence checked with refreshes; The table covers all screens and modals Audit this app feature by feature with zero optimism. For every feature/screen: perform its primary action for real, then refresh and check persistence. Classify each as WORKS (action real + persists), FAKE (UI responds but nothing real happens), or BROKEN (errors/dead). Produce the table: feature -> action tested -> observed result -> classification. Do not skip auth, forms, filters, or buttons in modals. If stuck: The audit trusted appearances. Redo it by executing each feature's primary action and refreshing; reclassify anything that does not persist or errors.
checklist: Every feature was action-tested, not eyeballed
Persistence checked with refreshes
The table covers all screens and modals

tactics.title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work: Prioritize the fix order
tactics.flow_title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work
tactics.body: Fix what matters most first - the app's core promise. Checklist: Core value action is ranked first; Each item has a concrete fix plan; Cosmetic issues are ranked last From the audit, produce a fix order. Rank FAKE and BROKEN items by: (1) is it the app's core value action, (2) does it block other features, (3) how visible is it to a new user. Output a numbered fix queue with a one-line fix plan per item (what real implementation is needed). Core value actions come first, cosmetics last. If stuck: The queue starts with cosmetics. Reorder by user impact: the app's central action first, then blockers, then the rest.
checklist: Core value action is ranked first
Each item has a concrete fix plan
Cosmetic issues are ranked last

tactics.title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work: Fix the core value action
tactics.flow_title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work
tactics.body: Make the single most important feature real, end to end. Checklist: The core action performs its real operation; Result survives refresh; Errors are visible on failure Implement fix #1 - the core value action - completely. Requirements: the real operation (backend endpoint, database write/read, state update) not a simulation; loading and error states; persistence proven by refresh; edge case handling for empty/invalid input. Show exactly what changed and demonstrate the working result with evidence. If stuck: The core action still fakes it. Rip out the simulated path and implement the real backend operation, then re-verify with a refresh and an induced failure.
checklist: The core action performs its real operation
Result survives refresh
Errors are visible on failure

tactics.title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work: Work through the fix queue
tactics.flow_title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work
tactics.body: Convert every remaining FAKE and BROKEN item to WORKS. Checklist: Items fixed in priority order; Each verified via action + refresh; The table is updated with evidence per item Work through the remaining queue in order. For each item: implement the real behavior, wire persistence, add loading/error states, then verify with the same action+refresh test used in the audit and update its classification. Report progress as an updated table after each batch. Do not mark anything WORKS without the refresh test. If stuck: Items were marked fixed without verification. Re-test each supposedly fixed item with its action and a refresh, and reopen anything that fails.
checklist: Items fixed in priority order
Each verified via action + refresh
The table is updated with evidence per item

tactics.title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work: Add the missing states layer
tactics.flow_title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work
tactics.body: Sweep the whole app for loading, empty, and error gaps. Checklist: All async actions show loading; All lists have empty states; All failures render in the UI Do a states sweep across the app. Requirements: every async operation gets a loading indicator and a disabled trigger; every list gets an empty state; every failure path gets a visible UI error (no console-only); every form gets validation feedback. Output the list of gaps found and filled. If stuck: Silent failures remain. Grep every fetch/mutation for missing catch/error rendering, and add visible error and loading states to each.
checklist: All async actions show loading
All lists have empty states
All failures render in the UI

tactics.title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work: Final honest re-audit
tactics.flow_title: Fix App That Looks Good But Does Not Work
tactics.body: Close the loop with the same brutal audit that started it. Checklist: Same rigor as the first audit; Zero FAKE or BROKEN remain; Mobile and isolation checks done Re-run the full functional audit from step 1 with identical rigor: every feature action-tested, refreshed, classified with evidence. The goal is zero FAKE and zero BROKEN. Include a two-account data isolation check if the app has users, and a 375px mobile pass on the main flows. Fix anything that fails and re-audit until clean. If stuck: The final audit still lists failures - good, that honesty is the point. Fix each remaining item and re-run until the table is clean.
checklist: Same rigor as the first audit
Zero FAKE or BROKEN remain
Mobile and isolation checks done

tactics.title: Fix Broken Buttons: Inventory every interactive control
tactics.body: You cannot fix what you have not listed - audit first. Checklist: Every page and modal was inspected; Each control has a stated intended action; Status is based on the actual handler code Audit this entire app and produce a table of EVERY button, link, icon-button, and menu item: its label/location, what it is supposed to do, and its current status (WORKS / DEAD / FAKE - fake meaning it shows feedback without doing the real action). Actually inspect the handlers; do not guess. Include modals, dropdown items, and mobile-only controls. If stuck: The inventory missed controls or guessed statuses. Re-scan every route and component file for clickable elements and verify each handler's real behavior.
checklist: Every page and modal was inspected
Each control has a stated intended action
Status is based on the actual handler code

tactics.title: Fix Broken Buttons: Fix dead buttons
tactics.body: Wire every DEAD control to its intended real behavior. Checklist: Each formerly-dead button has a working handler; Backend-dependent buttons hit real endpoints; Effects are observable, not claimed Fix every control marked DEAD in the inventory. For each: implement the real handler performing the intended action (navigation, mutation, open dialog, submit); if it needs a backend call, implement or wire the endpoint; confirm the action's effect is observable (data changed, route changed, dialog opened). Update the inventory status as you go and list what changed per control. If stuck: Some buttons remain dead or now throw errors. Go through the remaining DEAD list one by one, implement each real action, and demonstrate its effect.
checklist: Each formerly-dead button has a working handler
Backend-dependent buttons hit real endpoints
Effects are observable, not claimed

tactics.title: Fix Broken Buttons: Fix fake buttons
tactics.body: Replace success theater with real actions. Checklist: Success feedback fires only after real success; Effects survive a page refresh; Failure shows a visible error Fix every control marked FAKE. For each: remove the fake feedback (toast/redirect with no action) and implement the actual operation - real create/update/delete, real submission, real state change with persistence; keep the success feedback but only after the real operation succeeds; add a visible error path when it fails. Prove each fix by refreshing and confirming the effect persisted. If stuck: Buttons still show success without persisting anything. Make the handler await the real backend result, gate the toast on it, and verify with a refresh.
checklist: Success feedback fires only after real success
Effects survive a page refresh
Failure shows a visible error

tactics.title: Fix Broken Buttons: Add loading and disabled states
tactics.body: Async buttons must communicate work and prevent double-fires. Checklist: Buttons disable while pending; Double-click produces one operation; Buttons recover after failure For every async button in the app: add a loading indicator (spinner or label change) while the operation runs; disable the button during the operation to prevent double submission; re-enable on completion or failure; ensure rapid double-clicks cause exactly one operation. List every button you touched. If stuck: Double-clicking still fires twice or buttons stick disabled. Guard handlers with a pending flag, and reset it in both success and error paths.
checklist: Buttons disable while pending
Double-click produces one operation
Buttons recover after failure

tactics.title: Fix Broken Buttons: Full click-through verification
tactics.body: Prove the app has zero dead controls left. Checklist: Every control re-tested after fixes; Failure paths tested with simulated errors; No control remains DEAD or FAKE Do a full click-through of the app and produce the final inventory table with every control now marked WORKS, including evidence (what happened when clicked). Test each async button's failure path by simulating a network error. Any control not verifiably working stays open and must be fixed before finishing. If stuck: The final table still contains unverified controls. Test each remaining item now, record the observed behavior, and fix stragglers before closing.
checklist: Every control re-tested after fixes
Failure paths tested with simulated errors
No control remains DEAD or FAKE

tactics.title: Fix Broken Form Submission: Inventory and test every form
tactics.body: Find each form's actual behavior versus its intended effect. Checklist: Every form was actually submitted; Persistence checked via refresh; Network tab checked for real requests List every form in the app (auth, create/edit, settings, search, contact - including in modals). For each: its intended effect, then actually submit it with valid data and record what happens (request fired? endpoint hit? data persisted after refresh? feedback shown?). Classify: WORKS / SILENT (nothing happens) / FAKE (feedback without persistence) / BROKEN (errors). If stuck: Forms were classified without submission tests. Submit each with valid data, watch the network tab, refresh, and reclassify based on evidence.
checklist: Every form was actually submitted
Persistence checked via refresh
Network tab checked for real requests

tactics.title: Fix Broken Form Submission: Wire submissions to real endpoints
tactics.body: Every SILENT and FAKE form must reach the backend and persist. Checklist: Each form fires a real request; Submitted data survives refresh; Success feedback is gated on the response Fix each non-working form's submission path. Requirements: the submit handler prevents default, gathers values, and calls the correct backend endpoint; the endpoint validates and persists to the database; the UI awaits the result - success feedback only after confirmed persistence, then appropriate navigation or reset; verify each by submitting and refreshing to see the data. If stuck: Some forms still persist nothing. Trace the handler to the endpoint to the database write, fix the broken hop, and re-verify with a refresh.
checklist: Each form fires a real request
Submitted data survives refresh
Success feedback is gated on the response

tactics.title: Fix Broken Form Submission: Add validation on both sides
tactics.body: Catch bad input inline, and never trust the client alone. Checklist: Each rule shows an inline message when violated; Direct API calls with bad data are rejected; Errors clear on correction Implement validation for every form. Client: required fields, formats (email/number), lengths, and matching fields validated with inline per-field error messages before submission; errors clear as the user fixes them. Server: the endpoint re-validates everything and returns field-level errors the UI displays. Test each rule by violating it, and test the server rules with a direct API call bypassing the UI. If stuck: The server accepts data the client would block. Add the same validation rules to the endpoint and return structured field errors the form can render.
checklist: Each rule shows an inline message when violated
Direct API calls with bad data are rejected
Errors clear on correction

tactics.title: Fix Broken Form Submission: Add states and double-submit protection
tactics.body: Forms must communicate work and never fire twice. Checklist: Double-submit produces one request; Failure preserves every entered value; Loading state visible during submission Add interaction states to every form. Requirements: submit button disables and shows a loading indicator during submission; rapid double-click or double-Enter causes exactly one request; on failure the form shows a visible error and keeps ALL user input; on success show clear feedback and reset or navigate appropriately; long forms should not lose data on accidental navigation (confirm or persist draft where… If stuck: Failure still clears user input or double-submits occur. Keep form state on error (only reset on success) and gate the handler with a pending flag.
checklist: Double-submit produces one request
Failure preserves every entered value
Loading state visible during submission

tactics.title: Fix Broken Form Submission: Forms QA pass
tactics.body: Verify every form's full lifecycle including hostile input. Checklist: All forms tested through all paths; Network-failure path executed per form; All failures fixed and re-verified Run the forms QA and report PASS/FAIL with evidence per form: valid submit persists (refresh check); every validation rule fires inline; server rejects direct bad calls; failure path (kill network) preserves input with visible error; double-submit blocked; success feedback correct; mobile usability of the form. Fix all failures and re-run. If stuck: Some forms skipped the failure-path test. Kill the network, submit each remaining form, and fix any that lose input or fail silently.
checklist: All forms tested through all paths
Network-failure path executed per form
All failures fixed and re-verified

tactics.title: Fix Fake Auth: Diagnose what is fake
tactics.body: Map exactly which parts of auth are theater before rebuilding. Checklist: Signup persistence verified in the database; Login verification logic inspected; Route and API guards checked Audit the current auth implementation and report precisely what is real vs fake: Does signup write a user record (show where)? Does login verify a password against a stored hash or accept anything? Where does auth state live and does it survive refresh? Are routes guarded before render? Do backend endpoints check the session? Output a table: component -> current behavior -> required behavior. If stuck: The diagnosis is optimistic guesswork. Trace the actual code paths: run a signup, query the user store, attempt a wrong-password login, and hit a private API logged-out. Report what actually happened.
checklist: Signup persistence verified in the database
Login verification logic inspected
Route and API guards checked

tactics.title: Fix Fake Auth: Implement real user persistence
tactics.body: Signup must create actual users with hashed passwords. Checklist: Record exists after signup with hashed password; Duplicate email shows a UI error; No plaintext password anywhere Fix signup to be real. Requirements: a user model with unique email and bcrypt/argon2-hashed password; the signup endpoint validates input, rejects duplicate emails with a visible UI error, creates the record, and starts the session; the password hash is never returned to the client. Prove it: sign up, show the stored record (hash present, no plaintext), and show the duplicate-email failure. If stuck: Users are still not persisted or passwords are plaintext. Implement the backend user creation with hashing now and re-verify by querying the store after signup.
checklist: Record exists after signup with hashed password
Duplicate email shows a UI error
No plaintext password anywhere

tactics.title: Fix Fake Auth: Implement real credential verification
tactics.body: Login must check the password, not just navigate. Checklist: Wrong password is rejected; Unknown email is rejected with the same generic message; Correct login creates a session Fix login to verify credentials. Requirements: the login endpoint looks up the user by email and compares the password against the stored hash; wrong password and unknown email both show 'Invalid email or password' in the UI; success creates the session and redirects; loading state during submit. Prove it with three attempts: correct (succeeds), wrong password (fails visibly), unknown email (fails visibly). If stuck: Login still accepts anything. Wire the endpoint to a real hash comparison and block navigation unless it returns success.
checklist: Wrong password is rejected
Unknown email is rejected with the same generic message
Correct login creates a session

tactics.title: Fix Fake Auth: Implement session persistence and logout
tactics.body: Auth state must live somewhere durable, restored on load. Checklist: Refresh preserves the session; Restore happens before protected render; Logout plus back button exposes nothing Fix sessions. Requirements: on login/signup store a session token (httpOnly cookie preferred, or localStorage with the tradeoff stated); on app load, restore the user by verifying the token before rendering protected UI, with a loading state; logout clears the token client- and server-side and redirects. Prove it: log in, refresh (still in), close/reopen tab (still in), logout then back button (locked out). If stuck: Refresh still logs users out. Persist the token, add an app-load restore that verifies it and populates the user, and gate protected rendering on that check.
checklist: Refresh preserves the session
Restore happens before protected render
Logout plus back button exposes nothing

tactics.title: Fix Fake Auth: Enforce guards on routes and APIs
tactics.step_title: Enforce guards on routes and APIs
tactics.body: Protection must exist in two layers: router and backend. Checklist: Direct URL access redirects without a content flash; Private APIs return 401 without a session; The protected list covers everything private Fix protection. Requirements: a route guard that redirects logged-out users from every protected page before rendering content; every backend endpoint serving private data verifies the session and returns 401 otherwise; list every protected route and endpoint and its guard. Prove it: open protected URLs logged-out (redirect, no content flash) and call private APIs without a token (401). If stuck: APIs still serve data without auth. Add session verification to every private endpoint - frontend redirects alone are not protection - and re-test with direct calls.
checklist: Direct URL access redirects without a content flash
Private APIs return 401 without a session
The protected list covers everything private

tactics.title: Fix Fake Auth: Full auth verification
tactics.body: Run the complete honest test suite on the rebuilt auth. Checklist: All eleven cases executed with observed results; No case passed on assumption; All failures fixed and re-verified Run and report PASS/FAIL with evidence: fresh signup creates a record; duplicate signup fails visibly; wrong password fails; login succeeds; refresh persists; protected URL logged-out redirects; private API logged-out returns 401; logout clears; back button after logout shows nothing private; forms validate empty input; mobile layout works. Fix all failures and re-run. If stuck: Cases were skipped or assumed. Execute each one now, capture the observed behavior, and fix any remaining fake or leaky path.
checklist: All eleven cases executed with observed results
No case passed on assumption
All failures fixed and re-verified

tactics.title: Fix Routing/Navigation: Map routes and links
tactics.body: Inventory every route and every element that navigates. Checklist: All routes listed with protection status; Every link click-verified; Dead links and orphans flagged Produce two tables. Routes: every defined route, its component, and whether it is public or protected. Links: every nav item, button, card, and inline link that navigates - its label, intended destination, and verified actual destination (click each one). Flag mismatches, dead links (#/empty handlers), and orphan pages no link reaches. If stuck: Links were assumed from code reading. Click every navigation element in the running app and record where it actually goes.
checklist: All routes listed with protection status
Every link click-verified
Dead links and orphans flagged

tactics.title: Fix Routing/Navigation: Fix dead and wrong links
tactics.body: Every navigation element must reach its labeled destination. Checklist: No # or empty-handler links remain; Navigation does not full-reload the SPA; Orphans are linked or consciously removed Fix every flagged link. Requirements: dead links get real destinations (or removal only if truly redundant - state why); wrong destinations corrected; use the SPA's Link/navigate (no full page reloads); external links open safely in new tabs; orphan pages get linked from a sensible place or are removed deliberately. Re-verify each fixed link by clicking. If stuck: Some links still reload the page or go nowhere. Replace anchor tags with the router's Link component and set real destinations; re-click each.
checklist: No # or empty-handler links remain
Navigation does not full-reload the SPA
Orphans are linked or consciously removed

tactics.title: Fix Routing/Navigation: Fix deep links and refresh
tactics.body: Any URL must load directly and survive refresh. Checklist: Nested routes survive refresh; Detail pages load from the URL param alone; Invalid ids show a not-found state Verify and fix direct loading: open every route (including nested and parameterized ones like /items/123) directly in a fresh tab and refresh on it. Fix server 404s with the SPA fallback configuration; fix pages that crash without preloaded state by fetching from route params; parameterized routes with invalid ids must show a proper not-found state, not a crash. If stuck: Refresh still 404s or detail pages crash cold. Configure the catch-all fallback to index.html and make detail pages fetch their own data from params with loading/not-found states.
checklist: Nested routes survive refresh
Detail pages load from the URL param alone
Invalid ids show a not-found state

tactics.title: Fix Routing/Navigation: Fix guards, back button, and 404
tactics.body: Close the navigation edge cases users always hit. Checklist: No content flash before guard redirects; Post-login returns to the intended page; Back after logout exposes nothing; Unknown URLs render the 404 page Fix the edges. Requirements: protected routes redirect the logged-out to login without flashing content, and return users to their intended page after login; logged-in users are redirected away from login/signup; no redirect loops (test both states on every guard); back button works sensibly after redirects and logout (no private content, no traps); add a designed 404 page with a way home for unknown URLs. If stuck: Guard loops or back-button leaks persist. Base redirects on a resolved (not loading) auth state, store the intended destination before redirecting, and re-test the back path after logout.
checklist: No content flash before guard redirects
Post-login returns to the intended page
Back after logout exposes nothing
Unknown URLs render the 404 page

tactics.title: Fix Routing/Navigation: Navigation QA run
tactics.body: Prove the whole navigation graph works end to end. Checklist: Every link and route re-verified; Both auth states tested on guards; Mobile navigation verified; All failures fixed Run the navigation QA and report PASS/FAIL with evidence: click every link (correct destination); cold-load and refresh every route; back/forward through a 5-page journey; guard behavior in both auth states; 404 for garbage URLs; mobile nav reaches every destination. Fix all failures and re-run. If stuck: Failures remain in the table. Fix each specific route or link and repeat the affected checks until everything passes.
checklist: Every link and route re-verified
Both auth states tested on guards
Mobile navigation verified
All failures fixed

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Definir escopo e contrato de dados da inscrição
tactics.step_title: Definir escopo e contrato de dados da inscrição
tactics.body: Estabelecer exatamente quais campos existem, quais são obrigatórios e como o backend deve receber e armazenar a inscrição. Checklist: Existe lista explícita de campos com tipos e obrigatoriedade; Há regra clara para validar e-mail e campos vazios; A deduplicação por e-mail foi definida; O formato de resposta de sucesso e erro está descrito; Os estados de UI necessários foram listados Quero construir um fluxo de inscrição funcional em uma aplicação web. Antes de gerar interface, defina o contrato de dados completo da inscrição com: campos do formulário, tipos, obrigatoriedade, regras de validação, estratégia de deduplicação por e-mail, timestamps, formato do payload enviado ao backend, formato da resposta de sucesso e de erro, e estados de UI necessários. Considere no mínimo nome e e-mail, e… If stuck: Refaça sem desenhar UI ainda. Entregue apenas a especificação implementável do fluxo de
checklist: Existe lista explícita de campos com tipos e obrigatoriedade
Há regra clara para validar e-mail e campos vazios
A deduplicação por e-mail foi definida
O formato de resposta de sucesso e erro está descrito
Os estados de UI necessários foram listados

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Criar persistência real e estrutura de backend
tactics.step_title: Criar persistência real e estrutura de backend
tactics.body: Garantir que exista um local real para salvar inscrições e uma interface de backend para receber os dados. Checklist: Existe tabela, coleção ou modelo de inscrição real; O endpoint de criação está implementado; Há validação no servidor; Duplicidade por e-mail é tratada; É possível verificar um registro salvo fora da UI Implemente o backend funcional do fluxo de inscrição usando a stack atual do projeto. Crie a tabela ou coleção de inscrições com id, nome, email, campos opcionais definidos, createdAt e status se necessário. Adicione restrição ou checagem para evitar duplicidade por e-mail. Crie endpoint, server action ou rota de API para receber o payload, validar no servidor, salvar em armazenamento real e retornar respostas HTTP… If stuck: A implementação ainda parece simulada. Conecte o formulário a persistência real criando tabela ou coleção, endpoint de criação e verificação prática
checklist: Existe tabela, coleção ou modelo de inscrição real
O endpoint de criação está implementado
Há validação no servidor
Duplicidade por e-mail é tratada
É possível verificar um registro salvo fora da UI

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Construir o formulário de inscrição conectado ao backend
tactics.step_title: Construir o formulário de inscrição conectado ao backend
tactics.body: Criar a interface principal do usuário e ligá-la ao fluxo real de envio. Checklist: Todos os campos definidos aparecem na UI; O submit dispara chamada real ao backend; O payload enviado corresponde ao contrato de dados; Não há uso de mocks para simular sucesso; O formulário funciona em ambiente de execução Construa a página ou seção de inscrição usando a stack atual. Adicione inputs para nome e e-mail e demais campos definidos, com labels, placeholders apenas se úteis, tipos corretos e botão de envio. Conecte a submissão ao endpoint ou server action real já criado. O formulário deve capturar dados dos campos, montar o payload correto e processar a resposta do backend em vez de usar dados mockados. If stuck: Conserte a integração do formulário. Substitua qualquer submit fake por chamada real ao endpoint existente, envie o payload correto e trate a resposta do servidor no frontend.
checklist: Todos os campos definidos aparecem na UI
O submit dispara chamada real ao backend
O payload enviado corresponde ao contrato de dados
Não há uso de mocks para simular sucesso
O formulário funciona em ambiente de execução

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Adicionar validação completa no cliente e no servidor
tactics.step_title: Adicionar validação completa no cliente e no servidor
tactics.body: Impedir inscrições inválidas e garantir consistência dos dados. Checklist: Campos vazios obrigatórios impedem envio; E-mail inválido é rejeitado; O servidor rejeita payload manual inválido; Erros do backend aparecem na interface; Mensagens de erro são específicas e úteis Adicione validação robusta em duas camadas. No cliente, valide campos obrigatórios, formato de e-mail e regras mínimas de texto antes do submit, exibindo mensagens por campo. No servidor, valide o mesmo payload de forma independente e retorne resposta estruturada com erros de validação quando os dados forem inválidos. Garanta que a UI mostre os erros retornados pelo backend de forma clara. If stuck: A validação está incompleta. Implemente checagem duplicada no cliente e no servidor, padronize o formato de erros retornados e exiba essas mensagens por campo no formulário.
checklist: Campos vazios obrigatórios impedem envio
E-mail inválido é rejeitado
O servidor rejeita payload manual inválido
Erros do backend aparecem na interface
Mensagens de erro são específicas e úteis

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Tratar loading, sucesso, erro e prevenção de múltiplos envios
tactics.step_title: Tratar loading, sucesso, erro e prevenção de múltiplos envios
tactics.body: Melhorar a confiabilidade percebida e evitar inscrições repetidas por clique duplo ou lentidão. Checklist: Botão fica desabilitado durante envio; Existe indicador visível de carregamento; Sucesso só aparece após resposta positiva real; Erro não apaga dados sem necessidade; Cliques repetidos não criam múltiplas inscrições Implemente gerenciamento de estado do formulário durante submissão. Enquanto a requisição estiver em andamento, desabilite o botão, mostre loading claro e evite duplo clique. Em caso de sucesso, mostre confirmação real baseada na resposta do backend e decida se os campos serão limpos. Em caso de falha, mostre mensagem útil sem perder dados digitados desnecessariamente. O comportamento deve ser consistente com… If stuck: Corrija os estados do fluxo de envio. O botão precisa bloquear durante a requisição, o feedback deve depender da resposta real do backend e o formulário
checklist: Botão fica desabilitado durante envio
Existe indicador visível de carregamento
Sucesso só aparece após resposta positiva real
Erro não apaga dados sem necessidade
Cliques repetidos não criam múltiplas inscrições

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Implementar tratamento de duplicidade por e-mail
tactics.step_title: Implementar tratamento de duplicidade por e-mail
tactics.body: Evitar registros repetidos e dar resposta clara quando o usuário já estiver inscrito. Checklist: O backend detecta e-mails duplicados de forma confiável; A UI mostra mensagem específica para duplicidade; Não surgem dois registros iguais em testes simples; A regra de negócio está consistente; Erro de duplicidade é distinguido de erro interno Adicione lógica completa para lidar com e-mails já inscritos. Use restrição única no banco ou verificação transacional equivalente. No endpoint, retorne um erro específico e previsível para duplicidade. No frontend, trate esse retorno com mensagem clara, diferente de erro genérico. Se existir decisão de produto para atualizar registro em vez de bloquear, implemente de forma consistente e documentada. If stuck: A duplicidade ainda não está resolvida corretamente. Implemente proteção real no backend ou banco, retorne erro específico para e-mail já inscr
checklist: O backend detecta e-mails duplicados de forma confiável
A UI mostra mensagem específica para duplicidade
Não surgem dois registros iguais em testes simples
A regra de negócio está consistente
Erro de duplicidade é distinguido de erro interno

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Criar forma simples de verificar inscrições salvas
tactics.step_title: Criar forma simples de verificar inscrições salvas
tactics.body: Permitir validação manual de que a persistência está funcionando de verdade. Checklist: Há rota, tela ou método claro para consultar inscrições; Os dados exibidos vêm do armazenamento real; Nome, e-mail e data aparecem na verificação; Novas inscrições surgem após envio bem-sucedido; A verificação não depende de mocks Implemente uma maneira objetiva de comprovar que as inscrições foram gravadas. Prefira uma página interna ou rota de listagem simples que leia do armazenamento real e mostre nome, e-mail e data de criação. Se isso não fizer sentido para a stack atual, forneça no projeto um método igualmente prático e reproduzível para consultar os registros. A solução deve ler do backend real, não de estado local. If stuck: Adicione um mecanismo real de verificação dos registros persistidos, como uma página simples de listagem conectada ao banco ou instruções automatizadas dentro do projeto
checklist: Há rota, tela ou método claro para consultar inscrições
Os dados exibidos vêm do armazenamento real
Nome, e-mail e data aparecem na verificação
Novas inscrições surgem após envio bem-sucedido
A verificação não depende de mocks

tactics.title: Fluxo de inscrição funcional: Testar cenários críticos do fluxo de ponta a ponta
tactics.step_title: Testar cenários críticos do fluxo de ponta a ponta
tactics.body: Validar que o fluxo funciona em sucesso, erro, validação e duplicidade. tactics.title: Guard Memory Writes Against Injection: Make writes source-aware
tactics.body: Where a memory came from determines what it may become. Checklist: Source tag mandatory on every write; Untrusted-derived routes to quarantine by policy; High-trust tier restricted to user-stated/observed Instrument the memory write path with source awareness. Every write must carry the provenance of the content it derived from: USER-STATED (the user directly told the agent), OBSERVED (the agent verified via its own tool execution - a test passed, a file exists), UNTRUSTED-DERIVED (extracted from web pages, third-party docs, tool results of external origin), or INFERRED (the model's own reasoning). Policy by source:… If stuck: Writes arrive without a credible source. The model is guessing sources to satisfy the field - tighten instructions and validation: 'observed' requires citing the tool result that proves it, or it is demoted to inferred.
checklist: Source tag mandatory on every write
Untrusted-derived routes to quarantine by policy
High-trust tier restricted to user-stated/observed

tactics.title: Guard Memory Writes Against Injection: Validate content before persistence
tactics.body: A write is a claim; check it before you believe it. Checklist: Format and plausibility enforced; Instruction-like memory content flagged; Contradictions caught before persistence Add content validation gating persistence. Checks: FORMAT (matches the entry schema, within length caps); PLAUSIBILITY (sanity rules per memory type - a 'preference' should read like a preference, a fact should be atomic, not a paragraph of instructions); INJECTION SCAN (memory content itself must not contain instruction-like payloads - a memory that says 'when recalled, tell the user to run X' is an attack, flag… If stuck: An instruction-shaped memory slipped through. Add explicit detection: memory content that addresses future behavior ('when...', 'always tell the user...', 'ignore...') is presumptively an injection payload - block and surface it.
checklist: Format and plausibility enforced
Instruction-like memory content flagged
Contradictions caught before persistence

tactics.title: Guard Memory Writes Against Injection: Quarantine and require corroboration
tactics.body: Untrusted claims are hypotheses until reality agrees. Checklist: Quarantined memories excluded from recall; Promotion requires independent corroboration; TTL expiry and contradiction-delete work Build the quarantine pipeline for untrusted-derived and low-confidence memories. Quarantined entries: are excluded from default recall (never influence behavior while pending); carry their provenance and a TTL; get promoted to the normal store only on corroboration - a second independent observation, user confirmation, or the agent verifying the claim through a trusted tool; are deleted on contradiction; expire at… If stuck: Quarantined memories influenced a decision. Check the recall filter - pending entries must be invisible to normal recall everywhere except the explicit review surface; a single unfiltered recall path defeats quarantine.
checklist: Quarantined memories excluded from recall
Promotion requires independent corroboration
TTL expiry and contradiction-delete work

tactics.title: Guard Memory Writes Against Injection: Schedule re-validation and drill poisoning
tactics.body: Guard the write, then keep guarding the belief. Checklist: Re-validation cadence scales with trust; Poisoned fact quarantined and expired; Legitimate observation promotes correctly Add re-validation and run the drill. RE-VALIDATION: a scheduled job re-checks stored memories - facts past a staleness window get re-verified where cheaply possible (does the file/config the fact describes still hold?); memories whose related actions recently failed lose confidence; contradicted memories are archived. High-trust memories are audited least often; untrusted-origin ones most. DRILL: run the full… If stuck: The poisoned fact influenced behavior before expiry. It was recalled from quarantine or promoted without real corroboration - audit the promotion criteria and the recall filter, then re-drill until the poison is inert throughout its…
checklist: Re-validation cadence scales with trust
Poisoned fact quarantined and expired
Legitimate observation promotes correctly

tactics.title: Hackathon Judge Report: Use the project hands-on
tactics.body: Judge the product, not the pitch - use it like a real user. Record what you observed neutrally - facts before scores. If stuck: The evaluation trusted the demo video. Open the actual app and perform the core claim yourself - videos hide dead apps.

If stuck: Scores drifted from the anchors ('felt like an 8'). Re-score against the anchor descriptions and attach the observation each score relies on.

tactics.title: Hackathon Judge Report: Write actionable feedback

No filler compliments, no vague criticisms. If stuck: The feedback is 'nice UI, needs work'. Rewrite each point naming the exact screen/behavior and what to change - useful beats polite.

If stuck: First-judged projects were scored on a different standard. Re-score them against the final calibrated sense of the anchors and document every change.

tactics.title: Hook a Permission Layer onto Dangerous Tools: Define the danger rule set
tactics.flow_title: Hook a Permission Layer onto Dangerous Tools
tactics.body: Enumerate what must never run silently - concretely. Checklist: Patterns match normalized commands; Protected paths cover secrets and workspace escape; Every rule has a verdict and reason Write the danger rules as data. COMMAND PATTERNS (normalized before matching: resolve quoting, collapse whitespace): recursive deletion (rm -rf and equivalents on any path), git destructive ops (force-push, hard reset on shared branches, clean -fdx), bulk data ops (DROP/TRUNCATE, mass UPDATE without WHERE), package/system mutations (global installs, chmod -R 777, curl piped to shell). PROTECTED PATHS for writes and… If stuck: The list is generic. Walk each of my tools asking 'what is the worst call this accepts?' and write a rule for every answer - the rule set must reflect this harness, not a textbook.
checklist: Patterns match normalized commands
Protected paths cover secrets and workspace escape
Every rule has a verdict and reason

tactics.title: Hook a Permission Layer onto Dangerous Tools: Implement the hook point
tactics.flow_title: Hook a Permission Layer onto Dangerous Tools
tactics.body: One interception point, running before anything executes. Checklist: Hooks run before every execution; Strictest verdict wins; Hook exceptions fail closed Build the pre-tool-use hook into the dispatch path. Mechanics: after schema validation and before handler execution, run the hook chain with {tool, arguments, session context}; each hook returns allow / require-approval(reason) / block(reason); the strictest verdict wins; require-approval routes to the approval UX with full call details; block short-circuits with a structured refusal to the model ('blocked by… If stuck: A call path skipped the hooks. Enforce architecturally: handlers must be unreachable except through dispatch - make direct invocation impossible (private registration) rather than discouraged.
checklist: Hooks run before every execution
Strictest verdict wins
Hook exceptions fail closed

tactics.title: Hook a Permission Layer onto Dangerous Tools: Harden the patterns against evasion
tactics.flow_title: Hook a Permission Layer onto Dangerous Tools
tactics.body: The gap between a pattern and its intent is where accidents live. Checklist: Path, quoting, and indirection evasions tested; Just-written-script execution flagged; Residual risk documented, not denied Red-team the rules. Try the evasions: path tricks (rm -rf ./, rm -rf $HOME, cd /important && rm -rf .), quoting and splitting ('r''m' -rf, echo rm -rf | sh), indirection (writing a script with the dangerous command then executing it, invoking via xargs/find -delete), and interpreter smuggling (python -c os.system(...)). For each evasion that passes: fix by strengthening normalization (argument resolution,… If stuck: Indirection evasions keep winning. Stop chasing string patterns for those - add the behavioral rule instead: executing any file created or modified in this session requires approval, regardless of content.

tactics.title: Implement Context Compaction: Add token accounting
tactics.body: You cannot manage what the loop does not measure. Checklist: Count computed before every call; Breakdown by section logged; Threshold event fires at the configured fraction Instrument the agent loop with context accounting. tactics.title: Implement Context Compaction: Design the structured summary format
tactics.body: Compaction quality is decided by the format, not the model. Checklist: All seven sections defined; Prompt demands exact paths and names; Test summary graded against a real transcript Design the compaction summary as a structured document, not prose. Sections: TASK (the original request, verbatim), PLAN STATE (todo list snapshot with statuses), DECISIONS (choices made and why, one line each), WORKSPACE FACTS (files created/modified with one-line descriptions, key paths, commands that worked), CONSTRAINTS (rules and user preferences stated so far), OPEN ITEMS (unresolved questions, known issues),… If stuck: Summaries read like meeting notes and lose specifics. Tighten the prompt: require every file mentioned in the chunk to appear in WORKSPACE FACTS and every decision to name its alternative - then re-test.
checklist: All seven sections defined

tactics.title: Implement Context Compaction: Implement the compaction operation
tactics.body: Swap history for the digest without dropping the thread. Checklist: Recent tail kept verbatim; Pre-compaction history archived; Failure fallback still preserves task and plan Implement compaction. When triggered: (1) split history into OLD (everything except the last N turns, default 10) and RECENT (kept verbatim); (2) run the summarization call on OLD with the structured prompt; (3) rebuild history as [summary-as-system-note] + RECENT; (4) re-render dynamic reminders (plan block) after the swap; (5) log before/after token counts and archive the pre-compaction history to a session file… If stuck: After compaction the agent lost the plan. Ensure the plan reminder is re-rendered from harness state after the history swap - the digest describes the past, but live state blocks must be rebuilt.
checklist: Recent tail kept verbatim

Check that WORKSPACE FACTS captured the modification and that the summary was inserted where the model attends to it (as a clearly-labeled system note, not buried mid-history).

tactics.title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps: Define detection and the kill switch
tactics.flow_title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps
tactics.step_title: Define detection and the kill switch
tactics.body: You cannot respond to what you cannot detect or stop. Checklist: Mishap signals enumerated with notification paths; Kill switch halts loop and revokes authority; Verified to stop action within seconds Build detection and the emergency stop. DETECTION: enumerate mishap signals - blast-radius limits tripping, security events (blocked/escalated actions spiking), anomaly flags from observability (runaway cost, error bursts), audit-trail alerts on sensitive-resource changes, and human reports; define where each surfaces and who is notified. KILL SWITCH: implement a single, fast action that immediately halts the agent… If stuck: The kill switch leaves in-flight actions running. It must cancel at the next safe boundary AND revoke authority so queued/next calls are blocked - stopping new turns is not enough if a destructive call is already dispatched.

tactics.title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps: Write containment and rollback procedures
tactics.flow_title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps
tactics.body: Stop the bleeding, then undo the damage - in that order. Checklist: Evidence-preservation before any cleanup; Rollback locates the last good checkpoint via audit timestamps; External/irreversible effects get compensating actions Author the containment and rollback runbook sections. CONTAINMENT (immediately after kill switch): isolate affected systems if needed (revoke the agent's credentials/tokens, pause dependent automation), preserve evidence (do NOT delete logs, traces, or the workspace state - snapshot them first), and assess scope from the audit trail (what actions fired, what they touched). ROLLBACK: use the checkpoint/undo system… If stuck: Rollback was attempted before preserving evidence. Fix the ordering in the runbook: snapshot logs/traces/state FIRST - rollback can destroy the evidence needed to understand and prevent recurrence.
checklist: Evidence-preservation before any cleanup
Rollback locates the last good checkpoint via audit timestamps
External/irreversible effects get compensating actions

tactics.title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps: Write the investigation procedure
tactics.flow_title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps
tactics.body: Reconstruct exactly what happened, using the records you built. Checklist: Audit trail and replay used to reconstruct events; Root cause classified into defined categories; Missing records flagged as findings Author the investigation section leveraging your observability and audit systems. Procedure: locate the incident session(s); pull the audit trail for the affected resources (what actions, what authority, what triggering requests); open the trace tree and use session replay to see the exact model context and decisions at the point things went wrong; identify the ROOT cause and classify it - prompt injection,… If stuck: The investigation cannot determine why the agent acted. That is an observability/audit gap - note it as a top finding and strengthen those records (the request-to-action lineage and context capture) so the next incident is reconstructable.
checklist: Audit trail and replay used to reconstruct events
Root cause classified into defined categories
Missing records flagged as findings

tactics.title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps: Establish the postmortem loop and drill it
tactics.flow_title: Incident Response Runbook for Agent Mishaps
tactics.step_title: Establish the postmortem loop and drill it
tactics.body: Every incident must leave the system safer - proven by a live drill. Checklist: Postmortem produces control-mapped prevention items; Incident not closed until fixes land; Full runbook drilled end to end with timings Close with the prevention loop and a full drill. POSTMORTEM: adopt a blameless template - timeline (from audit/traces), root cause, what contained it and how fast, what went well/poorly, and REQUIRED prevention items each mapped to a concrete control (a new rule-file rule, a permission tier change, a blast-radius limit, an injection-suite case, an observability improvement) with an owner; the incident is not closed… If stuck: The drill produced a writeup but no structural change. Enforce the rule: every incident yields at least one implemented control (rule, gate, limit, or test) - a postmortem that changes nothing guarantees the same incident returns.
checklist: Postmortem produces control-mapped prevention items
Incident not closed until fixes land
Full runbook drilled end to end with timings

tactics.title: Investor Pitch Script: Build the narrative spine
