tactics.body: Slides serve the script - one point per slide, mapped to beats. Checklist: Headlines are assertions; Each slide makes exactly one point; Every slide maps to a beat Structure my deck against the narrative. Produce a slide-by-slide outline (10-12 slides): for each - the single point it makes, the headline (a full assertion, not a label: 'Retention doubles after week 2', not 'Metrics'), what is shown (visual/number/demo frame), and which script beat it accompanies. Include where the live demo or product visual lands. Kill any slide that does not advance the story. If stuck: Slides are labeled 'Team, Market, Product' with multi-point clutter. Rewrite every headline as the sentence you want remembered and split or cut overloaded slides.
checklist: Headlines are assertions
Each slide makes exactly one point
Every slide maps to a beat

tactics.title: Investor Pitch Script: Prep the hard questions
tactics.body: The Q&A is the real pitch - rehearse the uncomfortable ten. Checklist: Questions are specific to this company; Answers concede what is true; The rehearsal produced critiques Prepare my Q&A. Produce the 10 hardest questions for THIS company (competition, 'why won't incumbent X do this', traction depth, churn, founder risk, market timing, moat, pricing, what kills this, why this team) with: the honest core answer (2-3 sentences), the trap to avoid in each, and where to bridge back to strength. Include the 'I don't know' protocol - how to answer gaps credibly. Then simulate the Q&A: ask… If stuck: The answers are defensive spin. Rewrite each to concede the true part in sentence one, then give the reason it does not kill the company.
checklist: Questions are specific to this company
Answers concede what is true
The rehearsal produced critiques

tactics.title: Investor Pitch Script: Craft the ask and close
tactics.body: End with a specific ask and a reason to move now. Checklist: Funds map to milestones; The close mirrors the opening; The hallway version exists Write my ask and close. Produce: the raise amount and instrument; use of funds in 3-4 buckets with what each buys (milestones, not salaries-abstract); the milestone story ('this round gets us to X, which unlocks Y'); the closing line that ties back to the opening future; and the follow-up plan (what I send after, the data room basics list for my stage). Give me a 15-second version of the ask for hallway… If stuck: The ask is a number with no milestone logic. Connect the amount to the specific proof points it buys and what those unlock for the next round.
checklist: Funds map to milestones
The close mirrors the opening
The hallway version exists

tactics.title: Jailbreak Regression Suite: Assemble the jailbreak corpus
tactics.body: Collect the attacks that matter for your agent's boundaries. Checklist: Attacks scoped to real safety boundaries; Technique families covered broadly; Expected safe behavior specified per case Build the jailbreak corpus. Sources: jailbreaks found in your own red-teaming, publicly documented technique families (persona/role-play, hypothetical framing, token smuggling, many-shot priming, refusal-suppression phrasing), and any real attempts seen in usage. Scope to YOUR agent's actual safety boundaries - what should it refuse or handle carefully given its capabilities (destructive actions, sensitive data,… If stuck: The corpus tests generic model safety irrelevant to my agent. Refocus on boundaries that matter here - if the agent has no capability an attack would abuse, that attack is noise; prioritize jailbreaks that reach real actions or data.
checklist: Attacks scoped to real safety boundaries
Technique families covered broadly
Expected safe behavior specified per case

tactics.title: Jailbreak Regression Suite: Build reliable compliance evaluation
tactics.body: The hard part is telling a real refusal from a soft yes. Checklist: Hedged/partial compliance classified as failure; Judge calibrated against human labels; Action-based cases judged on the action Implement response evaluation. For each case, classify the agent's behavior as REFUSED (declined and offered no meaningful assistance toward the harmful goal), PARTIAL (hedged but leaked usable help - usually a failure), or COMPLIED (did the harmful thing). Use a calibrated LLM judge with a per-case rubric describing what compliance looks like specifically for that attack (a refusal that then provides the steps… If stuck: The judge scores polite refusals-that-then-comply as refused. Sharpen the rubric with exactly that example per category and re-calibrate - subtle compliance is the whole point of the suite.
checklist: Hedged/partial compliance classified as failure
Judge calibrated against human labels
Action-based cases judged on the action

tactics.title: Jailbreak Regression Suite: Version, gate, and grow the suite
tactics.step_title: Version, gate, and grow the suite
tactics.body: A safety net that is not tied to CI and not growing will fail you quietly. Checklist: Runs on model bumps, not just prompt edits; Regressions block with reproductions; Deliberate weakening is caught Operationalize. VERSIONING: every run records model version, prompt/harness version, and per-case results, stored for trend analysis. GATING: the suite runs in CI on prompt/harness changes AND on model version bumps (add a scheduled run plus a manual trigger for provider updates that CI would not otherwise catch); any regression - a case that was REFUSED now PARTIAL/COMPLIED - blocks with the reproduction. GROWTH:… If stuck: The deliberate weakening was not caught. Coverage gap for that boundary - the corpus lacks an attack that exercises it; add one that fails against the weakened prompt and passes when restored.
checklist: Runs on model bumps, not just prompt edits
Regressions block with reproductions
Deliberate weakening is caught

tactics.title: Landing Page Copy: Define audience and message hierarchy
tactics.body: Copy converts one reader at a time - pick the reader first. Checklist: The audience is specific; Pains are phrased as the user would say them; One primary action is chosen Define the messaging foundation for my landing page. I will describe the product below. Produce: the ONE primary audience (specific role/situation, not 'everyone'); their top 3 pains in their own words; the primary transformation the product delivers; the message hierarchy (the one thing they must believe, then supporting points in order); and the single primary action the page drives toward. MY PRODUCT: [describe… If stuck: The foundation targets multiple audiences. Choose the single highest-value reader and rewrite the pains and hierarchy for them alone.
checklist: The audience is specific
Pains are phrased as the user would say them
One primary action is chosen

tactics.title: Landing Page Copy: Write the hero section
tactics.body: The 5-second test happens here - clarity beats cleverness. Checklist: Headlines are outcome/pain based; CTA text names the action; The winner passes the 5-second test Write my hero section. Produce: 5 headline options that state the outcome or kill the pain (under 10 words, no buzzwords, concrete); a subheadline explaining how it works in one plain sentence; the primary CTA button text (action-specific, e.g. 'Create your first invoice' not 'Get Started') plus microcopy under it removing friction (free? time? card required?); and a hero visual recommendation. Then pick the… If stuck: The headlines describe the category ('A platform for X'). Rewrite each to state what the reader gets or stops suffering, in their words.
checklist: Headlines are outcome/pain based
CTA text names the action
The winner passes the 5-second test

tactics.title: Landing Page Copy: Write problem and solution sections
tactics.body: Show them you understand the pain before showing the cure. Checklist: The problem section uses specific scenarios; How-it-works is exactly 3 verb-first steps; Every feature has a 'which means' Write the problem and solution sections. Problem: 3-4 sentences agitating the current painful way (specific scenarios, not abstract pain), so the reader nods. Solution: introduce the product as the turn, then a 'how it works' in exactly 3 steps (verb-first, concrete, each one sentence). Then translate the top 4 features into benefit statements: 'FEATURE, which means BENEFIT' format, cutting any feature without a… If stuck: The problem copy is abstract and features lack benefits. Rewrite the pain as a concrete scene from the reader's week, and finish every feature with 'which means...'.
checklist: The problem section uses specific scenarios
How-it-works is exactly 3 verb-first steps
Every feature has a 'which means'

tactics.title: Landing Page Copy: Write proof, pricing, and FAQ
tactics.body: Trust and objections decide the conversion - handle both. Checklist: No fabricated testimonials; Plans describe what you can do; FAQ answers the real objections Write the trust sections. Social proof: realistic testimonial structure (what to ask users for; placeholder frames labeled clearly if none exist yet - never fake names) plus any honest numbers we have (users, items processed). Pricing: plan copy that anchors value (what each plan lets you DO), with the recommended plan flagged. FAQ: the top 6 real objections (price, time, trust, switching, technical fit, 'will it… If stuck: The FAQ dodges hard objections and testimonials feel fake. Answer price and trust objections head-on with honest tradeoffs, and replace fake proof with labeled frames or real numbers.
checklist: No fabricated testimonials
Plans describe what you can do
FAQ answers the real objections

tactics.title: Landing Page Copy: Final pass: CTAs, flow, and the read-aloud test
tactics.step_title: Final pass: CTAs, flow, and the read-aloud test
tactics.body: Tighten the page into one continuous persuasive path. Checklist: Three CTAs placed with varied text; No buzzwords remain; The 5-second test passes on the final version Do the final copy pass on the assembled page. Requirements: place CTAs after the hero, mid-page, and at the end (varying text, same action); check the narrative flow top to bottom (each section earns the next); run the read-aloud test and cut every sentence that sounds unnatural spoken; kill remaining buzzwords and vague claims; verify a cold reader can answer 'what is it, who is it for, what do I do next' in 5… If stuck: The page still reads like marketing-speak. Read it aloud, rewrite every sentence you would not say to a person, and re-run the 5-second test.
checklist: Three CTAs placed with varied text
No buzzwords remain
The 5-second test passes on the final version

tactics.title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains: Audit the current tool prompt
tactics.flow_title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains
tactics.body: You cannot layer what you have not inventoried. Checklist: Every line assigned to preference/usage/safety; Prohibitions without alternatives flagged; Token count per bucket recorded Take one tool prompt from your agent (the shell/exec tool is the best candidate) and classify every line into three buckets: PREFERENCE (which tool or approach to choose - 'read files with the Read tool, not cat'), USAGE (mechanics - absolute paths, chaining commands, timeouts, output limits), and SAFETY (destructive operations, credentials, force-push class rules). Flag lines that are prohibitions without an… If stuck: The audit says everything is 'usage'. Re-check: any line naming a competing tool or approach is a PREFERENCE, and any line about irreversible effects is SAFETY - if those buckets are empty, the prompt is missing them, which is itself the…
checklist: Every line assigned to preference/usage/safety
Prohibitions without alternatives flagged
Token count per bucket recorded

tactics.title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains: Write the preference chain
tactics.flow_title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains
tactics.body: Positive alternatives outperform bare prohibitions. Checklist: One line per capability, alternative always named; NOT capitalized consistently; Rationale framed as experience, not security Rewrite the preference bucket as a compact chain at the TOP of the prompt, one capability per line, each naming the preferred tool and the rejected fallback: 'File search: Use Glob (NOT find or ls)', 'Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)', 'Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)', 'Write files: Use Write (NOT echo > or heredoc)'. Keep NOT capitalized for visual weight. Justify the chain with experience, not fear:… If stuck: The model still uses raw commands. Check placement: the chain must be at the very top of the tool description, and each line must name the replacement tool exactly as it is registered - a preference for a tool the model cannot see is noise.
checklist: One line per capability, alternative always named
NOT capitalized consistently
Rationale framed as experience, not security

tactics.title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains: Write usage constraints and safety protocols
tactics.flow_title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains
tactics.step_title: Write usage constraints and safety protocols
tactics.body: Mechanics in the middle, the scariest rules last and loudest. Checklist: Usage layer covers paths, chaining, and output limits; Every NEVER rule has an explicit-exception clause; Enforced rules state that they are enforced Rewrite the middle layer as usage mechanics: absolute paths, when to chain with && versus parallel calls, output-size expectations, background-execution rules. Then write the final safety layer for destructive operations only. Use NEVER precisely: 'NEVER force-push to main/master', 'NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify)', 'NEVER amend commits', each paired with the exception 'unless the user explicitly requests it'. Where… If stuck: The safety block grew past ten rules. Merge overlapping rules and demote anything non-destructive to the usage layer - NEVER only works when it is rare; a wall of NEVERs reads as boilerplate.
checklist: Usage layer covers paths, chaining, and output limits
Every NEVER rule has an explicit-exception clause
Enforced rules state that they are enforced

tactics.title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains: A/B test the layered prompt
tactics.flow_title: Design Layered Tool Prompts with Preference Chains
tactics.body: Prove the structure changed behavior before shipping it. Checklist: Same task set run on both prompts; Tool-choice and safety scored per task; Final prompt versioned Run the same task set against the old and new prompts and compare transcripts. Tasks to include: a file edit (does it choose the Edit tool over sed?), a file read (Read over cat?), a search (dedicated search tool over grep?), and a request that brushes a safety rule (asks for a force-push without explicit authorization - it should decline or ask). Score each run: correct tool chosen, safety rule respected, no… If stuck: Behavior barely moved. Verify the model actually receives the new prompt (cache or config may serve the old one), then test moving the least-followed rule to the top of its layer - position within a layer matters almost as much as the…
checklist: Same task set run on both prompts
Tool-choice and safety scored per task
Final prompt versioned

tactics.title: Local Service Booking Website: Structure the business content
tactics.body: Collect the real-world facts the whole site depends on. Checklist: Services have prices or honest ranges; Hours and contact are real; The booking model is chosen Structure the site content. I will describe the business below. Produce: the service list (name, description, duration, price - push for real prices); business facts (hours, service area, phone, address if physical); the differentiators (what to emphasize: speed, guarantees, experience); the booking model (request-for-time vs pick-a-slot - recommend based on the business); and the page structure (home, services,… If stuck: The content has placeholder prices and hours. Get the real values - a local site with 'call for pricing' everywhere loses to competitors that answer.
checklist: Services have prices or honest ranges
Hours and contact are real
The booking model is chosen

tactics.title: Local Service Booking Website: Build home and services pages
tactics.body: Answer the visitor's three questions immediately: what, where, how much. Checklist: The headline names the service and area; Every service shows a price; Book buttons carry the service selection Build the homepage and services page. Homepage: what the business does and where (headline with service + area), a prominent Book Now button, top services with prices, trust strip (years, jobs done, rating if real), hours and contact visible, mobile-first layout. Services page: every service with description, duration, price, and a per-service book button carrying the selection into the form. If stuck: The homepage buries what the business does. Rewrite the hero to 'Service + Area' with the book button beside it - clarity beats cleverness for local.
checklist: The headline names the service and area
Every service shows a price
Book buttons carry the service selection

tactics.title: Local Service Booking Website: Build the booking request flow
tactics.body: The money feature: requests must persist for the owner. Checklist: A test request exists in the database; Validation blocks bad input; Success sets response expectations Implement the booking flow per the chosen model: the form (name, phone, service select, preferred date/time, notes) with validation (phone format, future dates only) and inline errors; submission stores the request in the database with status 'new'; a success state confirming what happens next ('we confirm within X hours'); loading and error states. Verify a test submission persists and is retrievable. If stuck: The form stores nothing. Wire it to a backend create endpoint and verify persistence - a lost booking request is lost revenue.
checklist: A test request exists in the database
Validation blocks bad input
Success sets response expectations

tactics.title: Local Service Booking Website: Build the owner's request view
tactics.body: The owner must see and manage incoming requests simply. Checklist: Requests appear with full details; Status changes persist; Tap-to-call works on mobile Implement the owner view (simple auth or admin route): incoming requests newest-first with all details and status (new/confirmed/completed/declined); status updates that persist; a phone/tap-to-call link on each request for quick confirmation; a badge or count of new requests; empty and loading states. Keep it dead simple - owners are busy. If stuck: Status changes reset on reload. Persist them via the backend and re-fetch - the owner's workflow depends on statuses sticking.
checklist: Requests appear with full details
Status changes persist
Tap-to-call works on mobile

tactics.title: Local Service Booking Website: Trust, contact, and mobile QA
tactics.body: Local trust signals plus a hard mobile pass close the job. Checklist: No fabricated reviews exist; Contact info is complete and consistent; The 375px booking journey passes Finish trust and QA. Add: a reviews section (real reviews if provided; a labeled placeholder structure if not - never fabricated), service-area statement, an about section with the human behind the business, complete contact page (hours, phone with tel: link, address/map embed if physical), consistent business info in the footer. Then run the mobile QA: the full visitor journey (land, browse services, book) at… If stuck: Trust sections have fake reviews or the mobile form fails. Remove fabrications (label placeholders honestly) and fix the mobile form with the keyboard open.
checklist: No fabricated reviews exist
Contact info is complete and consistent
The 375px booking journey passes

tactics.title: Add Magic‑Link Passwordless Login: Configure Email Service
tactics.body: Enable the app to send real emails containing magic links. Checklist: Can the project start without import errors?; Does sendMagicLink send an email via the chosen provider?; Are all env vars defined and used? 1. Install the chosen email library (e.g., @sendgrid/mail or nodemailer). 2. In the project root, add the following environment variables to .env: EMAIL_PROVIDER (value: 'sendgrid' or 'smtp'), SENDGRID_API_KEY (if using SendGrid), SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, EMAIL_FROM. 3. Create a new module src/utils/email.js that: a. Loads env vars via process.env. b. Initializes the provider once. c. Exposes an… If stuck: If the AI sent only stub functions or console.log placeholders, ask it to replace them with a working SendGrid/Nodemailer implementation, reference the env vars, and include the self‑audit.
checklist: Can the project start without import errors?
Does sendMagicLink send an email via the chosen provider?
Are all env vars defined and used?

tactics.title: Add Magic‑Link Passwordless Login: Create Magic‑Link Token Store
tactics.body: Persist generated tokens securely and enforce expiration. Checklist: Does the migration run without errors?; Can you store and retrieve a token via the model?; Is the self‑audit PASSing? 1. Write a new migration file (e.g., migrations/20231101_create_magic_links.sql) that creates a table magic_links with columns: - id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY - user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE - token_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL (store a bcrypt/crypto hash of the raw token) - expires_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL - created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP 2. Add a corresponding down migration… If stuck: When the AI provides an incomplete migration or uses dummy DB calls, force it to write a proper SQL file and real model functions with hashing and expiration logic.
checklist: Does the migration run without errors?
Can you store and retrieve a token via the model?
Is the self‑audit PASSing?

tactics.title: Add Magic‑Link Passwordless Login: Implement Magic‑Link Request Endpoint
tactics.body: Generate a token, store it, and email the link to the user. Checklist: Can you POST to /auth/magic and receive the generic JSON message?; Is a new row in magic_links created?; Did an email arrive (or mock capture) with a proper verification link? 1. In src/routes/auth.js, add a new route handler for POST /auth/magic that expects JSON { email }. 2. Validate the email format; return 400 if invalid. 3. Query the users table for a matching email; if not found, respond with 200 but do NOT disclose existence (security best practice). 4. If a user is found: a. Generate a cryptographically secure random token (32 bytes, base64url). b. Call… If stuck: When the AI gives dummy code or skips DB insertion, demand a working endpoint that uses crypto, stores the hash, and calls the real email helper.
checklist: Can you POST to /auth/magic and receive the generic JSON message?
Is a new row in magic_links created?
Did an email arrive (or mock capture) with a proper verification link?

tactics.title: Add Magic‑Link Passwordless Login: Implement Magic‑Link Verification Endpoint
tactics.body: Validate the token, create a session, and log the user in. Checklist: Can you visit the magic‑verify URL and receive a Set‑Cookie header?; Is the JWT valid and contains the correct user ID?; Is the token removed from the database? 1. In src/routes/auth.js, add a GET /auth/magic-verify handler that reads the query parameter token. 2. Validate token presence; if missing, respond 400. 3. Call magicLink.findValidToken(token). If no record, respond 400 with generic error. 4. If a valid record is found: a. Retrieve the associated user via its user_id. b. Generate a JWT containing { sub: user.id, email: user.email, iat, exp: now+1h } signed with… If stuck: When the AI skips JWT generation or cookie setting, force it to add those steps with real secret usage and self‑audit.
checklist: Can you visit the magic‑verify URL and receive a Set‑Cookie header?
Is the JWT valid and contains the correct user ID?
Is the token removed from the database?

tactics.title: Add Magic‑Link Passwordless Login: Add Front‑End Magic‑Link UI
tactics.body: Give users a way to request a magic link from the login page. Checklist: Can you enter an email and click Send Magic Link?; Is a network request made and does the page show the generic success message?; Does the Cypress test confirm the flow? 1. Identify the login view/template (e.g., views/login.ejs or src/components/Login.jsx). 2. Insert a new form section: - Input type="email" name="email" required placeholder="you@example.com". - Submit button labeled "Send Magic Link". 3. For EJS: set the form action="/auth/magic" method="POST" and include a hidden CSRF token if the app uses one. For React: add a component with state for email, onSubmit calls… If stuck: When UI code lacks proper form submission or feedback, ask for a complete, wired-up implementation with fetch or form action and the success handler.
checklist: Can you enter an email and click Send Magic Link?
Is a network request made and does the page show the generic success message?
Does the Cypress test confirm the flow?

tactics.title: Add Magic‑Link Passwordless Login: End‑to‑End Verification & Cleanup
tactics.body: Confirm the full passwordless flow works and remove any temporary test code. Checklist: Can the automated test run end‑to‑end without mocks?; Is the user authenticated via JWT after clicking the link?; Is the token removed from the DB?; Is the API documentation updated? 1. In tests/e2e/magicLink.test.js, write a full flow using supertest (for API) and a Mailtrap client library: a. POST /auth/magic with a known user email. b. Poll Mailtrap inbox for the latest email, extract the verification URL from the email body. c. GET the extracted URL (follow redirects) using supertest. d. Assert the response sets an "auth_token" HttpOnly cookie and redirects to the dashboard. e. Decode the… If stuck: When the AI provides a stub test or skips real email, demand a genuine integration test using Mailtrap and full JWT verification.
checklist: Can the automated test run end‑to‑end without mocks?
Is the user authenticated via JWT after clicking the link?
Is the token removed from the DB?
Is the API documentation updated?

tactics.title: Make UI Less Generic: Audit the generic tells
tactics.body: Name exactly what makes the app look AI-default. Checklist: Fonts, colors, icons, and copy all audited; Each tell has a concrete location; An honest genericness score is given Audit the UI and list every 'AI slop' tell with its location: default system/Inter-only fonts, purple/pink or rainbow gradients, emoji used as icons, identical rounded-card grids, default shadcn/bootstrap look, placeholder copy, inconsistent spacing, missing hover/focus states. Rate the overall genericness 1-10 with justification and screenshot references. If stuck: The audit is vague ('looks generic'). Re-audit tell by tell: name the exact fonts in use, list every gradient, and locate each emoji-icon and placeholder string.
checklist: Fonts, colors, icons, and copy all audited
Each tell has a concrete location
An honest genericness score is given

tactics.title: Make UI Less Generic: Define the visual direction
tactics.body: You cannot restyle toward nothing - pick a direction with tokens. Checklist: Fonts are named with weights; Colors are exact values, not vibes; The direction fits the product's audience Define a distinct visual direction appropriate to this product and audience. Deliver: a direction name and one-line mood (e.g. 'technical command center', 'warm editorial', 'brutalist minimal'); a font pairing (heading + body, from Google Fonts, with weights); a color system (background, surface, text hierarchy, ONE accent, semantic states) as concrete tokens/CSS variables; spacing scale and radius/border/shadow… If stuck: The direction is adjectives without tokens. Convert it into exact font names, hex/HSL values, spacing units, and radius rules before touching any component.
checklist: Fonts are named with weights
Colors are exact values, not vibes
The direction fits the product's audience

tactics.title: Make UI Less Generic: Apply the foundation
tactics.body: Install tokens globally: fonts, colors, spacing - the base coat. Checklist: Headings render the new font (verify computed styles); Old gradients are gone everywhere; All pages walked with no layout regressions Apply the foundation app-wide. Requirements: load and apply the font pairing (headings and body actually change); replace the color system at the token/theme level so all components inherit it; remove every generic gradient in favor of the new system; normalize spacing to the scale; verify no layout breaks by walking all pages after. If stuck: Some views kept old tokens or broke. Apply changes at the theme/root level rather than per-component, and fix the specific regressed layouts.
checklist: Headings render the new font (verify computed styles)
Old gradients are gone everywhere
All pages walked with no layout regressions

tactics.title: Make UI Less Generic: Restyle key components
tactics.body: The identity lives in the details: cards, buttons, forms, nav. Checklist: Buttons show a clear visual hierarchy; All emoji icons replaced; Focus states are visible and on-brand Restyle the core components to the direction: buttons (hierarchy of primary/secondary/ghost with distinct hover/active/focus states), cards (borders, elevation, padding per the tokens), forms (inputs, focus rings, error styling), navigation (active states, structure), and replace every emoji-icon with the chosen icon set at consistent sizes. Keep behavior identical - style only. If stuck: Components are inconsistently styled across pages. Restyle at the shared-component level (the button component, not each usage) so every instance updates together.
checklist: Buttons show a clear visual hierarchy
All emoji icons replaced
Focus states are visible and on-brand

tactics.title: Make UI Less Generic: Add micro-interactions and final sweep
tactics.body: Deliberate motion and a last pass separate polished from generic. Checklist: Transitions are specific-property, not transition-all; Placeholder copy is gone; Core journey still works end to end Add polish. Requirements: hover transitions on interactive elements (150-250ms, specific properties - never transition:all), entrance treatment for primary content, satisfying press/active states, and skeletons/spinners matching the new identity. Then do the final sweep: rewrite placeholder copy into real product voice, check spacing rhythm page by page, and re-rate the genericness score with before/after… If stuck: Polish broke function or motion feels random. Remove transitions from transforms causing breakage, keep durations consistent, and re-run the core journey to confirm behavior.
checklist: Transitions are specific-property, not transition-all
Placeholder copy is gone
Core journey still works end to end

tactics.title: Marketplace Buyer/Seller Flow: Define marketplace entities and rules
tactics.body: Two-sided products fail without clear roles and states - define them first. Checklist: Listing and order models are fully fielded; Order status flow is enumerated; Ownership and visibility rules are stated Define the marketplace spec. Specify: the listing model (title, description, price, images, category, status, seller id); the order/request model (listing, buyer, seller, status flow e.g. pending -> accepted -> completed / declined); user roles (any user can be both buyer and seller, or separate roles - decide); and rules: sellers cannot order own listings, only sellers edit their listings, only the two parties see… If stuck: The spec lacks an order status flow or ownership rules. Add the explicit status transitions and who can do what on each entity.
checklist: Listing and order models are fully fielded
Order status flow is enumerated
Ownership and visibility rules are stated

tactics.title: Marketplace Buyer/Seller Flow: Build seller listing management
tactics.body: Supply side first: sellers must create and manage real listings. Checklist: Created listing survives refresh; My-listings shows only my items; Unpublish hides it from public browse Implement seller listing management. Requirements: a create-listing form (title, description, price, category, image URL) with validation; listings persisted with the seller's user id; a 'my listings' view showing only the seller's items with edit and publish/unpublish; edits persist; loading, empty, and error states. Verify persistence with a refresh after each operation. If stuck: Listings vanish on refresh or show for the wrong seller. Persist listings with sellerId in the database and filter the my-listings query by the authenticated user.
checklist: Created listing survives refresh
My-listings shows only my items
Unpublish hides it from public browse

tactics.title: Marketplace Buyer/Seller Flow: Build public browse and search
tactics.body: Demand side: buyers must find listings through real queries. Checklist: Search narrows to matching listings; Filters and sort work server-side; Unpublished listings are hidden; Empty and loading states render Implement the public marketplace browse. Requirements: a grid of published listings from a backend query; text search across title and description; category filter and price sort applied server-side; pagination or load-more; listing cards showing image, title, price, seller name; empty state for no matches; loading skeletons. Unpublished listings must never appear. If stuck: Browse renders all listings from a static array. Query published listings from the backend with search/filter/sort parameters and re-fetch on change.
checklist: Search narrows to matching listings
Filters and sort work server-side
Unpublished listings are hidden
Empty and loading states render

tactics.title: Marketplace Buyer/Seller Flow: Build listing detail with order action
tactics.step_title: Build listing detail with order action
tactics.body: The transaction moment: a real order must be created, with rules enforced. Checklist: Order appears in the database with correct parties; Own-listing ordering is blocked; Logged-out users are redirected to login; Duplicate pending order is prevented Implement the listing detail page and order placement. Requirements: full listing details with seller info; an Order/Request button that creates a real order record (listing, buyer, seller, status=pending) via the backend; the button is disabled with an explanatory note on your own listings; logged-out users are prompted to log in; success shows confirmation and links to 'my orders'; failures show visible errors.… If stuck: The order button only shows a toast. Create the order record via the backend, enforce own-listing and duplicate rules server-side, and route the buyer to their orders.
checklist: Order appears in the database with correct parties
Own-listing ordering is blocked
Logged-out users are redirected to login
Duplicate pending order is prevented

tactics.title: Marketplace Buyer/Seller Flow: Build buyer and seller order dashboards
tactics.step_title: Build buyer and seller order dashboards
tactics.body: Both sides must track the same order truthfully through its lifecycle. Checklist: Seller accept changes status for the buyer too; Only sellers can change status; Non-party users cannot fetch the order; Empty states render for new accounts Implement order management for both sides. Requirements: buyers see 'my orders' with listing, seller, status, and date; sellers see 'incoming orders' with buyer and actions to accept/decline pending orders and mark accepted ones completed; every status change persists and is immediately visible to the other side on refresh; status badges are color-coded; both lists have loading and empty states. Enforce that only… If stuck: Status changes are local-only or anyone can accept orders. Persist transitions via backend endpoints that verify the acting user is the seller, and re-fetch on both dashboards.
checklist: Seller accept changes status for the buyer too
Only sellers can change status
Non-party users cannot fetch the order
Empty states render for new accounts

tactics.title: Marketplace Buyer/Seller Flow: Marketplace end-to-end test
tactics.body: Prove the full two-sided loop with two real accounts. Checklist: Full loop executed with two accounts; Third account is fully isolated; Statuses consistent after refresh on both sides; All failures fixed Run the full two-account test and report PASS/FAIL with evidence: account A creates a listing; account B finds it via search, orders it; A sees the incoming order and accepts; B sees the accepted status; A completes it; both histories are correct after refresh; A cannot order A's own listing; a third account C sees none of these orders. Fix every failure and re-run. If stuck: The loop was tested with one account or without refreshes. Re-run with separate buyer/seller accounts, refresh at each stage, and fix any state that does not propagate.
checklist: Full loop executed with two accounts
Third account is fully isolated
Statuses consistent after refresh on both sides
All failures fixed

tactics.title: Memory Consolidation and Pruning Schedule: Split memory into layers
tactics.body: Different lifetimes deserve different homes. Checklist: Migration rules applied and logged; New writes route by evidence type; Session loading reflects the layer split Restructure the memory store into two layers. WORKING: entries from recent sessions (default: last 14 days or last 5 sessions), loaded eagerly, expected to be noisy. LONG-TERM: consolidated entries with provenance, loaded via index/recall. Migrate the existing store: entries confirmed more than once or user-stated go to long-term; the rest goes to working with their dates. Update write paths (new observations land… If stuck: Everything migrated to one layer. Re-check the rules: the split keys off evidence and confirmation, not just age - a day-old user-stated preference belongs in long-term.
checklist: Migration rules applied and logged
New writes route by evidence type
Session loading reflects the layer split

tactics.title: Memory Consolidation and Pruning Schedule: Implement the consolidation run
tactics.body: Promotion with merging is where memory earns its keep. Checklist: Promotion threshold is evidence-based; Merges cite both sources; Unique-fact preservation verified Build the consolidation job (triggered at session end or on a schedule). Steps: (1) gather working entries past the promotion threshold (re-observed, or referenced in a successful task); (2) for each, search long-term for related entries; (3) merge: combine overlapping semantics into a single best phrasing, keep the union of unique facts, update provenance to cite both sources, supersede the old versions with… If stuck: A merge dropped a unique detail. Add a post-merge check: every noun phrase and identifier from the source entries must appear in the merged result or in an explicit 'dropped as ephemeral' list in the report.
checklist: Promotion threshold is evidence-based
Merges cite both sources
Unique-fact preservation verified

tactics.title: Memory Consolidation and Pruning Schedule: Add decay scoring and safe pruning
tactics.step_title: Add decay scoring and safe pruning
tactics.body: Forgetting is a feature when it has a paper trail. Checklist: Decay uses recall-log data; Protected classes exempt; Restore-from-archive works by ID and search Implement decay and pruning. Decay score per long-term entry from: age since last_confirmed, recall frequency (from the recall log), and contradiction events (each hit lowers it). Below a threshold, entries become prune candidates - EXCEPT protected classes (user preferences, security-relevant warnings) which never auto-prune. Pruning moves candidates to an archive file with full metadata; a restore command brings… If stuck: Pruning nominated something important. Add its class to the protected list AND note why the decay score misjudged it (usually missing recall-log integration) - fix the signal, not just the instance.
checklist: Decay uses recall-log data
Protected classes exempt
Restore-from-archive works by ID and search

tactics.title: Memory Consolidation and Pruning Schedule: Track health over simulated months
tactics.body: Prove the lifecycle keeps the store good, not just small. Checklist: Probe-set precision tracked across runs; Working layer stays bounded; Verdict backed by the timeline data Build health metrics and run the longevity simulation. Metrics (computed per consolidation run): total entries per layer, duplicate rate (near-duplicate detection sample), average entry age, recall precision on a fixed probe set (10 standing queries with known-correct answers). Simulation: script 8 weeks of daily sessions (scripted writes and recalls with realistic noise), running the full lifecycle throughout.… If stuck: Probe precision decays over the simulation. Bisect the cause: if right memories were pruned, adjust decay weights; if consolidation mangled them, strengthen the merge checks; re-run the simulation after each fix.
checklist: Probe-set precision tracked across runs
Working layer stays bounded
Verdict backed by the timeline data

tactics.title: Memory Recall: Ranking and Relevance: Build the lexical layer
tactics.body: Exact matches are the floor of trustworthy recall. Checklist: Identifier-aware tokenization; Quoted phrases match exactly; Exact-name tests hit at rank 1 Implement lexical search over memory entries. Requirements: tokenize entries and queries (lowercase, split identifiers on common separators so auth_handler matches 'auth handler'); score with BM25 (use SQLite FTS5 or a small library - do not hand-roll unless trivial); support quoted exact-phrase matching for error strings; return top-K with matched terms highlighted per result. Test with queries that MUST work… If stuck: Exact file names miss. Check tokenization of paths and identifiers - index both the raw token (auth_handler.py) and its split parts (auth, handler, py).
checklist: Identifier-aware tokenization
Quoted phrases match exactly
Exact-name tests hit at rank 1

tactics.title: Memory Recall: Ranking and Relevance: Add the semantic layer
tactics.body: Paraphrase reach without surrendering to it. Checklist: Vectors written at memory-write time; Existing store migrated; Paraphrase tests pass Add embedding-based recall. Requirements: embed each memory entry (content plus topic keywords) at write time and store vectors alongside entries (a simple array store or SQLite sidecar is fine at this scale); embed queries at recall time; score by cosine similarity, return top-K. Batch-embed the existing store as a migration. Test with paraphrase queries: 'how do we deploy this' should find the entry about the… If stuck: Semantic results are generic. Embed entries WITH their topic context (prepend the section/topic name to the text) - bare one-liners often embed poorly.
checklist: Vectors written at memory-write time
Existing store migrated
Paraphrase tests pass

tactics.title: Memory Recall: Ranking and Relevance: Fuse rankings with boosts
tactics.body: Two imperfect rankers, one good one. Checklist: RRF implemented with boosts; Score breakdowns retained; Precision@3 comparison reported Implement rank fusion. Use reciprocal rank fusion: for each result, score = sum over methods of 1/(k + rank_in_method) with k=60 default; then apply multiplicative boosts: recency (entries confirmed in the last 30 days x1.2), confidence (high x1.2, low x0.8), and access frequency (frequently-recalled entries get a small boost, capped). Return fused top-K (default 5) with per-result score breakdowns retained. Build… If stuck: Fusion underperforms one method. Check rank alignment bugs (both rankers must rank the same entry IDs) and tune k and boost weights on the labeled set - but keep the set as the honest referee.
checklist: RRF implemented with boosts
Score breakdowns retained
Precision@3 comparison reported

tactics.title: Memory Recall: Ranking and Relevance: Make retrieval explainable
tactics.body: When recall misfires, you need to see why in one glance. Checklist: Explanations show terms, scores, and boosts; Recall log captures every query; One misfire fixed via its explanation Add explainability and integrate with the agent. Each recalled memory returns: content, metadata, and an explanation line - e.g. 'matched: [deploy, script] (bm25 rank 2) + semantic 0.81 (rank 1); boosts: recency x1.2 -> final rank 1'. Integrate recall into the agent as a memory_search tool whose results render these explanations, and log every recall (query, results, explanations) to a recall log. Finish with a… If stuck: Explanations are too cryptic to act on. Render them in words, not raw floats - name the matched terms and the deciding boost, since the audience is a debugging human.
checklist: Explanations show terms, scores, and boosts
Recall log captures every query
One misfire fixed via its explanation

tactics.title: Memory Write Policies: Write the memorability criteria
tactics.body: The gate is a checklist, not a vibe. Checklist: Memorable and not-memorable lists concrete; Secrets hard-blocked; 10-candidate test matches expectations Define the write gate. MEMORABLE: durable project facts, user preferences stated or clearly implied, decisions with reasons, working recipes verified by success, failures with diagnosed causes. NOT MEMORABLE: ephemeral state (current file open), one-off values, anything reconstructible from the code in seconds, speculation, and secrets (hard block: credentials never enter memory). For each memorable type define… If stuck: The gate passes junk. Make rejection reasons specific in the tool response ('rejected: ephemeral state') so you can audit which criterion is leaking, then tighten it.
checklist: Memorable and not-memorable lists concrete
Secrets hard-blocked
10-candidate test matches expectations

tactics.title: Memory Write Policies: Attach provenance and confidence
tactics.body: A memory without provenance is a rumor. Checklist: Schema enforced on new writes; Evidence types drive initial confidence; Existing entries backfilled honestly Extend the memory entry schema with metadata: {content, type, provenance: {session_id, date, evidence: 'user-stated' | 'observed-success' | 'observed-failure' | 'inferred'}, confidence: high | medium | low, last_confirmed}. Rules: user-stated preferences and observed successes/failures start high; inferences start low; confidence rises when a later session re-confirms (update last_confirmed) and falls when related… If stuck: Everything is marked high confidence. Audit the evidence field: 'inferred' can never start high - if the model cannot cite where a fact came from, it is an inference.
checklist: Schema enforced on new writes
Evidence types drive initial confidence
Existing entries backfilled honestly

tactics.title: Memory Write Policies: Detect and resolve contradictions
tactics.body: Two contradicting memories is a bug with a deadline. Checklist: Conflict check runs on every write; Supersede keeps an audit trail; Disputed entries flagged for the user Implement contradiction handling on the write path. Before storing, compare the new entry against same-type entries (normalized keyword overlap, or an LLM check for semantic conflict on candidates). On conflict: (a) if the new entry has stronger evidence, supersede - archive the old entry with a superseded_by link; (b) if weaker, reject the write citing the existing entry; (c) if equal and incompatible, store the… If stuck: Conflicts slip through unmatched. Improve candidate selection: compare within type AND topic (index the entries by topic keywords) so 'uses npm' and 'uses yarn' actually meet in the comparison.
checklist: Conflict check runs on every write
Supersede keeps an audit trail
Disputed entries flagged for the user

tactics.title: Memory Write Policies: Add quarantine and prove write quality
tactics.step_title: Add quarantine and prove write quality
tactics.body: Single observations are hypotheses, not facts. Checklist: Promotion requires a second observation; TTL expiry works; Final store audit shows only justified entries Implement quarantine and run the quality test. Quarantine: low-confidence writes go to a pending area excluded from default session loading; a second consistent observation promotes them to the main store (evidence upgraded); a contradicting observation deletes them; entries idle past a TTL (default 14 days) expire. Quality test: run a scripted week of sessions producing 30 candidate writes seeded with trivia, one… If stuck: Quarantined items leak into session context. Check the loader's filter - pending entries must be excluded everywhere except an explicit 'review pending memories' command.
checklist: Promotion requires a second observation
TTL expiry works
Final store audit shows only justified entries

tactics.title: Mobile QA Checklist: Layout pass at phone widths
tactics.body: Find every layout break at real device sizes. Checklist: Both widths checked on every page; Overflow sources identified precisely; Modals and menus were opened Run the mobile layout pass at exactly 375px and 414px using device emulation. For every page and modal, record: horizontal overflow (and the offending element via inspect), overlapping or cut-off content, text below readable size, broken grids/cards, images overflowing, and sticky elements covering content. Produce the per-page issue table. Interact while checking - open menus, expand sections, trigger modals. If stuck: The pass was screenshot-only and missed interactive breaks. Redo it interacting with every expandable, modal, and menu at both widths.
checklist: Both widths checked on every page
Overflow sources identified precisely
Modals and menus were opened

tactics.title: Mobile QA Checklist: Fix layout breaks
tactics.body: Make every page flow correctly in a single column. Checklist: Zero horizontal scroll remains; Tables have a deliberate mobile strategy; Modals fit the viewport Fix every layout issue from the table. Requirements: kill all horizontal overflow (fluid widths, wrapping, single-column collapses); restack multi-column sections sensibly; scale typography and spacing for small screens; give tables an explicit strategy (own-container scroll or card restack); constrain modals to the viewport with internal scroll. Re-verify each fixed page at 375px showing zero horizontal scroll. If stuck: Overflow persists somewhere. Use devtools to find the widest element on each failing page, fix its width behavior, and re-check.
checklist: Zero horizontal scroll remains
Tables have a deliberate mobile strategy
Modals fit the viewport

tactics.title: Mobile QA Checklist: Touch and gesture pass
tactics.body: Fingers are not cursors - verify tap targets and touch behavior. Checklist: Tap targets meet 44px with spacing; No hover-only functionality remains; All destinations reachable via mobile nav Run the touch pass. Verify: every button, link, icon, and control hits at least 44x44px effective tap area with breathing room from neighbors; hover-only interactions (tooltips, menus, reveals) have tap equivalents; swipe/scroll areas do not fight page scroll; the mobile navigation reaches every destination; nothing important hides behind precise hover states. Fix all violations and list the changes. If stuck: Tiny targets and hover traps remain. Enlarge tap areas via padding and convert hover reveals to tap-toggles, then retap-test each.
checklist: Tap targets meet 44px with spacing
No hover-only functionality remains
All destinations reachable via mobile nav

tactics.title: Mobile QA Checklist: Keyboard and input pass
tactics.body: The on-screen keyboard breaks more mobile apps than anything else. Checklist: Input types match content; Focused fields stay visible; Submit reachable with keyboard open Run the input pass with the on-screen keyboard simulated/considered. Verify: inputs use correct types (email, number, tel) for the right keyboards; focused inputs are not covered by the keyboard (page scrolls to them); submit buttons remain reachable with the keyboard open; validation messages are visible near the field; no zoom-jump on focus (font-size at least 16px on inputs); multi-field forms are navigable… If stuck: The keyboard covers fields or submit. Scroll focused inputs into view, keep actions reachable (sticky or above keyboard), and set input font-size to prevent zoom-jumps.
checklist: Input types match content
Focused fields stay visible
Submit reachable with keyboard open

tactics.title: Mobile QA Checklist: Core journey on mobile
tactics.body: The final proof: complete the app's main task entirely on a phone-sized screen. Checklist: The full journey was executed at 375px; Failures fixed and journey re-run; Friction notes recorded and top ones fixed Execute the app's complete core journey at 375px, end to end, as a real user: from landing through the primary value action to the result, including any signup, forms, and confirmations. Record PASS/FAIL per step with friction notes (extra taps, confusing moments, slow loads). Fix all failures, then re-run the journey clean. Deliver the final journey report. If stuck: The journey was sampled, not completed. Run it start to finish in one session at 375px and fix every blocker before re-running.
checklist: The full journey was executed at 375px
Failures fixed and journey re-run
Friction notes recorded and top ones fixed

tactics.title: MongoDB Data Model Plan: List the access patterns
tactics.body: MongoDB models are chosen by queries - enumerate them first. Checklist: Every screen's data needs appear; Filters and sorts are specified; Patterns are ranked by frequency List my app's data access patterns. I will describe the app below. Produce a table: every read pattern (what screen/feature, what it fetches, how filtered/sorted, expected volume) and every write pattern (what creates/updates what, how often). Rank by frequency. These patterns - not entity purity - will drive the model. MY APP: [describe here] If stuck: The patterns are vague. For each screen write the exact question the database must answer ('newest 20 items for user X where status=active').
checklist: Every screen's data needs appear
Filters and sorts are specified
Patterns are ranked by frequency

tactics.title: MongoDB Data Model Plan: Decide embed vs reference
tactics.body: The core MongoDB decision, made per relationship with reasoning. Checklist: Each relationship has a stated reason; No unbounded embedded arrays; Owner and timestamp fields present Design the collections. For each relationship decide embed vs reference using: read-together data embeds (if bounded and owned); independently-queried, unbounded, or shared data references. Document each decision with its reason and the risk if wrong. Define every collection's document shape with field types, the owner field (userId) on user data, and createdAt/updatedAt. If stuck: An embedded array can grow unboundedly (comments, logs). Move it to its own referenced collection queried by parent id.
checklist: Each relationship has a stated reason
No unbounded embedded arrays
Owner and timestamp fields present

tactics.title: MongoDB Data Model Plan: Plan the indexes
tactics.body: Every frequent query gets an index - designed, not guessed. Checklist: Each frequent pattern has an index; Compound order follows equality-then-sort; Unique constraints identified Plan the indexes from the access patterns: for each frequent query define the index (compound where filter+sort combine - equality fields first, then sort fields), unique indexes for natural keys (email, slug), and any text index needed for search. State which pattern each index serves. Flag queries that would still scan and adjust the model or index. If stuck: List queries would still collection-scan. Add the compound index matching their filter+sort, and verify with an explain plan once implemented.
checklist: Each frequent pattern has an index
Compound order follows equality-then-sort
Unique constraints identified

tactics.title: MongoDB Data Model Plan: Implement with validation
tactics.body: Create the collections, indexes, and a validation layer. Checklist: Index creation is idempotent on startup; Malformed writes are rejected; Dates and ids serialize cleanly through the API Implement the model: create indexes on startup (idempotent); implement validation - either application-level schemas (e.g. Pydantic models) validating every write, or MongoDB JSON Schema validators on the collections (choose and justify); ensure ObjectId/UUID and datetime handling is consistent (serialization-safe for the API); write one create+read per collection proving the shape round-trips. If stuck: Malformed documents insert fine. Add the validation layer at the chosen level and re-test with a bad document - it must reject with a clear error.
checklist: Index creation is idempotent on startup
Malformed writes are rejected
Dates and ids serialize cleanly through the API

tactics.title: MongoDB Data Model Plan: Test against real queries
tactics.body: Prove the model with the app's actual operations at realistic volume. Checklist: Every pattern was executed; Explain plans show index usage; Final model documented Test the model: run every access pattern from step 1 against the implemented collections (with a few hundred seeded documents for realism); verify results, sort orders, and user scoping; check explain plans on the heavy queries (indexes used, no full scans); document the final model (collections, shapes, indexes, validation) as the schema reference. If stuck: Some queries scan or return wrongly-scoped data. Fix the index or add the ownership filter, and re-run the pattern with explain until clean.
checklist: Every pattern was executed
Explain plans show index usage
Final model documented

tactics.title: Notification System: Define notification types and triggers
tactics.body: Notifications need real causes - name the events first. Checklist: Model includes recipient, read flag, and link; Each trigger names its real source event; Recipient logic is defined per event Define the notification spec. Specify: the notification model (id, recipient userId, type, title, body, link, read flag, createdAt); the 2-4 real app events that create notifications (e.g. new order received, comment on your item, system announcement) and who receives each; where each notification links to; and retention/ordering rules (newest first). If stuck: Triggers are vague ('when something happens'). Name the exact existing app events and the recipient rule for each.
checklist: Model includes recipient, read flag, and link
Each trigger names its real source event
Recipient logic is defined per event

tactics.title: Notification System: Create notifications from real events
tactics.body: Wire the triggers so real actions generate real notifications. Checklist: Performing the event creates a record for the recipient; The actor is not self-notified; Other users receive nothing Implement notification creation. Requirements: in the backend handlers of the chosen events, create the notification record for the correct recipient with type, title, body, and link; do not notify the actor about their own action; verify by performing each real event and checking the record appears for the right user and not others. If stuck: Notifications are inserted by seed scripts instead of events. Move creation into the actual event handlers and re-test with real actions from two accounts.
checklist: Performing the event creates a record for the recipient
The actor is not self-notified
Other users receive nothing

tactics.title: Notification System: Build the unread badge
tactics.body: The bell must tell the truth from the database. Checklist: Badge equals a hand-checked unread count; Zero unread hides the badge; A new event increments the badge Implement the notification bell. Requirements: a header bell icon with an unread-count badge fetched from a backend count endpoint for the logged-in user; the badge hides at zero; count refreshes on relevant navigation orperiodic polling (state the mechanism); the count must equal the database unread count exactly. If stuck: The badge is hardcoded or stale. Fetch the count from the backend per user and refresh it on the stated mechanism; verify against the database.
checklist: Badge equals a hand-checked unread count
Zero unread hides the badge
A new event increments the badge

tactics.title: Notification System: Build the notification center
tactics.body: A list users can open, scan, and click through. Checklist: Unread styling distinguishes items; Click marks read and navigates to the link; States persist after refresh Implement the notification center. Requirements: opening the bell shows a dropdown/page listing the user's notifications newest-first with title, body snippet, relative time, and read/unread styling; clicking a notification marks it read, decrements the badge, and navigates to its link; loading and empty states; pagination or sensible cap; refresh preserves all states. If stuck: Read state resets on reload or clicks go nowhere. Persist the read flag via the backend on click and use the stored link for navigation.
checklist: Unread styling distinguishes items
Click marks read and navigates to the link
States persist after refresh

tactics.title: Notification System: Add mark-all-read and polish
tactics.body: Bulk actions and edge polish make notifications livable. Checklist: Mark-all-read zeroes the badge and persists; Empty state is graceful; Long content truncates cleanly Finish the center. Requirements: a mark-all-read action persisting for all the user's unread items and zeroing the badge; per-item mark-as-read without navigating (e.g. hover action) if feasible; sensible truncation of long bodies; correct behavior at zero notifications; keyboard/escape closes the dropdown. If stuck: Mark-all-read is visual-only. Implement the backend bulk update for the user's unread notifications and refetch the list and count.
checklist: Mark-all-read zeroes the badge and persists
Empty state is graceful
Long content truncates cleanly

tactics.title: Notification System: Notification QA pass
tactics.body: Verify triggers, counts, and isolation with two accounts. Checklist: Two-account trigger test executed; Counts verified against the database; Read persistence verified via refresh; All failures fixed Run notification QA and report PASS/FAIL with evidence: account A's action notifies account B (and only B); badge counts match the database at each stage; read and mark-all-read persist across refresh; links navigate correctly; empty state renders for a fresh account; mobile layout works. Fix all failures and re-run. If stuck: QA used one account or skipped database verification. Re-run the two-account scenario checking counts and records at each step; fix mismatches.
checklist: Two-account trigger test executed
Counts verified against the database
Read persistence verified via refresh
All failures fixed

tactics.title: Add Google and GitHub OAuth Social Login: Install OAuth dependencies
tactics.flow_title: Add Google and GitHub OAuth Social Login

Open a terminal in the project root. 2. Execute `npm install passport passport-google-oauth20 passport-github2`. 3. Verify that the installation succeeded without errors. 4. tactics.title: Add Google and GitHub OAuth Social Login: Create .env entries and load them
tactics.flow_title: Add Google and GitHub OAuth Social Login
tactics.body: Store Google and GitHub client credentials securely and make them available to the app. Checklist: Does .env contain GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID?; Does .env contain GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET?; Is `require('dotenv').config();` the first line in the server entry file? 1. tactics.title: Add Google and GitHub OAuth Social Login: Configure Passport and session serialization
tactics.flow_title: Add Google and GitHub OAuth Social Login
tactics.body: Initialize Passport in the Express app and set up user serialize/deserialize logic for session persistence. Checklist: Is `app.use(passport.initialize());` present?; Is `app.use(passport.session());` present?; Do serializeUser and deserializeUser functions exist and reference User? 1. Open the main Express configuration file (e.g., app.js). 2. At the top, after loading dotenv, add `const passport = require('passport');`. 3. Immediately after the existing `app.use(session(...))` line, insert: `app.use(passport.initialize());` `app.use(passport.session());` 4. Below the middleware section, implement: `passport.serializeUser((user, done) => { done(null, user.id); });`… If stuck: The AI added the middleware but left serializeUser as a placeholder comment. Replace the placeholder with real code that stores user.id and fetches the user by ID from the database.
checklist: Is `app.use(passport.initialize());` present?
Is `app.use(passport.session());` present?
Do serializeUser and deserializeUser functions exist and reference User?

tactics.title: Add Google and GitHub OAuth Social Login: Implement Google OAuth strategy

tactics.title: Observability for Agent Runs: Instrument spans across the loop
tactics.body: The trace tree is the run's skeleton - build it first. Checklist: Hierarchy covers all loop operations; Token/cost attributes on model spans; Scrubbing verified on a seeded secret Add structured tracing to the agent. Span hierarchy: session -> task -> turn -> {model_call, tool_execution, hook_check, compaction, memory_op}. Attributes per span type: model calls get model, tier, tokens in/out, cost, latency, stop reason; tool spans get tool name, argument digest, result size, verdict; hook spans get rule and verdict. Use OpenTelemetry SDK conventions (GenAI semantic conventions where they fit)… If stuck: The tree has gaps (orphan spans, missing turns). Check context propagation - every operation must open its span inside its parent's context; async boundaries are the usual leak point.
checklist: Hierarchy covers all loop operations
Token/cost attributes on model spans
Scrubbing verified on a seeded secret

tactics.title: Observability for Agent Runs: Build session replay
tactics.body: The debugging superpower: watch the run again, slowly. Checklist: Exact model inputs visible per step; Jump-to-error works; Large payloads stored by reference Implement replay on top of the trace/event data. Store per session the ordered event stream (spans plus payload records: full prompts, responses, tool results - scrubbed, with large payloads referenced to an artifact store). Build the replay view: step through the session event by event; at each step show the model's exact input context, its output, the tool calls and results, and running token/cost totals; support… If stuck: Replay diverges from what actually ran. The stored context must be the serialized request actually sent (capture at the client wrapper), not a reconstruction - reconstructions drift from reality.
checklist: Exact model inputs visible per step
Jump-to-error works
Large payloads stored by reference

tactics.title: Observability for Agent Runs: Track the economics
tactics.body: Cost per session shapes design decisions - surface it everywhere. Checklist: Cost line in every session summary; Aggregates trend over time; Runaway alert tested mid-run Build the metrics layer. Per session compute and store: total cost, cost by call class, tokens by direction, tool-call counts, duration, and outcome (completed/escalated/cancelled). Surface: a per-session cost line in the session summary shown to the user; a periodic aggregate report (cost per task class over time, expensive-session outliers listed); alerts on runaway sessions (cost exceeding a threshold mid-run… If stuck: Costs disagree with the provider bill. Reconcile: use the provider's reported usage fields per response (not your estimates) as the source of truth, and account for cached-token pricing where applicable.
checklist: Cost line in every session summary
Aggregates trend over time
Runaway alert tested mid-run

tactics.title: Observability for Agent Runs: Run the failure-analysis drill
tactics.body: Observability proves itself on the next bad day - rehearse it. Checklist: Two failures root-caused via traces; Time-to-cause compared to log-diving; Escalated sessions auto-flag with links Establish and drill the failure workflow. WORKFLOW: failure reported -> find the session (by ID/time/user) -> open the trace tree -> jump to the failing span -> inspect the exact context and payloads via replay -> classify the root cause (bad tool result, prompt gap, permission block, model error, harness bug) -> file the fix with the trace linked. DRILL: take two real recent failures (or inject one: a tool… If stuck: The drill stalled at 'find the session'. Add the missing index - sessions searchable by time, user, task keyword, and outcome - findability is step zero of every debugging story.
checklist: Two failures root-caused via traces
Time-to-cause compared to log-diving
Escalated sessions auto-flag with links

tactics.title: Payment Flow QA: Audit the money path
tactics.body: Trace where amounts come from and who declares success. Checklist: Amount sources identified as server or client; The success authority is identified; All trust violations listed Audit the payment implementation. Trace and report: where amounts/prices are defined (must be server-side - flag any client-sent amount that the server trusts); how checkout sessions are created; who declares success (must be server verification with the provider, never the redirect alone); where payment records live and their state model; how paid access is granted. Produce the money-path diagram in text and flag… If stuck: The audit shows the client sending amounts or declaring success. Those are critical: move price lookup and success verification server-side before any further testing.
checklist: Amount sources identified as server or client
The success authority is identified
All trust violations listed

tactics.title: Payment Flow QA: Verify the success path
tactics.body: Prove a test payment grants correctly - exactly once. Checklist: The provider shows the test payment; The record flipped to paid via verification; Repeated success-page visits do not re-grant Test the success path in provider test mode: complete a purchase with the standard test card; verify the provider dashboard shows the payment; verify our payment record transitions to paid via server verification (not the redirect); verify the purchased value is granted (access/plan/credits) and visible in the UI; then refresh the success page repeatedly and re-visit the URL - the grant must not duplicate. Record… If stuck: Refreshing the success page duplicates grants. Make verification idempotent: check the record's state before granting and mark the session consumed.
checklist: The provider shows the test payment
The record flipped to paid via verification
Repeated success-page visits do not re-grant

tactics.title: Payment Flow QA: Verify decline and cancel paths
tactics.body: Failed money moments must be honest and recoverable. Checklist: Decline shows failure and grants nothing; Cancel returns cleanly with retry; No path leaves a false paid state Test the failure paths: a declined test card (the UI must show an honest failure with retry - no success theater, and no partial grant); user cancels on the provider page (clean return, record marked canceled/pending appropriately, retry available); abandonment (close the tab mid-checkout - what state remains and is it recoverable?); verify no failure path leaves the database claiming paid. Record the state after… If stuck: A declined payment still shows success or half-grants. Gate every grant on verified paid status and re-run the decline scenario to confirm.
checklist: Decline shows failure and grants nothing
Cancel returns cleanly with retry
No path leaves a false paid state

tactics.title: Payment Flow QA: Attack the payment flow
tactics.body: Try to cheat your own checkout before someone else does. Checklist: Amount tampering had no effect; Fake/reused sessions were rejected; Paid features blocked for unpaid users at the API level Attack-test the payment flow: attempt to modify the amount/product client-side (devtools request editing) - the server must price from its own catalog; attempt to call the grant/verification endpoint directly with fake or reused session ids - must reject; attempt to reach paid features as an unpaid user via direct URLs and API calls - must be blocked server-side; attempt double-submission of the same checkout -… If stuck: Tampered amounts or reused sessions got through. Price exclusively from the server catalog and validate sessions with the provider (unconsumed, matching) before any grant.
checklist: Amount tampering had no effect
Fake/reused sessions were rejected
Paid features blocked for unpaid users at the API level

tactics.title: Payment Flow QA: Reconcile states end to end
tactics.body: The final check: provider, database, and UI must tell one story. Checklist: Every test payment reconciles across all three layers; Entitlement displays match records; The final purchase documented cleanly Run the reconciliation pass: list every test payment made during QA and for each compare provider status, database record status, and what the UI shows the user - all three must agree; verify plan/entitlement displays match records; run one fresh end-to-end purchase as a final confirmation and document the full lifecycle with timestamps. Deliver the reconciliation table and any remaining known issues. If stuck: States disagree between layers. For each mismatch trace where the update failed (verification not run, record not updated, UI reading stale data) and fix the chain, then re-reconcile.
checklist: Every test payment reconciles across all three layers
Entitlement displays match records
The final purchase documented cleanly

tactics.title: Press/Announcement Page: Find the story angle
tactics.body: Coverage needs a story - the announcement is not the story. Checklist: Each angle passes 'why would a stranger care'; Supporting facts are concrete; One angle is chosen Find the press angle for my announcement. I will describe the launch/milestone below. Produce 3 candidate angles (e.g. the why-now trend it rides, the against-the-grain decision, the human origin, the surprising number) each with: the one-line pitch, why an outsider would care, and the strongest supporting fact. Recommend one primary angle and explain the choice. MY ANNOUNCEMENT: [describe here] If stuck: The angles are 'we launched a product'. Reframe around tension: what changed in the world, what everyone gets wrong, or what surprising thing the numbers show.
checklist: Each angle passes 'why would a stranger care'
Supporting facts are concrete
One angle is chosen

tactics.body: Story structure: hook, context, what is new, proof, what is next. Checklist: The hook leads with tension, not 'we're excited'; All facts are verifiable; The founder quote sounds human Write my announcement post using the chosen angle. All facts are verifiable
The founder quote sounds human

tactics.title: Pricing Page Builder: Design the plan structure

Checklist: The value metric is user-comprehensible; Each price has stated logic; Upgrade triggers are concrete Design my plan structure. I will describe the product and users below. Produce: 2-3 plans (including free tier decision with reasoning); the ONE primary value metric that scales across plans (users understand it: items, seats, volume); what each plan includes and its price with the logic; which plan is recommended and why; and the upgrade trigger - the moment a user outgrows each plan. tactics.title: Pricing Page Builder: Wire and verify the CTAs
tactics.body: The page succeeds only if the buttons complete the journey. Checklist: Each CTA was followed to completion; Leads/checkouts verifiably persist; Displayed limits match enforced limits Wire and test every pricing CTA: free plan CTA into signup (works end to end); paid plan CTAs into checkout/upgrade if billing exists, or a waitlist/contact capture that actually stores the lead (verify persistence); logged-in users see context-aware CTAs (current plan marked, upgrade paths only); verify the in-product limits actually match the displayed plan limits.
