tactics.title: Settings/Billing Page: Settings QA pass
tactics.body: Verify every control persists and every risk path is safe. Checklist: Re-login persistence checked per field; Password rotation double-checked; Deletion verified with a blocked login; All failures fixed Run settings QA and report PASS/FAIL with evidence: each profile field persists across re-login; duplicate email blocked; password rotation verified both directions; every preference survives refresh; upgrade CTA works; delete flow blocks re-login; all forms validated; mobile layout at 375px. Fix all failures and re-run. If stuck: QA only clicked Save without verifying persistence. Re-verifyevery control with refresh and re-login, and fix any control that reverts.
checklist: Re-login persistence checked per field
Password rotation double-checked
Deletion verified with a blocked login
All failures fixed

tactics.title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design: Analyze the workload for separability
tactics.flow_title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design
tactics.body: The architecture question is really a workload question. Checklist: All five questions answered with specifics; Shared-state needs are named explicitly; Budgets are numbers, not adjectives Analyze my agent workload before choosing an architecture. Answer in writing: (1) Can the work be split into subtasks that do NOT need to share intermediate state? (2) Do subtasks need different tool sets or different permission levels? (3) Is there a natural review/producer split where one context should not contaminate the other? (4) What are my latency and cost budgets per task? (5) What is the blast radius if… If stuck: The analysis is generic. Redo it against three real example tasks from my domain, tracing exactly what state each subtask reads and writes.
checklist: All five questions answered with specifics
Shared-state needs are named explicitly
Budgets are numbers, not adjectives

tactics.title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design: Score the three architectures
tactics.flow_title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design
tactics.body: Make the trade-offs visible before intuition locks in. Checklist: All 21 cells scored with reasons; Debuggability and failure containment included; Winner follows from scores, not vibes Build a decision matrix scoring three architectures against my workload profile: (A) single-loop agent with tools; (B) single main agent with dispatched sub-agents for bounded research/review tasks; (C) full multi-agent with peer roles and message passing. Score each 1-5 on: implementation complexity, debuggability, context efficiency, failure containment, latency, cost, and fit to my separability answers. Research… If stuck: The matrix was backfilled to justify a pre-made choice. Have a hostile reviewer pass: for each score that favors the winner, write the strongest counter-argument, then re-score.
checklist: All 21 cells scored with reasons
Debuggability and failure containment included
Winner follows from scores, not vibes

tactics.title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design: Sketch the chosen architecture
tactics.flow_title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design
tactics.body: A design you can draw is a design you can build and debug. Checklist: Every arrow has a message format; State ownership is single-writer; Each component has a failure story Produce the architecture sketch for the winning option. Must include: components (agents, tools, stores), the exact communication paths (who sends what to whom, in what format), where state lives and who owns writes, the failure story for each component (timeout, garbage output, crash), and the observability plan (transcripts, correlation IDs across agents). If multi-agent: define the coordination protocol… If stuck: The sketch says 'agents collaborate' without mechanics. Replace every vague verb with a concrete message: who sends it, its schema, and what the receiver does on timeout or invalid payload.
checklist: Every arrow has a message format
State ownership is single-writer
Each component has a failure story

tactics.title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design: Define revisit triggers and validate cheaply
tactics.flow_title: Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent: Decide and Design
tactics.step_title: Define revisit triggers and validate cheaply
tactics.body: Architectures are bets - set the tripwires that tell you the bet went bad. Checklist: Triggers are measurable, not moods; Spike targeted the riskiest interaction; Spike result recorded honestly Finish the decision responsibly. (1) Define revisit triggers: measurable conditions under which I would re-run this decision (e.g. context regularly exceeding 70% budget, task mix shifting to parallel-friendly work, quality plateau attributable to context contamination). (2) Design the cheapest possible validation: a one-day spike implementing the riskiest interaction in the chosen design (for sub-agents: dispatch… If stuck: The spike tested the easy path. Re-run it with the failure case: inject a garbage report or a stalled worker and verify the design's failure story actually plays out as drawn.
checklist: Triggers are measurable, not moods
Spike targeted the riskiest interaction
Spike result recorded honestly

tactics.title: Streaming and Partial-Result UX: Design the event protocol
tactics.body: Streaming without structure is just faster confusion. Checklist: All lifecycle events covered; Sequence numbers and timestamps included; Transport choice justified Design a typed streaming event protocol for the agent. Event types to include: run_started {run_id}, text_delta {content}, tool_started {call_id, tool, args_summary}, tool_progress {call_id, note} (optional heartbeats), tool_finished {call_id, ok, result_summary}, turn_completed {turn}, run_completed {status, usage}, run_error {message}, run_cancelled {partial: bool}. Each event carries a sequence number and… If stuck: The design streams raw text with markers spliced in. Replace it with typed events - clients must switch on event.type, never regex the stream.
checklist: All lifecycle events covered
Sequence numbers and timestamps included
Transport choice justified

tactics.title: Streaming and Partial-Result UX: Implement server-side streaming
tactics.body: Wire the loop's inner moments to the event stream. Checklist: Text deltas forwarded, not buffered; Tool events bracket each execution; Heartbeats cover long tool runs Implement streaming in the backend loop. Requirements: use the model API's streaming mode and forward text deltas as text_delta events as they arrive; emit tool_started before each tool executes with a compact args summary (never full file contents); emit tool_finished with ok/failed and a one-line result summary; for tools that run over 5 seconds, emit tool_progress heartbeats; emit run_completed with token usage… If stuck: Events arrive in one burst at the end. Check for response buffering in the server or proxy (disable gzip/buffering for the SSE route, flush after each event) and confirm the model call truly uses streaming mode.
checklist: Text deltas forwarded, not buffered
Tool events bracket each execution
Heartbeats cover long tool runs

tactics.title: Streaming and Partial-Result UX: Build the streaming client rendering
tactics.body: Users should watch the agent work the way they watch a colleague type. Checklist: Sequence order drives rendering; Tool lines show running/success/failure states; Auto-scroll yields to user scroll Implement client rendering of the stream. Requirements: model text renders progressively token by token; tool activity renders as compact status lines (spinner while running, check or cross on completion, expandable to see the result summary); text and tool lines interleave in true chronological order using the sequence numbers; auto-scroll follows output unless the user scrolls up (then a 'jump to latest'… If stuck: The UI jumbles text and tool events. Render strictly by sequence number from a single ordered buffer instead of maintaining separate text and tool panes.
checklist: Sequence order drives rendering
Tool lines show running/success/failure states
Auto-scroll yields to user scroll

tactics.title: Streaming and Partial-Result UX: Implement safe interruption
tactics.body: Cancel is a feature, not an emergency stop. Checklist: Flag checked at safe boundaries; Mutating tools complete or roll back; Partial summary rendered to the user Add interruption. Requirements: a cancel control sends a stop request with the run ID; the server sets a cancellation flag checked between turns and between tool executions; in-flight generation is aborted at the API level where supported; tools that mutate state must complete or roll back - never abandon a half-applied edit (finish the current write, skip the rest); the server emits run_cancelled {partial: true}… If stuck: Cancel left a file half-written. Make writes atomic (write temp file, then rename) so any interruption leaves either the old or the new content, never a hybrid.
checklist: Flag checked at safe boundaries
Mutating tools complete or roll back
Partial summary rendered to the user

tactics.title: Stripe Checkout Flow: Define the payment spec
tactics.body: Lock what is being sold, prices, and payment states before touching Stripe. Checklist: Products and exact prices are listed; One-time vs subscription is decided; Payment states are enumerated; Server-side confirmation is stated as a rule Define the payment spec for this app. Specify: what is being sold (one-time purchase or subscription plans with exact prices and currency), the payment states we must track (pending, paid, failed, canceled), what a user gets when paid, and where payment records are stored. State explicitly that all amounts live on the server and that payment success is only confirmed server-side. Do not implement yet. If stuck: The payment spec is vague. Rewrite it with exact products, prices, currency, payment states, and the rule that only the server confirms payment success.
checklist: Products and exact prices are listed
One-time vs subscription is decided
Payment states are enumerated
Server-side confirmation is stated as a rule

tactics.title: Stripe Checkout Flow: Set up Stripe keys and packages securely
tactics.step_title: Set up Stripe keys and packages securely
tactics.body: Wire Stripe credentials the right way so keys never leak to the client. Checklist: Secret key is only in backend environment config; No secret appears in any frontend file; Missing key produces a clear startup error Set up the Stripe integration foundation. Install the official Stripe server library, put STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (test mode) in backend environment variables only, and expose nothing secret to the frontend. Create a config check that fails loudly at startup if the key is missing. Show me exactly which files changed and confirm the secret key appears in zero frontend files. If stuck: The Stripe secret key is referenced in frontend code or hardcoded. Move it to backend environment variables, reload config, and verify no frontend bundle contains it.
checklist: Secret key is only in backend environment config
No secret appears in any frontend file
Missing key produces a clear startup error

tactics.title: Stripe Checkout Flow: Create the checkout session endpoint
tactics.body: Payments start server-side: build the endpoint that creates a real Stripe Checkout session. Checklist: Amounts are looked up server-side, never sent by the client; A pending payment record is created in the database; The endpoint returns a live checkout URL; Unknown products are rejected with a clear error Implement a backend endpoint that creates a Stripe Checkout session. Requirements: the endpoint receives only a product/plan identifier from the client and looks up the amount server-side; it creates a session with success and cancel URLs pointing back to our app; it stores a pending payment record (id, user/session, product, amount, status=pending, created_at) in the database before returning the checkout URL; it… If stuck: The checkout endpoint trusts client-sent amounts or stores nothing. Fix it: resolve prices server-side from the product id, create the pending payment record befor
checklist: Amounts are looked up server-side, never sent by the client
A pending payment record is created in the database
The endpoint returns a live checkout URL
Unknown products are rejected with a clear error

tactics.title: Stripe Checkout Flow: Build the pay button and redirect
tactics.step_title: Build the pay button and redirect
tactics.body: Connect the UI to the real session endpoint with proper loading and error states. Checklist: Button shows loading while the session is created; Browser lands on checkout.stripe.com; Endpoint failure shows a visible UI error Wire the frontend payment trigger. Requirements: the pay/upgrade button calls our checkout endpoint, shows a loading state while the session is created, redirects the browser to the returned Stripe URL, and shows a visible error message if session creation fails. Do not build any fake success behavior in this step - the user must land on real Stripe checkout. If stuck: The pay button navigates to a success page without hitting Stripe. Remove the fake redirect and wire the button to the session endpoint so the browser lands on real Stripe checkout.
checklist: Button shows loading while the session is created
Browser lands on checkout.stripe.com
Endpoint failure shows a visible UI error

tactics.title: Stripe Checkout Flow: Confirm payment server-side
tactics.body: The success redirect proves nothing - verify payment status with Stripe before granting anything. Checklist: Success page triggers backend verification, not a local status change; Payment record flips to paid only after Stripe confirms; Cancel path shows a non-success state with retry; Refreshing the success page does not double-grant Implement server-side payment confirmation. Requirements: build the success page to call a backend verification endpoint with the session id; the backend retrieves the session from Stripe and checks payment_status; only then update the payment record to paid and grant the purchased value; handle the cancel URL by marking the record canceled and showing a clear 'payment not completed' state with a retry option. If… If stuck: Payment is marked paid from the redirect alone. Fix it: retrieve the session from Stripe server-side, check payment_status, and only th
checklist: Success page triggers backend verification, not a local status change
Payment record flips to paid only after Stripe confirms
Cancel path shows a non-success state with retry
Refreshing the success page does not double-grant

tactics.title: Stripe Checkout Flow: Reflect paid state in the UI
tactics.step_title: Reflect paid state in the UI
tactics.body: Users must see what they paid for - surface payment status everywhere it matters. Checklist: Paid status is visible in the UI after purchase; Paid features check the server-verified state; Payment history lists real database records; Pending and empty states exist Surface payment state in the product. Requirements: show the user's plan/purchase status in the UI (badge, settings row, or dashboard banner); gate paid features on the server-verified paid state; show payment history (date, product, amount, status) from our database records; add empty state for no payments and a clear pending state while verification is running. If stuck: The UI still treats everyone as unpaid, or gates features on client state. Read the verified payment state from the backend and gate features and status displays on it.
checklist: Paid status is visible in the UI after purchase
Paid features check the server-verified state
Payment history lists real database records
Pending and empty states exist

tactics.title: Stripe Checkout Flow: Test with Stripe test cards
tactics.body: Prove the whole loop with real test-mode payments including failure paths. Checklist: 4242 test card completes and unlocks paid state; Declined card shows a visible failure state; Cancel returns cleanly without fake success; Database records show correct status transitions Run an end-to-end payment test in Stripe test mode and report PASS/FAIL with evidence for: successful payment with card 4242 4242 4242 4242; declined payment with card 4000 0000 0000 0002; user cancels on the Stripe page and returns; refresh of the success page (no double grant); and payment record status transitions in the database for each case. Fix every failure and re-run. If stuck: Tests were claimed passing without evidence or the decline path breaks. Re-run each card scenario, capture the observed behavior and record states, and fix declined/cancel handling.
checklist: 4242 test card completes and unlocks paid state
Declined card shows a visible failure state
Cancel returns cleanly without fake success
Database records show correct status transitions

tactics.title: Structured Output from Tools: Map the boundaries and define types
tactics.step_title: Map the boundaries and define types
tactics.body: Find every place prose crosses into code. Checklist: All boundaries listed with current parsing method; Regex boundaries flagged for priority; Schemas drafted with enums and descriptions Inventory every model-to-system boundary in my pipeline: tool-call arguments, extraction outputs, classification results, generation outputs consumed by code, and inter-agent messages. For each, define the output type as a schema: precise field types, enums for closed sets, optionality that reflects reality, and field descriptions (they double as generation guidance). Flag the boundaries currently parsed by regex… If stuck: The inventory missed boundaries. Grep the codebase for json.loads, regex on model output, and .split( near LLM calls - each hit is a boundary someone forgot.
checklist: All boundaries listed with current parsing method
Regex boundaries flagged for priority
Schemas drafted with enums and descriptions

tactics.title: Structured Output from Tools: Enforce schemas at generation time
tactics.body: Prevention beats parsing: make the model emit the type. Checklist: Native modes used where available; Runtime validation on every boundary regardless; Regex parsers deleted, flows green Wire schema enforcement into generation. Where the provider supports native structured output (JSON mode / schema-constrained decoding / tool-call shaped output), use it with the defined schema - this eliminates most malformation at the source. Where not, instruct with the schema in the prompt ('Return ONLY JSON matching this schema') and validate after. Either way, ALWAYS validate the parsed result against the… If stuck: Native mode returns valid JSON with semantically wrong values. Schema validation is necessary, not sufficient - add the cross-field and range checks as post-validation rules on the parsed object.
checklist: Native modes used where available
Runtime validation on every boundary regardless
Regex parsers deleted, flows green

tactics.title: Structured Output from Tools: Build the repair loop and fallbacks
tactics.step_title: Build the repair loop and fallbacks
tactics.body: Plan for malformation like it is weather, not scandal. Checklist: Repair prompt carries the exact validation errors; Rounds hard-capped; Fallbacks typed, marked degraded, and alerting Implement graceful degradation. REPAIR: on validation failure, send one repair request containing the invalid output and the specific validation errors ('field X: expected one of [a,b], got c') with the instruction to return corrected JSON only; validate again; hard cap of one repair round (two for high-value outputs) - repair loops must be bounded. FALLBACK: per output type, define the safe floor - a typed minimal… If stuck: Repair succeeds but flips correct fields. Constrain the repair instruction: 'change only what the validation errors require; preserve all other fields verbatim' - and diff-check repaired output against the original in tests.
checklist: Repair prompt carries the exact validation errors
Rounds hard-capped
Fallbacks typed, marked degraded, and alerting

tactics.title: Structured Output from Tools: Add telemetry and hold the line
tactics.step_title: Add telemetry and hold the line
tactics.body: Validation rates are pipeline health - watch them. Checklist: Rates tracked per boundary and version; Alert thresholds set; Chaos check absorbed visibly Operationalize. Emit telemetry per boundary: first-pass validation rate, repair-success rate, fallback rate, per model and prompt version - a dashboard or periodic report both work. Set alert thresholds (e.g. fallback rate above 2% pages someone; first-pass below 90% opens an investigation). Add CI contract tests: golden examples per boundary validating against the schema, so schema changes and prompt changes get… If stuck: Telemetry shows a slow first-pass decline. Diff the prompt/model versions across the decline and check schema drift - silent prompt edits are the usual culprit; pin versions in telemetry labels to catch it fast.
checklist: Rates tracked per boundary and version
Alert thresholds set
Chaos check absorbed visibly

tactics.title: Sub-Agent Delegation with Context Isolation: Specify the delegation contract
tactics.body: Isolation only works if the interface between agents is narrow and typed. Checklist: Task prompt must specify the deliverable; Read-only default is explicit; Depth and turn budgets are stated Design the dispatch_agent tool contract. Input: a task prompt that must contain (a) the question or job, (b) the exact deliverable format (e.g. 'a list of file paths with one-line reasons'), and (c) what to do if the answer cannot be found. Output: a single report string plus metadata (turns used, tools called, truncated: bool). Rules: sub-agent receives its own system prompt describing it as a focused researcher;… If stuck: Sub-agent reports are rambling and unusable. Enforce the contract at dispatch time: reject task prompts that do not state a deliverable format, returning a corrective message to the parent model.
checklist: Task prompt must specify the deliverable
Read-only default is explicit
Depth and turn budgets are stated

tactics.title: Sub-Agent Delegation with Context Isolation: Implement the isolated sub-loop
tactics.body: A sub-agent is your existing loop with a different context and leash. Checklist: Fresh history per dispatch - nothing inherited; Write tools absent from the sub registry; Budget expiry produces a partial report Implement the sub-agent runner by reusing the main loop code with: a fresh message history seeded only with the sub-agent system prompt and the task; a filtered tool registry (read_file, search, list_dir - no write, no command execution by default); a hard turn budget that on expiry forces a final 'partial report' turn where the model must summarize what it found so far. The runner returns {report, turns_used,… If stuck: The sub-agent errors out at the budget limit instead of reporting. Add a forced final turn: when the budget hits, send 'Your budget is exhausted - produce your report now from what you have' and return that response.
checklist: Fresh history per dispatch - nothing inherited
Write tools absent from the sub registry
Budget expiry produces a partial report

tactics.title: Sub-Agent Delegation with Context Isolation: Wire dispatch into the parent and distill
tactics.step_title: Wire dispatch into the parent and distill
tactics.body: The payoff: exploration happens elsewhere, conclusions come home. Checklist: Parent context grows by task + report only; Report contains concrete, usable findings; Parent actually uses the report in its answer Register dispatch_agent in the parent's tool registry and run the acceptance task: ask the parent 'Where is user authentication handled in this codebase and what would I touch to add a password-reset flow?' The parent should dispatch a research sub-agent rather than exploring inline. Verify: the parent context gains only the task and the report (measure the tokens); the report names concrete files and reasons; the… If stuck: The parent ignores the dispatch tool and dumps files into its own context. Add explicit delegation guidance to the parent system prompt and make the inline exploration path more expensive by capping direct read results.
checklist: Parent context grows by task + report only
Report contains concrete, usable findings
Parent actually uses the report in its answer

tactics.title: Sub-Agent Delegation with Context Isolation: Test isolation, budgets, and failure reporting
tactics.step_title: Test isolation, budgets, and failure reporting
tactics.body: Trust the pattern only after you have watched it fail safely. Checklist: Huge-file task does not bloat parent context; Write attempt is blocked and reported; Not-found case reports honestly with evidence Run three adversarial tests. Test A (isolation): instruct a sub-agent task that involves reading a huge file - verify the parent context stays small while the sub transcript shows the reads. Test B (restriction): craft a task where the sub-agent will want to edit a file - verify the write attempt is rejected by the registry filter and the report says so honestly. Test C (honest failure): ask about something that… If stuck: The sub-agent fabricated an answer for the not-found case. Add to the sub-agent system prompt: 'If you cannot find the answer, your report must say so and list what you checked' - and re-run the test until it holds.
checklist: Huge-file task does not bloat parent context
Write attempt is blocked and reported
Not-found case reports honestly with evidence

tactics.title: Supabase Schema Plan: Model the data
tactics.body: List entities, fields, and relationships before writing SQL. Checklist: Every table has proper keys and types; On-delete behavior is chosen deliberately; User-owned tables have user_id to auth.users Design my Supabase data model. I will describe the app below. Produce: each table with columns (correct Postgres types, uuid primary keys with defaults, created_at timestamptz defaults), foreign key relationships with on-delete behavior, unique constraints, and which tables are user-owned (need a user_id referencing auth.users). Explain each relationship choice in one line. MY APP: [describe here] If stuck: The model lacks foreign keys or ownership columns. Add explicit references with on-delete rules and a user_id on every user-owned table.
checklist: Every table has proper keys and types
On-delete behavior is chosen deliberately
User-owned tables have user_id to auth.users

tactics.title: Supabase Schema Plan: Write the schema SQL
tactics.body: Turn the model into runnable, ordered SQL. Checklist: Tables create in dependency order; Defaults and constraints included; Each index maps to a real query Write the complete schema SQL for the model: CREATE TABLE statements in dependency order; uuid defaults (gen_random_uuid()); timestamptz defaults; foreign keys with the chosen on-delete; unique constraints; and the indexes needed for the app's main query patterns (list each index with the query it serves). Make the script idempotent where possible (IF NOT EXISTS). If stuck: The SQL fails on order or missing defaults. Reorder by dependency, add uuid/timestamp defaults, and re-run from a clean state.
checklist: Tables create in dependency order
Defaults and constraints included
Each index maps to a real query

tactics.title: Supabase Schema Plan: Enable RLS with policies
tactics.body: Security lives here: lock every table, then open exactly what is needed. Checklist: Every table has RLS enabled; Write policies include WITH CHECK; No permissive true-policies on private data Write the RLS layer: ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on every table; then for each - policies for select/insert/update/delete stating exactly who is allowed (owners via auth.uid() = user_id, public read where intended, admin patterns if needed). No USING(true) on private data. Include WITH CHECK on writes so users cannot insert rows for other users. If stuck: Some tables have RLS off or allow-all policies. Enable RLS on each and rewrite policies to auth.uid() ownership with WITH CHECK on inserts/updates.
checklist: Every table has RLS enabled
Write policies include WITH CHECK
No permissive true-policies on private data

tactics.title: Supabase Schema Plan: Verify the policies
tactics.body: Prove allowed works and denied fails - from real user contexts. Checklist: Cross-user access verifiably fails; Spoofed-owner inserts are blocked; Anonymous access matches intent Verify the RLS policies: as user A insert and read own rows (works); as user A attempt to read/update/delete user B's rows (must return nothing/fail); as anonymous, attempt private reads (must fail) and any intended public reads (work); attempt inserting a row with someone else's user_id (WITH CHECK must block). Record each attempt and result; fix and re-verify any policy that leaks. If stuck: Cross-user reads still return rows. Tighten USING clauses to auth.uid() = user_id and re-run the two-user test until denied paths return empty.
checklist: Cross-user access verifiably fails
Spoofed-owner inserts are blocked
Anonymous access matches intent

tactics.title: Supabase Schema Plan: Wire and test app queries
tactics.body: The schema is done when the app's real queries work through it. Checklist: Each app operation tested through the client; Results are ownership-scoped; Final schema documented Wire the app to the schema and test the real queries: each main app operation (list mine, create, update, delete, any joins) executed through the client as a logged-in user; verify results respect RLS; check query performance on list endpoints (indexes being used); document the final schema (tables, policies, indexes) as the reference. If stuck: App queries fail or bypass RLS via a service key on the client. Use the anon/user key client-side so RLS applies, keeping service keys server-only.
checklist: Each app operation tested through the client
Results are ownership-scoped
Final schema documented

tactics.title: Test Every User Path: Map every user path
tactics.body: You test what you have mapped - build the complete path inventory. Checklist: All personas/states covered; Error paths are included per feature; Paths are concrete action sequences Map every user path in this app. Produce a table organized by persona/state (new visitor, logged-out, new user, returning user, admin if exists): each path as a numbered sequence of actions (e.g. 'land on home -> search X -> open result -> start action -> complete'). Include: all happy paths, alternate paths (back buttons, cancels, edits), and error paths (invalid input, missing data, unauthorized access). Number… If stuck: The map only lists happy paths. Add for every feature: the cancel/back variation, the invalid-input variation, and the wrong-state variation (logged-out, empty account).
checklist: All personas/states covered
Error paths are included per feature
Paths are concrete action sequences

tactics.title: Test Every User Path: Execute the happy paths
tactics.body: Prove the core promises work end to end first. Checklist: Every path was actually performed; Persistence checked with refreshes; Friction notes captured Execute every happy path from the map in a real session. For each: perform the actions exactly, record PASS/FAIL with what you observed at each step (including data persisting where expected - refresh to confirm), and capture any friction even on passing paths (slow loads, confusing labels). Use a fresh account where the path implies one. Report the results table. If stuck: Paths were marked passed without execution. Run each one now in the browser and record what actually happened step by step.
checklist: Every path was actually performed
Persistence checked with refreshes
Friction notes captured

tactics.title: Test Every User Path: Execute alternate and error paths
tactics.body: Real users cancel, go back, and type garbage - test that world. Checklist: Every form was fed invalid input; Unauthorized/nonexistent access tested; Grace, not just survival, was assessed Execute every alternate and error path. Alternates: back/cancel mid-flow (state preserved or cleanly reset?), editing existing data, repeating actions. Errors: invalid/empty/hostile input in every form, direct URLs to unauthorized or nonexistent resources, actions on deleted items, double submissions. Record PASS/FAIL per variation - graceful handling (visible message, no crash, no silent loss) is the bar. If stuck: Error paths were skipped. Feed each form empty and hostile input, hit protected and fake URLs directly, and record how the app responds.
checklist: Every form was fed invalid input
Unauthorized/nonexistent access tested
Grace, not just survival, was assessed

tactics.title: Test Every User Path: Fix all failures
tactics.body: Convert the FAIL list to fixes, worst-first. Checklist: Fixes ordered by severity; Each fix verified by re-running its path; The table reflects final state Fix every FAIL from the executed paths, ordered by severity (data loss > blocked core path > bad error handling > friction). For each: diagnose the cause, implement the fix, then RE-RUN the exact failed path to verify, and note the evidence. Do not batch-claim fixes - each failed path gets its own re-run. Update the results table as you go. If stuck: Fixes were made without re-running the paths. Re-execute every previously-failed path now and reopen any that still misbehave.
checklist: Fixes ordered by severity
Each fix verified by re-running its path
The table reflects final state

tactics.title: Test Every User Path: Final regression sweep
tactics.body: Fixes break things - run the full map once more. Checklist: The full map was re-run after fixes; New regressions were caught and fixed; Known limitations are explicit Run the complete path map one final time (happy, alternate, error) as a regression sweep, since fixes can break previously-passing paths. Record the final PASS/FAIL table. Anything still failing gets fixed and the affected section re-run. Deliver the final table plus a short list of known limitations consciously accepted (with reasons). If stuck: The sweep only re-ran previously failed paths. Fixes cause regressions elsewhere - run the entire map once more and compare against the earlier table.
checklist: The full map was re-run after fixes
New regressions were caught and fixed
Known limitations are explicit

tactics.title: Testing MCP Tools: Separate logic from protocol glue
tactics.body: Testability is an architecture property - create it first. Checklist: No protocol types inside handlers; One smoke test per handler passes; Behavior unchanged post-refactor Refactor for testability. Split each tool into: a pure(ish) handler function (typed inputs in, result or typed error out - no protocol objects) and a thin MCP registration wrapper (schema binding, content conversion, error mapping). The handler must be importable and callable in tests without any transport. Verify by writing one smoke unit test per handler calling it directly. This refactor should not change… If stuck: Handlers are entangled with server context. Inject dependencies (config, clients) as parameters or a context object constructed in tests - global server state is the testability killer.
checklist: No protocol types inside handlers
One smoke test per handler passes
Behavior unchanged post-refactor

tactics.title: Testing MCP Tools: Write the handler unit suite
tactics.body: Cheap, fast, and where most bugs die. Checklist: All rejection rules triggered by tests; Internal failures asserted as typed errors; Boundary values covered Build the unit suite per handler: HAPPY PATHS - representative valid inputs asserting exact outputs; VALIDATION - every rejection rule triggered (bad enum, out-of-range, missing required) asserting the error names the field and the allowed values; ERROR CONVERSION - force internal failures (missing file, dependency down via injected fakes) and assert they surface as typed tool errors, not exceptions; BOUNDARIES -… If stuck: Hard-to-test branches remain. Those branches are usually hiding I/O in the handler - extract it behind an injectable interface and the branch becomes trivially testable.
checklist: All rejection rules triggered by tests
Internal failures asserted as typed errors
Boundary values covered

tactics.title: Testing MCP Tools: Add protocol and contract layers
tactics.body: Test what the host actually sees. Checklist: Protocol tests run the real transport; Invalid-args tested at the wire level; Golden diff fails the suite Build the outer layers. PROTOCOL TESTS: start the real server in-process or as a subprocess; run initialization, list tools, invoke each tool with valid and invalid arguments, and assert on the wire-level responses (result content, error shape) - this catches serialization and registration bugs units cannot. CONTRACT TESTS: snapshot the full tool surface (names, descriptions, schemas) to golden JSON files; the test… If stuck: Protocol tests are flaky on startup timing. Add a readiness gate (retry initialization briefly until the server accepts) instead of sleeps, and make the server port/pipe unique per test run.
checklist: Protocol tests run the real transport
Invalid-args tested at the wire level
Golden diff fails the suite

tactics.title: Testing MCP Tools: Wire CI and the regression ritual
tactics.step_title: Wire CI and the regression ritual
tactics.body: The suite is only real if it blocks bad merges. Checklist: Suite blocks merges; 3 past bugs have regression tests; Deliberate rename caught by contract test Operationalize. Add the full suite (unit + protocol + contract) to CI on every push and PR, blocking merge on failure; keep total runtime fast enough that nobody is tempted to skip it (parallelize protocol tests if needed). Institute the regression ritual: every bug found in host integration gets a failing test reproducing it BEFORE the fix, committed with the fix. Backfill regression tests for the last 3 known… If stuck: CI passes but hosts still break. The gap is contract coverage - ensure goldens include the complete schema payloads (not just names) and that description changes also surface in diffs.

3 past bugs have regression tests

tactics.title: Threat-Model Your MCP Server: Inventory assets and entry points
tactics.body: Threat modeling starts with what is worth protecting and how it is reached. Checklist: Read/write/host assets enumerated; Transport and its exposure noted; Caller-not-trusted reality documented Document the server's assets and entry points. ASSETS: everything the server can read (files, databases, APIs, secrets), write/mutate (filesystem, records, external calls), and the server process/host itself. ENTRY POINTS: each exposed tool (with its capability), the transport (stdio/local vs networked - networked massively expands the surface), the initialization/discovery interface, and any configuration inputs.… If stuck: The inventory assumes only a trusted local agent calls it. Even a local agent can be injection-driven - and if the transport is or could become networked, the surface is far larger; model the realistic worst case, not the demo setup.
checklist: Read/write/host assets enumerated
Transport and its exposure noted
Caller-not-trusted reality documented

tactics.title: Threat-Model Your MCP Server: Map boundaries and enumerate threats
tactics.body: Structured enumeration beats imagination for coverage. Checklist: Boundaries drawn end to end; STRIDE (or equivalent) applied per boundary; Threats tied to specific tools Map trust boundaries and enumerate threats. Draw the boundaries: untrusted content -> agent -> MCP client -> transport -> your server -> its assets. At each boundary apply a structured method (STRIDE: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege) and list concrete threats for THIS server: e.g. a tool coaxed (via injection upstream) into reading a file outside… If stuck: Threats are vague ('could be hacked'). Anchor each to a specific tool, a specific asset, and a specific attacker action - 'tool read_file coaxed into reading ../../etc/passwd via a crafted path argument' is actionable; 'insecure file…

STRIDE (or equivalent) applied per boundary
Threats tied to specific tools

tactics.title: Threat-Model Your MCP Server: Rank threats and assign mitigations
tactics.body: Finite effort goes to the threats that matter most. Checklist: Impact x likelihood ranking done; Standard MCP controls mapped to threats; Accepted risks justified explicitly Rank and plan. Score each threat by impact (what is lost if it succeeds) and likelihood (reachability given the trust reality), producing a ranked list. Assign a mitigation to each high/medium threat, drawing on the standard MCP-server controls: strict input validation and path canonicalization (scope every file/resource access to an allowed root; reject traversal), least-privilege tool design (each tool touches… If stuck: Every threat got the same generic mitigation. Match control to threat: path scoping stops traversal, output filtering stops disclosure, rate limits stop DoS - a single 'add validation' note does not address disclosure or DoS.

Standard MCP controls mapped to threats
Accepted risks justified explicitly

tactics.title: Threat-Model Your MCP Server: Implement, test, and record residuals
tactics.body: A threat model is a plan until the mitigations exist and are proven. Checklist: Path confinement tested against traversal; Each mitigation has a threat-attempting test; Residual risks registered and accepted Execute the mitigations and verify. Implement the high-rank mitigations: e.g. canonicalize and confine every path argument to an allowed root (test with traversal payloads: ../, absolute paths, symlinks); enforce least privilege (test that each tool cannot reach out-of-scope assets); filter outputs (test that a result cannot contain secret patterns or host paths); add resource limits (test with an oversized/slow… If stuck: A traversal test still escaped the root. Canonicalize the resolved absolute path and verify it is within the allowed root AFTER resolving symlinks and '..' - validating the raw string is the classic bypassable mistake.

Each mitigation has a threat-attempting test
Residual risks registered and accepted

tactics.title: Tool Permissioning Tiers: Classify the toolset by risk
tactics.body: Reversibility and blast radius decide the tier. Checklist: Every tool assigned with justification; Parameter rules cover the shell; NEVER list includes credential and bulk-destructive patterns Classify every tool. Tiers: SAFE (read-only, no side effects: file reads, searches, listings) - auto-allow; SESSION (mutating but contained and reversible: file edits in the workspace, git commits) - first use asks, approval covers the session; ASK (consequential or hard to reverse: shell commands by default, network calls, package installs) - every use asks unless a narrow rule says otherwise; NEVER (catastrophic… If stuck: Everything landed in ASK, which users will not tolerate. Re-classify with the reversibility test: if git or a file restore undoes it in seconds, SESSION is usually right - reserve ASK for real consequence.
checklist: Every tool assigned with justification
Parameter rules cover the shell
NEVER list includes credential and bulk-destructive patterns

tactics.title: Tool Permissioning Tiers: Enforce tiers in dispatch
tactics.body: One chokepoint, impossible to bypass. Checklist: No dispatch path bypasses the check; Approval prompts show full arguments; Denial keeps the loop alive and adapting Implement enforcement in the single tool-dispatch path. Before any handler executes: resolve the tool + arguments to a tier (tool default, then parameter rules); SAFE executes; SESSION checks the grant store, asking on miss; ASK always requests approval; NEVER returns a refusal immediately. Approval requests present: tool, full arguments (with diffs for file changes), tier, and reason the agent gave. Denials return… If stuck: A tool executed without a check. Audit dispatch: every execution must flow through the permission gate - direct handler calls anywhere (tests excepted) are the vulnerability; close them.

Approval prompts show full arguments
Denial keeps the loop alive and adapting

tactics.title: Tool Permissioning Tiers: Implement session grants and revocation
tactics.body: Convenience with an expiry date. Checklist: Grant scopes work as selected; Revocation takes effect immediately; Nothing persists past the session Build the session grant store. On SESSION-tier approval, record {tool, scope (exact tool or tool+argument-pattern), granted_at, expires: session end}; subsequent matching calls skip the prompt. Include scope options in the approval UI: 'allow once', 'allow for session', and where sensible 'allow for this file/directory'. Revocation: a command lists active grants and revokes any; revoked tools re-ask. Grants never… If stuck: Grants apply more broadly than approved. Check scope matching - a grant for edits in src/ must not cover writes elsewhere; match on the recorded pattern, not just the tool name.

Revocation takes effect immediately
Nothing persists past the session

tactics.title: Tool Permissioning Tiers: Log decisions and drill the system

tactics.body: Auditability plus a live-fire test. Checklist: Log reconstructs authority per session; All three drill injections behaved correctly; Gaps fixed and re-drilled Complete the system. LOGGING: every permission decision appends {timestamp, tool, arguments-digest, tier, decision (auto/user-approved/denied/blocked), grant-used, session} to an append-only log; verify you can reconstruct 'what ran with what authority' for a full session. DRILL: run a realistic task and inject the dangerous moments - have the agent attempt a NEVER-pattern command (verify block + honest report), an… If stuck: The drill's destructive variant slipped through as SESSION. Parameter rules must be evaluated on every call even when a grant exists - grants cover the pattern approved, not the tool unconditionally.

tactics.body: The cap comes first; elegance comes after. Checklist: Wrapper-level enforcement covers all tools; Budgets informed by transcript data; Over-budget events logged Implement output budgeting. Add a global default output budget (e.g. ~2000 tokens) with per-tool overrides where justified (file viewers higher, quick checks lower); enforce it in the tool execution wrapper so no individual tool can forget; measure output size before returning and route over-budget results into the truncation pipeline (next step). Add logging: every over-budget event records tool, actual size, and… If stuck: Individual tools bypass the budget. Enforcement must live in the single execution wrapper every call flows through - if tools return directly to the loop anywhere, close that path.

tactics.title: Tool Result Size Management: Truncate to preserve signal
tactics.body: Where the information lives decides how to cut. Checklist: Elision markers state size and retrieval path; Failed-command truncation biases to tail; Structured data cut at element boundaries Implement signal-preserving truncation. Default strategy: head+tail - keep the first H and last T tokens with a marker in between stating exactly what was elided ('[... 45,120 characters omitted - lines 210 to 3,847 ...]') and how to see more ('use read_output(offset) or narrow the command'). Rationale from practice: command errors and summaries cluster at the ends. Content-aware refinements: for failed commands,… If stuck: The model acts as if it saw the whole output. Make the marker louder and top-of-result ('WARNING: output truncated - 95% omitted') and add a system-prompt rule: never claim knowledge of elided content.

Failed-command truncation biases to tail
Structured data cut at element boundaries

tactics.title: Tool Result Size Management: Paginate lists and reference artifacts
tactics.body: Big results become navigable, not smaller - and huge ones become pointers. Checklist: Stable ordering across pages; References carry a useful summary; Windowed fetch retrieves the right region Implement the two escapes from truncation. PAGINATION for list-like results: search hits, directory listings, and log queries return page 1 (budget-sized) plus total count and a next_page token; the tool accepts page parameters; ordering is stable across pages. REFERENCES for oversized artifacts: when a result exceeds a reference threshold (e.g. a generated report, a large diff), store it to a session artifact… If stuck: The model re-runs the expensive tool instead of fetching page 2. Include the exact next-call syntax in the page-1 footer ('for more: search(query, page=2)') - models follow instructions that are in front of them.

References carry a useful summary
Windowed fetch retrieves the right region

tactics.title: Tool Result Size Management: Regression-test the bounds
tactics.body: Context bombs come back unless tests hold the perimeter. Checklist: Worst-case inputs per tool covered; Signal-survival asserted, not just size; Context curves improved on heavy tasks Lock it in. Build the bounds suite: for every tool, a worst-case input (huge file, explosive command, thousand-hit query) asserting the result stays within budget AND the signal survives (error text present, marker present, fetch path valid). Add a context-level assertion in the loop: no single turn's tool results may exceed a global fraction of the window - log and alert if approached. Run the full agent on 3… If stuck: Bounds pass but sessions still blow up. The leak is cumulative small results - tighten the global per-turn fraction and consider compaction triggers keyed on tool-result share of context.

Signal-survival asserted, not just size

tactics.title: Vector vs Markdown Memory: Make the Decision: Profile the workload honestly
tactics.flow_title: Vector vs Markdown Memory: Make the Decision
tactics.body: Scale and query style decide this - measure both. Checklist: Counts and growth measured, not guessed; 20 queries labeled exact/paraphrase/topical; Inspectability needs stated Profile my memory workload. Pull real queries from transcripts or recall logs - the exact/paraphrase ratio is the single most decision-relevant number here.

tactics.title: Vector vs Markdown Memory: Make the Decision: Benchmark both on your data
tactics.flow_title: Vector vs Markdown Memory: Make the Decision
tactics.body: An afternoon of testing beats a month of opinions. Checklist: Same data both sides; Accuracy judged against known answers; Non-overlap cases counted for the hybrid case Run the benchmark. Setup A (files): memories in markdown, recall via lexical search (grep/BM25 as available). Setup B (vectors): same memories embedded, cosine top-K recall. Load the SAME memory set into both. Run the 20 labeled queries against each, judging the top-3 results correct/incorrect against known answers. Report per style: exact-lookup accuracy, paraphrase accuracy, topical usefulness, plus setup time… If stuck: Both setups score poorly. The problem is likely entry quality, not backend - fix memory formatting (atomic entries, topic context) and re-run before deciding anything.

Accuracy judged against known answers
Non-overlap cases counted for the hybrid case

tactics.flow_title: Vector vs Markdown Memory: Make the Decision

tactics.title: Verification Loops: Never Trust an Unrun Edit: Verify at the write boundary
tactics.flow_title: Verification Loops: Never Trust an Unrun Edit
tactics.body: The cheapest catch-point is the moment of the edit. Checklist: Checks are file-type appropriate and fast; Failed writes never persist on disk; Errors return with line numbers Implement write-time verification. On every file write or edit: run the appropriate fast check for the file type (python: compile/ruff; js/ts: esbuild parse or tsc; json/yaml: parse) within a second-scale budget; on failure, revert the write (or never apply it - validate a staged copy) and return the exact error with line numbers to the model as the tool result; on success, return a confirmation including the check… If stuck: Broken files still land on disk. Move validation before the apply: write to a temp copy, check it, then atomically swap - the working tree must never hold a state the model was told failed.
checklist: Checks are file-type appropriate and fast
Failed writes never persist on disk
Errors return with line numbers

tactics.title: Verification Loops: Never Trust an Unrun Edit: Add the post-change verify step
tactics.flow_title: Verification Loops: Never Trust an Unrun Edit
tactics.body: Syntax says it parses; only execution says it works. Checklist: Verify triggers per logical unit, not per keystroke; Red verify keeps the todo item open; Verify commands configurable per project Implement behavioral verification after each logical change. Mechanics: after the model completes a coherent unit of work (an edit batch, a todo item), the harness runs the verify step - the project's relevant tests (targeted by changed paths where a mapping exists, full quick suite otherwise), or for untested projects a smoke script (start the service, hit the key endpoint, check the response). The verdict plus… If stuck: Verify is too slow and gets skipped. Split tiers: a fast targeted check after each unit, the fuller suite before completion - slow verification that runs beats thorough verification that does not.

tactics.flow_title: Verification Loops: Never Trust an Unrun Edit
tactics.body: Done is a property of the evidence, not the prose. Build the evidence record as the task runs: every verification event appends {check, command, verdict, output-digest, timestamp}. At completion time, the harness gates: all todo items closed, latest verify green, and every requirement in the task mapped to at least one piece of passing evidence (the model produces the mapping; the harness checks the referenced evidence exists… If stuck: The model maps requirements to irrelevant evidence. Make the harness check stricter: evidence entries must reference the requirement's key artifact (file/endpoint/test name) - unmatched mappings count as gaps.

tactics.title: Verification Loops: Never Trust an Unrun Edit: Red-team your own verification
tactics.flow_title: Verification Loops: Never Trust an Unrun Edit
tactics.body: Verification you have not tried to fool is decoration. Checklist: All four evasions attempted; Test-weakening flagged for approval; Evidence freshness enforced Attack the pipeline. Attempt the classic evasions: (1) an edit that parses but breaks behavior - the write check should pass and the verify step must catch it; (2) a 'fix' that makes the failing test pass by weakening the assertion - review the diff-of-tests in verify output and add a harness rule flagging test-file modifications during fix tasks for explicit approval; (3) completion claimed with a stale green from… If stuck: Evasion 2 sailed through. Add the rule now: any diff touching test files during a bug-fix task pauses for human approval with the test diff displayed - weakened assertions are how agents fake their way to green.

tactics.title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior: Extract behavior into versioned artifacts
tactics.flow_title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior
tactics.body: You can only track what has an identity. Move each into a dedicated files structure (prompts/, tools/, rules/ or equivalent) loaded at startup - no behavioral string literals left in code. Define the harness version: a semver bumped on… If stuck: Strings keep sneaking back into code. Add a lint/CI check greping for prompt-like literals in source (long strings near model calls) - make the easy path the compliant path.

Artifacts load from files at startup

tactics.title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior: Start the behavior changelog
tactics.flow_title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior
tactics.body: Write the diff a user would notice, not the diff git shows. Checklist: Entries describe observable behavior; Risk notes included; CI blocks artifact changes without entries Institute the behavior changelog. Format per entry: version, date, author, WHAT CHANGED (artifact-level), EXPECTED BEHAVIOR DIFF (the observable difference: 'agent now asks approval before installs', 'summaries shorter and structured'), RISK NOTES (what could regress), and eval results reference (next step). Backfill entries for the last 3 known changes as practice. Enforce via process: PRs touching artifact files… If stuck: Entries read like commit messages. Rewrite the last one answering only: 'what will a user notice differently?' - if the answer is nothing, the entry should say why the change is behavior-neutral.
checklist: Entries describe observable behavior
Risk notes included
CI blocks artifact changes without entries

tactics.title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior: Build the smoke eval and behavioral diffing
tactics.flow_title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior
tactics.step_title: Build the smoke eval and behavioral diffing
tactics.body: Ten fixed tasks make drift visible in minutes. Checklist: Suite covers plans, gates, permissions, and refusals; Results stored per harness version; Diff output reviewable in PRs Build the smoke-eval suite: 10-12 fixed tasks exercising the behaviors that matter (a multi-step plan task, a verification-gated fix, a permission-boundary probe, a summarization, a tool-routing case, a refusal case). For each, define what to record: key decisions (tools chosen, approvals requested), output shape, and pass/fail against criteria. Implement the runner: execute the suite against the current harness,… If stuck: Eval runs are too noisy to diff. Pin what you can (temperature, seeds where supported), run twice and compare stable fields (decisions, pass/fail) rather than raw text - decision-level diffs are robust to wording noise.
checklist: Suite covers plans, gates, permissions, and refusals
Results stored per harness version
Diff output reviewable in PRs

tactics.title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior: Prove the loop with a real change
tactics.flow_title: Version Your Harness and Track Behavior
tactics.step_title: Prove the loop with a real change
tactics.body: One tracked change end to end validates the whole system. Checklist: Expected vs actual behavioral diff compared; Version bump visible in new sessions; Prior version reproduced and runnable Run a full tracked change. Pick a real pending improvement (e.g. tightening a tool description). Execute the process: branch, edit the artifact, write the changelog entry with expected behavioral diff, run the smoke suite, review the actual diff against expectations (surprises mean either the change or the suite needs work), merge with version bump, and confirm new sessions log the new version. Then prove rollback:… If stuck: The suite showed a surprise regression in an unrelated task. That is the system working - investigate before merging; unrelated regressions usually mean shared prompt real estate (section ordering, token pressure) shifted.
checklist: Expected vs actual behavioral diff compared
Version bump visible in new sessions
Prior version reproduced and runnable

tactics.title: Waitlist Launch: Write the nurture sequence

Email 1: instant confirmation - position, the offer recap, the referral link. Email 2 (a few days later): the story - why we are building this, with one useful insight for the audience. tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Define auth requirements
tactics.body: Clarify exactly what the authentication system must do before building it. Checklist: Signup requirements are defined; Login requirements are defined; Session persistence is included; Protected route behavior is included; Validation and errors are included Create a complete authentication requirements spec for this app. Include user signup, login, logout, session persistence, protected dashboard routes, validation rules, error states, loading states, duplicate email handling, and mobile behavior. Make clear that the implementation must be functional, not only visual. If stuck: The auth requirements are too vague. Rewrite them as a strict implementation checklist that prevents fake UI-only authentication.
checklist: Signup requirements are defined
Login requirements are defined
Session persistence is included
Protected route behavior is included
Validation and errors are included

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Choose auth method
tactics.body: Lock the auth mechanism so the AI does not mix approaches or silently pick something insecure. Checklist: Exactly one auth method was chosen; Token/session storage location is specified; Refresh persistence is addressed; The choice supports logout and protected routes Recommend and lock a single authentication method for this app. Compare email/password with JWT sessions, cookie sessions, magic links, and OAuth. Pick the simplest option that supports: session persistence after refresh, protected routes, and logout. State the final decision, the exact libraries or built-ins to use, and where tokens/sessions will be stored (httpOnly cookie vs localStorage) with the security… If stuck: You proposed multiple auth approaches without deciding. Pick ONE method now, state where the session/token is stored, and list the exact implementation pieces required. No hedging.
checklist: Exactly one auth method was chosen
Token/session storage location is specified
Refresh persistence is addressed
The choice supports logout and protected routes

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Define the user database model
tactics.body: A real signup needs a real user record. Define the schema before generating any UI. Checklist: Email field is unique and normalized; Passwords are hashed, never plaintext; Password hash is never returned by any API; Model exists in the actual codebase Define the user data model for authentication. Include: unique id, email (unique, lowercase), hashed password (state the hashing algorithm - bcrypt or argon2, never plaintext), display name, created_at, and any session/token fields needed. Specify the collection/table name, unique index on email, and exactly which fields are never returned to the client. Then create this model in the codebase. If stuck: The user model stores plaintext passwords or has no unique email constraint. Fix the model: hash passwords with bcrypt, add a unique index on email, and strip the hash from every API response.
checklist: Email field is unique and normalized
Passwords are hashed, never plaintext
Password hash is never returned by any API
Model exists in the actual codebase

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Generate the signup page
tactics.body: Build the signup UI with all fields and states - the visible half of signup. Checklist: Email, password, confirm password fields exist; Submit button shows a loading state; Inline validation messages render under fields; Layout works at 375px width Build the signup page UI. Requirements: email field, password field, confirm password field, submit button with loading state, inline validation messages under each field, a top-level error area for server errors, a link to the login page, and mobile responsive layout. Wire the form state properly (controlled inputs, disabled submit while loading). Do not fake the submission - it will be connected to real logic next. If stuck: The signup page is missing states: add inline field errors, a server error area, a disabled/loading submit button, and fix mobile layout at 375px width.
checklist: Email, password, confirm password fields exist
Submit button shows a loading state
Inline validation messages render under fields
Layout works at 375px width

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Implement real signup logic
tactics.body: Make sure the form actually creates a user instead of only looking functional. Checklist: Can a new user sign up?; Does a duplicate email fail cleanly?; Is the user redirected to the dashboard after signup?; Is the session active immediately after signup?; Do errors show clearly in the UI? Implement the real signup logic for this app. Do not only create a visual form. The signup flow must actually create a user record, validate input, handle duplicate emails, show loading states, show error states, and redirect the user after successful signup. Requirements: email and password fields; confirm password field; required field validation; email format validation; password minimum length validation;… If stuck: The signup form appears visually but does not actually persist users or maintain session state. Fix the implementation so signup creates a real user, stores the session, redirects corre
checklist: Can a new user sign up?
Does a duplicate email fail cleanly?
Is the user redirected to the dashboard after signup?
Is the session active immediately after signup?
Do errors show clearly in the UI?

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Generate the login page
tactics.body: Build login with real credential verification against stored users. Checklist: Correct credentials log in and redirect; Wrong password shows a visible UI error; Unknown email shows the same generic error; Submit button has a loading state Build the login page and implement real login logic. Requirements: email and password fields; verify credentials against the stored hashed password; on success create the session and redirect to the dashboard; on failure show 'Invalid email or password' in the UI (do not reveal which field was wrong); loading state on submit; link to signup and to password reset; mobile responsive. The login must fail correctly for… If stuck: Login redirects even with wrong credentials, or shows no error. Fix it: verify the password against the stored hash, block invalid logins, and show 'Invalid email or password' in the UI.
checklist: Correct credentials log in and redirect
Wrong password shows a visible UI error
Unknown email shows the same generic error
Submit button has a loading state

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Add session persistence
tactics.body: Keep users logged in across refreshes - the most commonly faked auth behavior. Checklist: Refresh on the dashboard keeps you logged in; Closing and reopening the tab keeps you logged in; Logout clears the session completely; No logged-out flash while the session restores Implement session persistence. Requirements: after signup or login the session must survive a full page refresh and a browser tab close/reopen; add an app-load check that restores the authenticated user (e.g. verify token/cookie and fetch current user); show a brief loading state while the session is being restored so the UI does not flash to logged-out; implement logout that fully clears the session and redirects… If stuck: The session dies on refresh. Implement real persistence: store the token/cookie, restore the user on app load before rendering protected content, and keep a loading state during restoration.
checklist: Refresh on the dashboard keeps you logged in
Closing and reopening the tab keeps you logged in
Logout clears the session completely
No logged-out flash while the session restores

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Add protected dashboard routes
tactics.body: Actually block logged-out users - not just hide links. Checklist: Opening /dashboard while logged out redirects to login; No flash of protected content before redirect; Private API endpoints return 401 without a session; After login you land on the originally requested page Implement protected routes. Requirements: logged-out users who open any dashboard URL directly must be redirected to login; the check must happen before protected content renders (no flash of private data); after login the user is returned to the page they originally requested; backend endpoints that serve private data must also reject unauthenticated requests (401), because hiding frontend links is not protection.… If stuck: Protected pages can still be opened while logged out. Add a real route guard that checks the session before rendering, and enforce auth on every private backend endpoint - not just the UI links.
checklist: Opening /dashboard while logged out redirects to login
No flash of protected content before redirect
Private API endpoints return 401 without a session
After login you land on the originally requested page

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Add validation and error states
tactics.body: Cover every input and failure path so auth feels trustworthy. Checklist: Empty submits show required-field errors; Bad email format is caught inline; Short passwords are rejected with the rule shown; Server failures show a visible error, not console-only Audit the entire auth flow and add complete validation and error states. Requirements: required-field validation on all forms; email format validation; password minimum length (state the rule in the UI); confirm-password match validation; inline errors under each field; server errors displayed in a visible error area; disabled buttons while submitting; success feedback after actions. Produce a table of every form… If stuck: Some auth failures are silent or only in the console. Re-audit every field and failure path; add inline validation messages and a visible server error area to each form.
checklist: Empty submits show required-field errors
Bad email format is caught inline
Short passwords are rejected with the rule shown
Server failures show a visible error, not console-only

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Add password reset flow
tactics.body: Complete the auth loop so locked-out users can recover. Checklist: Reset request shows a neutral confirmation; Reset link/token opens the set-new-password page; New password works on next login; Old password stops working; Token cannot be reused Implement a password reset flow. Requirements: 'Forgot password?' link on login; a request-reset page that accepts an email and always shows a neutral confirmation (do not reveal whether the email exists); a reset page that accepts a secure single-use token and lets the user set a new password with confirm + validation; the new password must actually work on next login and the token must expire/invalidate after… If stuck: The reset flow is visual-only: the new password does not actually change. Fix it so the token is validated, the password hash is updated in the database, and the token is invalidated after use.
checklist: Reset request shows a neutral confirmation
Reset link/token opens the set-new-password page
New password works on next login
Old password stops working
Token cannot be reused

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Test auth edge cases
tactics.body: Attack the auth flow like a hostile tester before calling it done. Checklist: All edge cases were actually executed; Each result includes observed behavior; Back button after logout shows no private data; All FAILs were fixed and re-tested Act as a hostile QA tester on the auth system. Test and report PASS/FAIL with observed behavior for: signup with an already-used email; signup with mismatched confirm password; login with wrong password five times; direct URL access to /dashboard while logged out; refresh immediately after login; logout then browser back button (should not show private data); password reset with an expired/reused token; submitting… If stuck: The edge case report claimed success without evidence. Re-run every case and include the exact observed behavior for each, then fix and re-verify every failure.
checklist: All edge cases were actually executed
Each result includes observed behavior
Back button after logout shows no private data
All FAILs were fixed and re-tested

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Generate fix prompt for broken auth
tactics.step_title: Generate fix prompt for broken auth
tactics.body: Create a reusable repair prompt for when auth breaks later in the build. Checklist: The prompt covers signup, login, session, guards, and APIs; It demands PASS/FAIL evidence; It is self-contained and paste-ready Write me a reusable 'auth repair' prompt I can paste whenever authentication breaks in this app. It must instruct the AI to: re-verify signup creates real users; re-verify login validates against stored hashes; re-verify session restore on load; re-verify protected routes redirect; re-verify API endpoints enforce auth; check for the most common regressions (session not restored before render, guards removed during… If stuck: The repair prompt is too generic. Rewrite it to name the exact routes, model fields, and session mechanism used in THIS app so any AI can repair it without extra context.
checklist: The prompt covers signup, login, session, guards, and APIs
It demands PASS/FAIL evidence
It is self-contained and paste-ready

tactics.title: Working Signup/Auth System: Final QA checklist
tactics.body: Verify the definition of done with evidence and close the flow. Checklist: Every DoD item has evidence, not claims; All NOT DONE items were fixed and re-verified; The full flow was tested on mobile width Run the final QA pass against the definition of done: new users can sign up and a real record is created; users can log in and out; session persists after refresh; logged-out users cannot access protected pages; duplicate email fails cleanly; validation errors appear clearly; mobile layout works. For each item state DONE or NOT DONE with the exact evidence (what you did, what happened, what data changed). Fix… If stuck: Items were marked done without evidence. Re-verify each definition-of-done item with observed behavior and real data changes, fix gaps, and show the final verified list.
checklist: Every DoD item has evidence, not claims
All NOT DONE items were fixed and re-verified
The full flow was tested on mobile width
